Greave takes his cap off as he sits, wiping his sleeve across his forehead. He looks ragged now, his hair and beard unkempt, his armour battered, and his uniform stained and frayed. 

He is a far cry from the straight-laced man you met weeks ago, but his eyes sparkle with confidence, and he carries himself more easily.

He takes a small object on a chain out of his pocket and sets it in the fire, then turns toward you and smiles.

|"You know, it doesn't take much to see how I'm the odd man out in this operation. I may well have held the key to many of these peoples' cells myself. 

It's with no small amount of humility that I admit I regret that. 

When I first talked myself into coming to Lukatt, it was because I believed what I was told, that this place is a fortress where the most dangerous of criminals are locked up, to keep the rest of our nation safe. 

|Maybe once, that was even true, but that isn't the Lukatt I found when I got here. 

At first, I thought it was just because I was new, that I didn't yet understand, but more and more, I began to see the stocks as what they really are - a miscreants' playground masquerading as a pillar of justice. 

The guards, most of them are every bit as criminal as the people in the cells. Men who abused their power, and who were 'reassigned' to the imposing but important station here, not out of any sense of duty, but so that their superiors could quietly cover scandals and sweep their complicity under the rug. 

It's just a place to toss inconvenient people and hope that they disappear.

|I came here because I believed there was an important job to be done. My superiors on the mainland tried to dissuade me, but none of them told me anything resembling the truth. 

I think eventually, they decided that someone as wholeheartedly 'do-gooder' as me would be better off shipped out anyway. 

Having joined up with you, I'm more convinced than ever that I was right. 

There is a very important job to do here, and it is nothing less than the complete dismantling of the lie we are all told. 

|I think that if we keep going, we can take this island, corner-to-corner. The mainland powers will not dare land soldiers here because they know they will never get them back. 

If we conquer this island, people will notice. 

The mainland will notice, and the lie will shatter, and if nothing else, conquering this island will stop them sending more convicts. Once that happens, all sorts of remarkable things are possible.

Rebuilding. Commerce. Families. 

That possibility alone is reason enough to turn my sword back on the dogs who shepherd this place."

|Greave reaches down with a carefully gloved hand and pulls the metal object out of the fire. Holding your gaze intently, he draws his collar back and presses the trinket against his neck.

He winces and draws a sharp breath, but does not waver, and when he pulls his hand away a moment later, you see it. 

It is crudely shaped, but clear. Greave has branded the glyph for "traitor" into his own flesh.

When he speaks again, his voice quavers, but his smile is confident. 

"Here until the end.
column2:
我可以坐下吗？”

Greave 坐下时摘下帽子，用袖子擦过额头。他现在看上去憔悴不堪，头发和胡子都不修边幅，护甲坑坑洼洼，制服又污又破。

他和几周前你遇见的那个一本正经的人判若两人，可他眼里闪着自信，举止也自在了许多。

他从口袋里掏出一件拴在链子上的小物件，放进火里，然后转向你，微笑。

|“你知道，不难看出我在这桩事里有多格格不入。这里许多人的牢房钥匙，很可能就是我亲手拿过的。

我得相当谦卑地承认，我后悔了。

我当初说服自己来到卢卡特，是因为我相信别人告诉我的：这地方是一座要塞，最危险的罪犯被锁在里面，好让我们国家的其余地方平安。

|也许从前的确如此，可那不是我到了这里看见的卢卡特。

起初我以为只是因为自己是新人，还没弄懂，可我越来越看清枷场的真面目——一个伪装成正义支柱的恶棍游乐场。

那些卫兵，大多和牢房里的人一样是十足的罪犯。他们滥用过权力，于是被“重新指派”到这里，这个威严却要紧的岗位上，不是出于任何职责，而是好让上司悄悄捂住丑闻，把他们自己也脱不了干系的事掩盖过去。

这里不过是个扔掉碍事的人、再指望他们消失的地方。

|我来这里，是因为我相信有一件重要的工作要做。大陆上的上司试图劝阻我，可他们谁也没告诉我半点像样的真相。

我想他们到最后认定，像我这样全心“做好人”的家伙，反正送走了更省心。

加入你的团伙之后，我比以往任何时候都更确信自己是对的。

这里有一件非常重要的工作要做，那正是把我们所有人被告知的那个谎言彻底拆穿。

|我想只要我们继续下去，就能拿下这座岛的每一个角落。大陆上的势力不敢派兵在此登陆，因为他们知道这些士兵再也回不去。

如果我们征服这座岛，人们会注意到。

大陆会注意到，谎言会碎裂，至少，征服这座岛会拦住他们，不再送来更多罪犯。一旦如此，种种了不起的事就都有了可能。

重建。贸易。家庭。

单是这种可能，就足够让我掉转剑锋，指向看管这地方的那些狗。”

|Greave 伸出一只仔细戴好手套的手，从火里抽出那件金属物件。他目不转睛地看着你，拉开衣领，把那小饰物按在自己的脖子上。

他皱起眉，猛地吸了口气，却没有动摇。片刻后他把手拿开，你看见了。

形状粗糙，却清清楚楚。Greave 把“叛徒”的符文烙进了自己的皮肉。

他再次开口时，声音发颤，笑容却很自信。

“留到最后。

column1: I can't believe I used to see things in such simple black and white. I was not tried, but truly, I am no less a criminal than those who were. I'm not sorry, either. I did what was right. I wonder how many others have like reasons for wearing their scars?
column2: 真不敢相信我从前把事情看得这么非黑即白。我没有受审，可说真的，我和那些受过审的人一样是罪犯。我也不后悔。我做了该做的事。不知道还有多少人，身上的伤疤也是出于同样的理由？

column1: You can't be serious. After all of this? After I... you'd just throw me out?
column2: 你不是认真的吧。经历了这一切之后？在我……之后，你就要把我扔掉？

column1: Hello, friend. I hope everything is well.
column2: 你好，朋友。希望一切都好。

column1: Are you testing my commitment? There are kinder ways to do so, you realize.
column2: 你是在考验我的决心吗？你该知道，有更温和的办法。

column1: This comes as a shock, I have to say. Just... give me a bit to collect myself and I'll go.
column2: 这真让我震惊，我得说。就……给我一点时间定定神，我就走。

column1: This salty air is terrible for the iron. Maybe I can find someplace inland that needs a smith.
column2: 这咸湿的空气对铁太糟了。也许我能在内陆找个需要铁匠的地方。

column1: I haven't had a good hard hammering in a while. You need something worked over?
column2: 我有阵子没好好狠锤过了。你有什么要让我敲打敲打的？

column1: Right, back to unskilled labour.
column2: 行，回去干粗活。

column1: There are more wandering merchants and tradesmen on this island than you might think. If you set up an attractive place to do business, you'll probably attract some. I might even come out and see it myself!
column2: 这座岛上游荡的商人和手艺人比你想的多。你要是搭个招人的地方做生意，大概能招来一些。我说不定自己也会去看看！

column1: New faces! Hopefully you remembered to bring some money with you, eh?
column2: 新面孔！希望你记得带钱来了，嗯？

column1: Right, well come back if you realize you forgot something. I'll be here.
column2: 行，要是发现忘了什么，就回来。我在这儿。

column1: Oh how exciting!
column2: 哦，多刺激！

column1: A pack of villains!
column2: 一群恶棍！

column1: Oh, a dingledoo or somesuch.
column2: 哦，一个叮铃宝什么的。

column1: What's this thingamajig for,\ndo you think?
column2: 这玩意儿是用来干什么的，\n你觉得呢？

column1: Oh, that poor sod...
column2: 哦，那个可怜虫……

column1: That tears it!\nI'll make crepes out of you!
column2: 这下忍无可忍了！\n我要把你做成可丽饼！

column1: What a strange smell.
column2: 好怪的味道。

column1: Ugh, I need to sneeze,\nbut it won't come out.
column2: 呃，我想打喷嚏，\n可就是打不出来。

column1: This one... doesn't have a\nhappy ending, does it?
column2: 这一场……不会有\n好结局，对吧？

column1: No dessert tonight lads. Sorry.
column2: 今晚没甜点了，伙计们。抱歉。

column1: But if we don't win, there'll be no dessert!\nEntirely unacceptable!
column2: 可我们要是不赢，就没有甜点了！\n完全不能接受！

column1: What a silly thing to say.\nI've got more tricks up my sleeve yet!
column2: 这话真傻。\n我袖子里还有不少花样呢！

column1: I'll have your share of dinner then!
column2: 那你那份晚饭归我了！

column1: If you're going to be such a glum-bum about it,\nwe'll do it without you!
column2: 你要是非要当这么个丧气包，\n我们就不带你干了！

column1: Oh. Well, that's a shame.
column2: 哦。嗯，真可惜。

column1: Any of us could be next!
column2: 我们谁都可能是下一个！

column1: Really, you ruin one lousy nobleman's wedding, and you get locked up for conspiracy and shipped out to this horrid place. What is the world coming to?
column2: 真是的，不过是毁了某个讨厌贵族的一场婚礼，就因为密谋被关起来，送到这可怕的地方。这世道到底怎么了？

column1: Gracious, that's sudden.  You're saying you want to be rid of me?
column2: 我的天，这么突然。你是说你想甩掉我？

column1: A good day to you, such as it is.
column2: 祝你日安，就眼下这样。

column1: Oh, forgive me for misunderstanding then. Would you like a biscuit? I'm going to have a biscuit.
column2: 哦，那就请原谅我误会了。你想来块饼干吗？我要吃块饼干。

column1: Well I certainly don't want to be on your bad side, so I'll get my things and go. I'm sorry you didn't find me helpful. Goodbye.
column2: 嗯，我当然不想惹你不痛快，所以我收拾东西走。抱歉我没能帮上你。再见。

column1: Stop it, stop it! I give up!
column2: 停下，停下！我投降！

column1: You're only trying to disarm me for a slaughter!  I'll have none of it!
column2: 你不过是想缴了我的械，好动手屠杀！我才不吃这一套！

column1: Oh goodness, fine just take it and leave me be!
column2: 哦，天哪，好吧，拿去就是，别再烦我！

column1: Isn't being prisoner here bad enough already? No, I won't be a slave!
column2: 在这儿当囚犯还不够惨吗？不，我才不当奴隶！

column1: And... then you'll stop hitting me, right? Fine, I'll go with you!
column2: 而且……然后你就不会再打我了，对吧？好吧，我跟你走！

column1: Oh thank goodness! I'll be right off!
column2: 哦，谢天谢地！我马上就走！

column1: Oh, smashing, my mouth is already watering! Lead the way!
column2: 哦，妙极了，我已经在流口水了！带路吧！

column1: I came here hoping to find an easy meal and ended up with nothing but a sprained ankle. Ugh, it's quite a pickle I'm in. Goodness, I could go for a pickle about now, and I don't even like pickles.
column2: 我来这儿本想找顿容易的饭，结果只落了个扭伤的脚踝。唉，我这处境可真是泡进咸菜缸了。天哪，我现在还真想来口咸菜，可我根本不喜欢咸菜。

column1: I don't know what I'd have done if you hadn't come along. Thanks again.
column2: 要不是你来了，我真不知道该怎么办。再谢你一次。

column1: You want me to follow along, do you? Well, if it ups my chances of a full belly, I'm all for it. You keep me fed, and I'll conjure all you like. Sound good?
column2: 你想让我跟着，是吗？嗯，要是能让我吃饱的机会大一些，我完全赞成。你把我喂饱，我就随你变个够。听着不错？

column1: Well, if you can't help me find food I'm going to have to focus on it alone. It really is pretty important you know.
column2: 嗯，你要是不能帮我找到吃的，我就只好自己一门心思去找了。这真的挺要紧的，你知道。

column1:
I hope I'm not imposing. I just needed to get away from my tent for a bit.

I magicked up what was, in hindsight, a very ill-advised crock of molasses beans. 

I am not cut out for wilderness survival, but this feels halfway civilized. Most nights, nobody goes hungry, and while the accomodations aren't what I might call "inviting", we're warm and dry. 

|And hey, you invited me along! 

Still a bit surprised by that one, honestly. Nobody's ever really taken me seriously before. 

Back at the academy when I was practicing, nobody thought that my flavour of conjuring was worth much notice. 

I mean, when you consider all the strange and magnificent things that magic can do, I guess conjuring food seems a little elementary, but I conjure excellent food, and honestly, what if you were all by yourself on an inescapable island? 

Conjuring food would be positively brilliant then, wouldn't it?

|But maybe it's too much trouble sometimes. The last time I did something really big, it got me sent here. What a rotten time that was. 

I'd perfected a formula for conjuring cake, you see. A nice big one, all fluffy and warm with lemon-buttercreme, sugar roses, and jelly ribbons. 

Jelly ribbons, for heaven's sake. 

Let that sink in for a moment.

|Well I finally tested out the formula and it works a treat, and that cake is positively the best one I've ever tasted. You really couldn't blame me for indulging, could you?

Well, later that night, when I'm so deliriously full of cake I can scarcely stand, some guards come crashing in. 

You see, it turns out I didn't conjure the cake from noplace, as I thought, but instead I conjured it from Prince Jank's wedding party, right out from under their noses!

Such a scandal over a cake, honestly. 

|They accused me of conspiring to disrupt the royal wedding, of being some kind of political saboteur.

They put that awful burn on my neck and then sent me out here to waste away in obscurity.

It's really not all bad though, is it? Here, my skills are actually useful!

Just... for the love of god, don't ask me to make another crock of molasses beans. 

|Oh, and also, I magicked up something for you, as a way of saying thanks. It's just a little trinket, really, a gesture more than a treasure, but I wanted you to know that I appreciate my place here. 

I've put it in your stash, so take a look when you get a chance.
column2:
希望我没有打扰。我只是需要离开帐篷一会儿。

我用法术变出了一坛事后看来非常不明智的糖蜜豆。

我不是在荒野里活命的料，可这儿感觉有了半点文明。大多数夜里没人挨饿，住处虽然称不上“宜人”，我们却暖和又干燥。

|而且嘿，是你邀我一起来的！

说真的，这件事我到现在还有点惊讶。以前从来没有人真正把我当回事。

在学院练习的时候，没人觉得我这种变食的路数值得多看一眼。

我是说，想想魔法能做到的那些奇异又壮丽的事，变出食物似乎有点小儿科，可我变出来的食物极好，而且老实说，要是你孤身一人困在一座逃不掉的岛上呢？

那时候变出食物可就绝顶高明了，不是吗？

|可有时候也许太麻烦了。我上一次做了件真正了不得的大事，结果就被送到了这儿。那段日子可真糟。

我把一套变出蛋糕的配方完善了，你瞧。好大一个，松软又温热，缀着柠檬黄油霜、糖玫瑰和果冻丝带。

果冻丝带，我的天哪。

你先体会体会。

|后来我终于把配方试了出来，效果好极了，那蛋糕绝对是我尝过最棒的一个。你真不能怪我放开了吃，对吧？

结果那天夜里，我被蛋糕撑得晕乎乎的，几乎站不住，几个卫兵闯了进来。

你瞧，原来我并不是像自己以为的那样凭空把蛋糕变出来，而是从 Jank 王子的婚宴上变来的，就在他们眼皮底下！

就为了一块蛋糕闹成这样的丑闻，说真的。

|他们指控我密谋破坏皇家婚礼，说我是某种政治破坏分子。

他们在我脖子上烙了那道可怕的伤，然后把我送到这儿，让我在无人问津里慢慢憔悴。

不过也不全是坏事，对吧？在这儿，我的本事真的有用！

只是……看在老天的份上，别再让我做一坛糖蜜豆了。

|哦，另外，我用法术给你变了样东西，算是道谢。其实只是个小饰物，与其说是宝物，不如说是份心意，可我想让你知道，我珍惜自己在这儿的位置。

我把它放进你的储物里了，有空去看看。

column1: This is quite an adventure after all isn't it? With monsters and maidens and... well more monsters than maidens really. And what maidens there are tend to be more menacing than the monsters. Also, all this alliteration is making me quite hungry. Maybe I'll magic up some meringues?
column2: 这毕竟算得上一次冒险，对吧？有猛兽，有美女，还有……好吧，猛兽其实比美女多。而那些美女往往比猛兽更加凶猛。再说，这一连串头韵把我弄得怪饿的。也许我变几份蛋白霜出来？

column1: Oh my. I hope I'm hearing that wrong. Are you telling me to go out there on my own again?
column2: 哦，天哪。希望我听错了。你是要让我再一个人到外面去吗？

column1: Ah hello! It's good to see you.
column2: 啊，你好！见到你真好。

column1: I'm being paranoid, sorry. The thought of being alone again now that I'm here is quite a dreary one.
column2: 是我太多心了，抱歉。既然已经到了这儿，再想到又要一个人，实在太丧气了。

column1: I really... thought we were becoming friends. I suppose that's my just dessert for being so naive. Keep the meringues. I've rather lost my appetite.
column2: 我真的……以为我们正在变成朋友。我想，这就是我太天真活该得到的那份甜点。蛋白霜你留着吧。我差不多没胃口了。

column1: I might not have the best grain on this island, but the boys need their beer, and I know how to make do with what's available. I'm getting pretty damn good at it too. Try a tankard and judge for yourself.
column2: 我也许拿不出这岛上最好的谷物，可小伙子们需要他们的啤酒，我也知道怎么将就手头有的东西。我他妈也越做越有两下子了。来一扎，你自己评判。

column1: Come on in, put your feet up. What can I get you?
column2: 进来吧，把脚搁起来。给你来点什么？

column1: You come back whenever you're thirsty.
column2: 渴了你就回来。

column1: Sorry, I'm not buying right now, got too much stock as it is. If you're looking to spend some coin though, I've got plenty of room for that.
column2: 抱歉，我眼下不进货，存货已经太多了。不过你要是想花几个钱，我这儿有的是货。

column1: You're probably looking for some weapons and gear, right? I can hook you up.
column2: 你大概是来找武器和装备的，对吧？我能给你配上。

column1: Come back anytime. As long as you got coin, I got goods.
column2: 随时回来。只要你有钱，我就有货。

column1: Subtle magics can be used to ease the body back to wholeness. These magics I can perform, and the injured among us will recover more quickly for it.
column2: 精微的法术可以让身体慢慢恢复完好。这些法术我能施展，我们当中的伤者也会因此好得更快。

column1: Do you need something?
column2: 你需要点什么？

column1: Do take care.
column2: 请多保重。

column1: I know much of herbs, salves, poisons, and the like. There is much that surrounds us that can be used to mend our bodies, if one knows what to look for. The injured will need my expertise.
column2: 我对草药、药膏、毒药之类颇为了解。我们周围有许多东西能用来修补身体，只要知道该找什么。伤者会需要我的本事。

column1: Yes? What is it?
column2: 嗯？什么事？

column1: Of course. I've preparations to make.
column2: 当然。我还有准备要做。

column1: Yes, have a look at my collection. I'm sure there is something you will want. You have coin, yes?
column2: 是的，看看我的收藏吧。我敢肯定有你想要的东西。你有钱，对吧？

column1: I have many things. Things which may be of use to you.
column2: 我有许多东西。也许对你有用的东西。

column1: I must go hunting soon, yes. Buy what you need now, before I leave.
column2: 我很快就得去狩猎了，是的。趁我走之前，现在把需要的买了。

column1: Yeah, I got a few things, I know a few folks. I'll help you out if you help me out. Simple.
column2: 是啊，我有几样东西，也认识几个人。你帮我，我就帮你。简单。

column1: It's rude to stare, you know.
column2: 盯着人看可不礼貌，知道吗。

column1: Gotta keep moving. See you later, maybe.
column2: 得继续走。回头见，也许吧。

column1: I can forge keys with the best of 'em! Let's see what you got, and I'll show you what I can do.
column2: 我打钥匙不输任何行家！让我看看你带来什么，我再让你看看我能做什么。

column1: Evenin', chaps. Don't get many customers 'round 'ere no more.
column2: 晚上好啊，伙计们。如今这地界可没多少客人了。

column1: Lots o' nasties been crawlin' around 'ere lately. Mind 'ow you go.
column2: 最近这附近爬着不少恶心玩意儿。走路留神。

column1: All part of the job!
column2: 都是分内的事！

column1: You should really surrender.
column2: 你真该投降了。

column1: Shall we?
column2: 来吧？

column1: I can do that.
column2: 这我能做。

column1: Shit, we lost someone!
column2: 操，我们少了一个人！

column1: Neutralize them now!
column2: 现在就解决他们！

column1: Hey, what... oh. \nNah, it's nothing.
column2: 嘿，什么……哦。\n不，没什么。

column1: Should we really be doing this?
column2: 我们真该这么做吗？

column1: Okay, come on Ki. Game face.
column2: 好了，加油，Ki。把脸绷起来。

column1: Pff, this isn't even a thing.
column2: 切，这根本不算回事。

column1: Keey your eyes and your weapons up!
column2: 眼睛睁大，武器举起！

column1: You don't have to like it, you just have to DO it!
column2: 你不必喜欢，你给我去做！

column1: If your complaining doesn't kill us first.
column2: 只要不是你的抱怨先把我们烦死。

column1: Keep your eyes forward!
column2: 眼睛看着前面！

column1: It's not over yet!
column2: 还没完！

column1: Before joining up with you, I was mostly hanging out in caves and stuff. This is way better. It's nice to be able to share the chores and let someone else watch the fire for once.

column1:
You know, when we first met, I had a good feeling about you. That's not something that Lukatt gives you a lot of opportunities to say. I know there's a sorta "don't ask" rule we have about each others' brands, but I wanted to tell you how I got mine. 

It's nothing that crazy, but... well maybe it is sorta crazy, but it's been a while since I told anybody about it, and I trust you, so... here goes. 

I used to be a guard, long time ago. Just a small town guard, your standard "Orc thug in a metal suit" kinda guy. I loved it though. I love people, I love looking out for people, and I love kicking the bad guys' butts, and for a while, that's what I did. 

|At some point though, I blinked and missed it. I started gettin' orders to avoid areas where we knew some rotten stuff was going down. I'd get pulled off of investigations only to find out that nobody else had been put on. 

Someone was getting their palms or their knobs greased to turn a blind eye. Maybe a lot of someones were. I was the only orc in the guard, and... I know that we don't always have the best reputation for being squeaky-clean when it comes to human lands, but I loved my job, and it made me sick to see someone shitting all over it like that. 

I quit, but I refused to walk away.

|I... sorta kept doing what I'd been taught to do, but without the authority of the guards. I fucked up a bunch of the people who'd been placing bribes, and a bunch of the guards who'd been taking 'em. 

At first it was just me, but then some of the other guards who felt the same way I did turned coat and started following me instead. We worked in the dark, but we kept that little town safer than it'd ever been, and man was the guard ever pissed at us. 

They smeared us pretty bad, tried to get the people to hate us, but it didn't work too well. The little guys knew who was really looking out for them. 

|Problem was, I got too safe in that. One night when I was out on a job, I got injured. Looking for a place to lay low, I went to a guy I'd helped out once. He took me in, bandaged me up and fed me... and then brought the guards right to me while I was asleep. I never had a damn chance. 

They were gonna string me up right there, but they wanted to make an example out of me, put the fear into the rest of my guys. 

They took me to the capital court, and put me through a joke trial just so they could say they had a good reason to ship me out here. 

I don't know what happened to the rest of my guys, and I probably never will.  They're smart though, and they can look after themselves. We knew the risks, and we did good work.  No regrets. 

|It's even hard to call this place a regret, isn't it? After all, I got to meet you, and here, in our own way, we're still doing good. In a lot of ways, it reminds me of what I was doing back home, which I guess is why I was thinking about it, and why I wanted to talk about it. Just waxing nostalgic, I suppose. 

Anyway, I don't mean to make you sit up and listen to me gab all night. I put together a little something for you, but it can wait till tomorrow. Just have a look in your stash when you get a chance. 

And Bru, thanks again. Mean it.

你知道，我们第一次见面时，我对你感觉就不错。这种话，卢卡特可不太给你机会说出口。我知道咱们对彼此的烙印有种“别问”的规矩，可我想告诉你我这块是怎么来的。

也不是那么疯狂的事，可是……好吧，也许是有点疯狂，可我有一阵没跟任何人讲过了，我信任你，所以……那就说了。

我以前当过卫兵，很久以前的事了。就是个小镇卫兵，标准的“铁壳里的兽人打手”那种家伙。不过我喜欢。我喜欢人，喜欢照看人，也喜欢踢坏人的屁股，有一段时间，我干的就是这个。

|可不知从哪一刻起，我眨了下眼就错过了。我开始接到命令，要我躲开我们知道有烂事发生的地方。我被从调查里撤下来，事后才发现根本没派别人去接手。

有人的手心被抹了油，或者鸡巴被抹了油，就换来他们睁一只眼闭一只眼。这样的人也许还不少。我是卫队里唯一的兽人，而且……我知道一到人类的地盘，我们并不总是以清白干净出名，可我爱这份工作，看见有人那样往上面拉屎，我恶心透了。

我辞了职，可我拒绝一走了之。

|我……算是继续做我被教过的那些事，只是没有卫兵的权威。我把一帮行贿的人往死里揍，也把一帮受贿的卫兵往死里揍。

起初只有我一个人，后来有些跟我一样想的卫兵倒戈，改跟着我。我们在暗处干活，可我们让那个小镇比以往任何时候都安全，卫队可真是气炸了。

他们拼命抹黑我们，想让人们恨我们，可不太成功。小人物知道到底是谁在照看他们。

|问题是，我因此太安心了。一天夜里我出任务，受了伤。我想找个地方躲躲，就去找一个我帮过一次的人。他收留了我，给我包扎，给我吃的……然后趁我睡着，把卫兵直接领到了我面前。我他妈一点机会都没有。

他们本想当场把我吊死，可他们想拿我做个样子，让我其余的人害怕。

他们把我带到都城的法庭，走了一场笑话似的审判，好让他们能说自己有充分的理由把我送到这儿。

我不知道我其余的人后来怎样了，大概永远也不会知道。不过他们聪明，能照顾自己。我们知道风险，我们也干了好事。不后悔。

总之，我不是有意让你坐起来听我唠叨一整夜。我给你凑了点小东西，不过可以等到明天。有空去你的储物里看看。

column1:
Hey, can we talk? It's important."

Leftie sits cross-legged in front of the fire, a mountain of brown skin glistening in the light.

"It's important to me, anyway. You seen my brand, no doubt."

Leftie gestures to the scar branded on his neck. It reads "misanthropist", a brand you have not seen before or since. After letting you look for a moment, Leftie sighs deeply and hangs his head. 

"I'm gonna tell you how I got it, and then, I'm gonna pack my things. I don't want to go, but you of all people deserve to know.

|I'm not a good person. I've hurt lots of people. Crippled them. Sometimes it was an accident but sometimes it wasn't. Maybe I always thought I had good reasons.

Anyway, when I was young, I got locked up for fighting quite a bit. Maybe just a few days in the bricks here and there, but it was enough that I got used to it. Enough that they were keeping their eyes on me. 

Well, when I got older I got a little tired of it. It's no fun having your whole life come to a crashing halt just because you couldn't help but punch someone acting a raving idiot. I was on good behavior for a long time. I tried real hard, I swear I did.

|On my thirtieth birthday, I decided to celebrate by going out to the pub. Everything was fine. Someone found out it was my birthday, and those that weren't scared of me started buying me rounds. 

I was nearly drunk to death.

I remember a lady there, pretty as you please, with tits like prize pumpkins. She was real interested in me, and it had been a long time since I'd been with a woman, so I'm sure I was interested in her too.

|I say "I'm sure" because I don't really remember. 

Like I said, I was really, really drunk. That whole night is just a blurry spot.

The next thing I remember after that was puking my guts out, covered in blood, beat to shit, and strapped in irons. They wouldn't even tell me what I did until I got to the court and heard the judge read it out.

|The witnesses said I followed her home when the bar closed, broke into her house, and raped her. 

Then, her husband came home and tried to stop me, so I beat him to death in front of his wife. 

In order to make sure she didn't squeal, I strangled her to death too. 

Then, in a craze, I ate parts of them, and ultimately set fire to the house to try to hide the evidence.

They found me unconscious on the street, my mouth full of blood. The neighbor across the alley said she saw everything.

|Murder. Rape. Assault. Arson. Cannibalism. Buggery, for good measure, I suppose. I did so many things, they thought up a new brand just for me."

Leftie looks up, a profound sadness shadowing his face.

"I said I did it. I could have done it. I don't remember doing it, but I did awful things before. I don't know for sure that I didn't do it.

Maybe the alcohol really did something terrible to me, really fucked with my head. 

If I really did those things, then, I'm just the sort of monster who really belongs here on this island, locked away where decent folks don't have to be afraid of me."

|Leftie tosses a log into the fire, watching the sparks fly upward. His voice seems small and distant.

"So that's it. That's the kind of monster you keep under your wing. "

He stands up slowly, putting his hand on your shoulder before walking away. As he goes, his voice floats over his shoulder.

"I'll be ready to leave on a moment's notice. Just say the word, and I'll be gone.
column2:
嘿，能谈谈吗？这事很重要。”

Leftie 指了指脖子上烙下的伤疤。上面写着“厌世者”，这种烙印你从前没见过，以后也不会再见到。让你看了一会儿，Leftie 深深叹了口气，低下了头。

“我要告诉你我是怎么挨上它的，然后我就去收拾东西。我不想走，可偏偏你最该知道。

|我不是个好人。我伤过很多人。把他们打残了。有时候是意外，有时候不是。也许我总觉得自己有正当理由。

总之，我年轻的时候，因为打架没少被关。这儿蹲几天班房，那儿蹲几天，可也够我习惯了。够他们盯上我了。

后来年纪大了些，我有点厌倦了。就因为忍不住揍一个发癫的白痴，整个人生就砸得粉碎，这可一点也不好玩。我安分了很长一段时间。我真的很努力，我发誓，我真的努力了。

|三十岁生日那天，我决定去酒馆庆祝。一切都好好的。有人发现那天是我的生日，那些不怕我的人就开始一轮一轮请我喝酒。

我差点喝死过去。

我记得那儿有个女人，要多标致有多标致，一对奶子跟得奖的南瓜似的。她对我很有兴趣，而我也很久没跟女人睡过了，所以我肯定也对她有兴趣。

|我说“我肯定”，是因为我其实并不记得。

就像我说的，我喝得非常、非常醉。那一整晚只剩一片模糊。

那之后我记得的下一件事，就是吐得肠子都快出来了，浑身是血，被打得稀烂，还戴着镣铐。他们甚至不肯告诉我干了什么，直到我上了法庭，听见法官当众念出来。

|证人说，酒馆打烊后我跟着她回了家，闯进她的屋子，强奸了她。

然后她丈夫回来想阻止我，我就当着他妻子的面把他打死了。

为了不让她把这事嚷出去，我把她也勒死了。

然后我发了疯，吃了他们身上的几块，最后放火烧了房子，想把证据毁掉。

他们在街上发现我昏倒着，嘴里全是血。巷子对面的邻居说，她什么都看见了。

|谋杀。强奸。伤害。纵火。食人。鸡奸，算是再凑上一条，我想。我干的事太多了，他们专门为我想出一种新烙印。”

Leftie 抬起头，深深的悲伤罩在他脸上。

“我说是我干的。我干得出来。我不记得自己干过，可我以前确实做过可怕的事。我没法确定自己没干。

也许酒真的让我做出了可怕的事，真他妈把我的脑子搞砸了。

如果那些事真是我干的，那我就是确实该待在这座岛上的那种怪物，锁在这儿，让正经人不用怕我。”

|Leftie 把一根木头扔进火里，看着火星往上飞。他的声音显得又小又远。

“就是这样。你罩着的，就是这种怪物。”

他慢慢站起来，把手放在你肩上，然后走开。走的时候，声音从他肩后飘过来。

“你一句话，我马上就能走。说一声，我就走了。

column1: You've been great. Whatever you're doing, I want you to know that I will always have the deepest respect for you. I know there have been ups and downs, but it's been a privilege to be along for the ride. Thank you.
column2: 你一直都很好。不管你在做什么，我想让你知道，我对你永远怀着最深的敬意。我知道有起有落，可能跟着走这一程是我的荣幸。谢谢你。

column1: I'm ready.
column2: 我准备好了。

column1: Oh. Um.. hi. Is it time?
column2: 哦。呃……嗨。是时候了吗？

column1: Really? I don't know what to say, other than thank you. I've got your back. On my life, I swear it.
column2: 真的？我不知道该说什么，除了谢谢。我罩着你。用我的命起誓。

column1: I think I've been ready for a long time now. Thank you for everything, and... goodbye.
column2: 我想我已经准备好很久了。谢谢你的一切，还有……再见。

column1: Most of the locks I've seen so far are a much older design. Pretty simple to make keys for if you know what you're doing, which I do. Let me hook you up.
column2: 我到目前为止见过的锁，大多是老得多的样式。懂行的话，配钥匙很简单，而我懂行。我来给你配上。

column1: I got what you need.
column2: 你要的我有。

column1: Happy hunting.
column2: 狩猎愉快。

column1: I never mentioned this before, but this is quite a neat operation you've got here. Hell, you put together twenty people when I asked you to, and I think you could put together a lot more than that. Gives and old mind new things to think about.
column2: 我以前没提过，可你这摊子弄得还真像样。见鬼，我让你凑二十个人，你就凑齐了，我看你还能再凑出多得多。够我这老脑子想想新事了。

column1:
You don't mind if I borrow your ear for a moment?"

Logus takes off his hat and gazes into the firelight, a tired expression stretched across his face.

"This may come as a surprise to you, but I was a naval captain before I was a Lukattite. For more than fifteen years, I sailed the waters between Crest and Tsarath, sometimes as a freighter, sometimes as a patrol. 

Nothing like it, being out on the water.
|Maybe I just got too cocky. Started thinking of the ship as mine, the crew as mine, the ocean as mine. 

I did my job, of course, but that became an afterthought.

I was often tasked with taking down pirates, but I often found ways to deal with them that didn't involve stringing them up. 

I was never specifically told to string them up, of course. Not at first, anyway, but when word got back to the nobility in Crest, they weren't too happy. 

I was reprimanded, given a stern warning and all, but you can imagine what I thought of that, I'm sure. 

|I kept doing things my way. I foolishly thought that there was nothing they could do about it. 

Eventually, they'd had enough, and put a sniffer in my crew.

We had on different hands all the time, so I thought nothing of it, really, but when we get back into port, they're waiting with guards, and this swabber turns around and puts me under arrest for defying the crown. What was I gonna say? I did defy the crown, didn't I?

|Well that was probably bad enough, but I fought them. My crew came to my side, or most of 'em did. 

It didn't matter. 

They beat us down, put me on trial, and executed nine of my sailors. They made me watch.

As for me, I'll give you three guesses as to what old Captain Logus' fate was. They wanted to make sure that all the other captains in their employ got the message loud and clear, and fell into line like trained hounds. 

|Well, I've been trying to find a way off this island ever since. I found that boat, but before you came along, I never managed to put together crew enough to actually sail it. 

Fat lot of good that did us. 

At least now we know our enemy, such as it is. I got no idea how we're gonna overcome a Sud'umKatch, but when you don't have any ideas, that's when you get creative, ain't it?

|Anyway, thanks. For everything. For getting me out of the shipyard, for lighting that beacon, for patching me up and bringing me along. 

You've done enough to prove to me that you're the stuff a real captain is made of, and for that, I salute you.
column2:
不介意我借你耳朵说一会儿吧？”

Logus 摘下帽子，凝视着火光，脸上绷着疲惫的神情。

“这也许会让你意外，可我成为卢卡特人之前，是一名海军舰长。十五年以上，我在克雷斯特和察拉思之间的海上航行，有时跑货运，有时巡逻。

出海的感觉，什么也比不上。
|也许只是我太自以为是了。开始把船当成我的，把船员当成我的，把大海也当成我的。

我当然还在干活，可那已经变成了次要的事。

我常常受命去对付海盗，可我总找得到不必把他们吊死的办法。

当然，从来没有人明确命令我把他们吊死。反正一开始没有。可话传回克雷斯特的贵族那儿，他们可不大高兴。

我挨了申斥，得了严厉警告之类的，可你肯定想得到我是怎么看的。

|我还是按自己的办法来。我愚蠢地以为他们拿我没办法。

最终他们受够了，往我的船员里安了个探子。

船上的人手一直在换，所以我根本没当回事。可等我们回到港口，他们带着卫兵等在那儿，这个擦甲板的转过身来，以违抗王权把我逮捕了。我能说什么？我确实违抗了王权，不是吗？

|这大概已经够糟了，可我还跟他们打了起来。我的船员站到了我这边，起码大部分人是这样。

没用。

他们把我们打趴下，把我送上法庭，处决了我的九名水手。他们让我看着。

至于我，老船长 Logus 的下场是什么，我让你猜三次。他们想让手下所有其他船长都把话听得明明白白，像驯好的猎犬一样乖乖站队。

|自那以后，我一直在想办法离开这座岛。我找到了那条船，可在你来之前，我始终凑不齐真正能把船开走的人手。

结果屁用没有。

至少现在我们认识敌人了，就这么个敌人。我完全不知道要怎么打败一头 Sud'umKatch，可没主意的时候，人才会想办法，对吧？

|总之，谢谢。谢谢一切。谢谢你把我弄出船厂，谢谢你点燃那座信标，谢谢你给我治伤，还带着我。

你做的这些，已经够向我证明你是真正船长的料。为此，我向你敬礼。

column1: This fucking island. There is something really weird happening here. On the one hand, I'm glad to be a part of it, but on the other hand, it would be a lot easier to toss my hat into the sea and spend the rest of me days getting drunk at the shipyard. \nAh well. This is more fun, probably. Nobody at the shipyard took me seriously anyway.
column2: 这他妈的岛。这儿真有邪门的事在发生。一方面，我高兴自己也算一份，可另一方面，把帽子扔进海里，剩下的日子在船厂喝到醉，会轻松得多。\n算了。这样大概更好玩。反正船厂也没人拿我当回事。

column1: You want me to bring anything in particular out to the next raid? Or you just want me to stand by to carry whatever we come out with? EIther way, I'm good to go when you are.
column2: 下次出击，要我带什么特别的吗？还是你只想让我候着，出来带什么我就扛什么？哪种都行，你准备好我就走。

column1: You need somethin'?
column2: 你要什么？

column1: Just let me know when we're heading out.
column2: 出发的时候跟我说一声就行。

column1: Carry your weapons? Rub your feet? You keep me sheltered and fed, and I'll do anything you want. Anything. As long as it ain't fighting, that is.
column2: 帮你扛武器？给你揉脚？你管我住、管我吃，你要我干什么我就干什么。什么都行。只要不是打架。

column1: Whatever you need.
column2: 你需要什么都行。

column1: Don't leave home without me.
column2: 出门别落下我。

column1: I ain't got magic or nothin', but there's still a lot I can do to make sure the injured recover as quick as possible. Just leave it to me.
column2: 我没什么魔法，可要让伤员尽快好起来，我还是能做不少事。交给我就行。

column1: Somethin' up?
column2: 怎么了？

column1: 'Course. Don't get yourself killed.
column2: 当然。别把自己弄死。

column1: If you need some work done, just bring me two identical pieces, and I'll hammer 'em into something even better. You might wanna stand back though. There'll be hot slag flying all over the place.
column2: 要是有活要干，拿两件一模一样的来，我能把它们锤得更好。不过你最好站远点。热渣会溅得到处都是。

column1: Need your weapon worked?
column2: 武器要加工吗？

column1: Sure thing. I'll be here when you need me to do some hammerin'.
column2: 行。你要我抡锤的时候，我就在这儿。

column1: Get ready to die.
column2: 准备受死。

column1: You're already dead.
column2: 你已经死了。

column1: It didn't have to be this way.
column2: 本来不必走到这一步。

column1: Damn.
column2: 该死。

column1: Nothing.
column2: 没什么。

column1: I'm not afraid to die.
column2: 我不怕死。

column1: If we go down, you go down with us!
column2: 我们要是倒下，你也得跟着倒下！

column1: You can do better than that.
column2: 你能打得比这更好。

column1: Shut up and fight.
column2: 闭嘴，动手。

column1: Shut up.
column2: 闭嘴。

column1: When we're done with them, you'll be next.
column2: 收拾完他们，下一个就是你。

column1: You should have tried harder.
column2: 你本该再拼一点。

column1: I won't miss you.
column2: 我不会想念你。

column1: I don't do well in crowds. If you're going somewhere, take me with you.
column2: 我受不了人多。你要去哪儿，带上我。

column1: Well, that's not surprising. I have that effect on people.
column2: 嗯，不意外。我对人就是这效果。

column1: Nothing to say.
column2: 没什么可说的。

column1: Hmm. Well, good to know I'm making you nervous.
column2: 嗯。知道我让你紧张，也好。

column1: Put me down already!
column2: 快把我放下！

column1: I will not be robbed!
column2: 谁也别想抢我！

column1: Fine.
column2: 行。

column1: I will never be a slave!
column2: 我绝不当奴隶！

column1: If that's what it takes.
column2: 非这样不可的话。

column1: You're crazy. Ah well, I don't have anything better to do. Maybe you'll at least be entertaining.
column2: 你疯了。算了，我也没什么更好的事可做。也许你至少能让人解闷。

column1: You just don't take a hint, do you? Let me make this really clear for you - I kill people, and I don't feel bad about it. I've done it a lot, and I'll do it again. Leave me alone.
column2: 你就是听不懂暗示，对吧？那我跟你说清楚——我杀人，而且不觉得难受。我干过很多次，还会再干。离我远点。

column1: Look, I don't care. Leave.
column2: 听着，我不在乎。走开。

column1: You have to be joking.
column2: 你一定是在开玩笑。

column1: Don't waste my time. Go away.
column2: 别浪费我的时间。走开。

column1:
I'm gonna keep this short, but I've got something to say. 

How I got here, I killed a man who ran his mouth. 

I'm not sorry. I'd do it again. 

Killing him made me realize what a stupid joke it was for me to follow all those rules for so long. 

Everything felt like it was made of paper. I could hardly wait to get away from all that bullshit. 

|Life here is real. You work for what you have, and if you don't pull your weight, you die. It's simple, and I like it that way. 

Nothing pisses me off more than being disrespected, and the fact that I haven't buried an axe in you yet speaks to how you've treated me. 

I think you're someone who gets it, and I appreciate that. 

Anytime you need me, I'll have your back.
column2:
我长话短说，可我有句话要说。

我到这儿，是因为杀了一个乱放话的男人。

我不后悔。再来一次我还干。

杀了他，我才明白，自己守那些规矩守了那么久，是个多蠢的笑话。

一切都像是纸糊的。我恨不得马上甩开那堆狗屁。

|这儿的日子是真的。你拥有的都是自己挣来的，不扛自己那份，就得死。很简单，我就喜欢这样。

没有什么比被轻视更他妈让我火大。我到现在还没把一柄斧子埋进你身体，就说明你是怎么待我的。

我觉得你是个懂的人，这我领情。

什么时候你需要我，我都罩着你。

column1: You need someone to knock some heads? I can do that. Just let me know.
column2: 要人去敲几个脑袋？我能办。跟我说一声。

column1: You don't need me?
column2: 你不需要我？

column1: What is it?
column2: 什么事？

column1: Don't run your mouth if you aren't even sure.
column2: 你自己都没准，就别乱放话。

column1: Well, at least I don't have to play nice anymore.
column2: 行，至少我不用再装客气了。

column1: You need access? Oh yes, I can do that. What kind of lock do you need opened?
column2: 你要进去？哦，当然，这我能办。你要开哪种锁？

column1: What is it this time?
column2: 这次又是什么？

column1: Just remember to spread it around a little.
column2: 记得帮我传扬一点。

column1: The creature acknowledges your presence.
column2: 那生物向你致意。

column1: The creature seems to have noticed you, but is not attacking.
column2: 那生物似乎注意到了你，但并没有攻击。

column1: Hmph. A warmup maybe.
column2: 哼。也许热热身。

column1: Watch me work!
column2: 看我怎么干！

column1: How do you want to handle this?
column2: 这事你想怎么处理？

column1: Check this out.
column2: 瞧瞧这个。

column1: Not this again!
column2: 怎么又是这样！

column1: I've lost enough!
column2: 我失去的已经够多了！

column1: Nothing to report, chief.
column2: 没什么可汇报的，老大。

column1: Have I been here before?
column2: 我以前来过这儿吗？

column1: If I live, you owe me a beer!
column2: 我要是活下来，你得请我一杯酒！

column1: See if you assholes \ncan bring down Nazar!
column2: 看你们这帮混蛋\n能不能放倒 Nazar！

column1: Nah, we'll laugh about it later.
column2: 没事，回头再笑。

column1: Just watch my back \nand we'll be fine.
column2: 看好我背后\n我们就没事。

column1: Why do you have to \nbe such a drag?
column2: 你为什么非要\n这么扫兴？

column1: Stop whining and \nput your back into it!
column2: 别抱怨了，\n把劲使上！

column1: Better you than me!
column2: 死你总比死我强！

column1: Wow, did you see that?
column2: 哇，你看见了吗？

column1: You just got shipped out recently, didn't you? I've been here for... oh it must be seven or eight years now. Seems like forever. There's groups of people here and there, little pockets of civilization, but they rise and fall so fast, a fellow scarcely has time to dry his boots.
column2: 你是最近才被押送来的吧？我在这儿……哦，该有七八年了。感觉像过了一辈子。这儿那儿都有一群人，零星几处还算有人烟的地方，可他们兴起又败落得太快，一个人连靴子都来不及晾干。

column1: You tired of looking at me already?
column2: 已经看我看腻了？

column1: What can I do for you?
column2: 我能为你做什么？

column1: Nah, 'course you aren't.
column2: 不，你当然不是。

column1: Well, good luck with everything. On this island, you're gonna need it.
column2: 那好，祝你一切顺利。在这座岛上，你会用得上的。

column1: Why couldn't you just let me walk away?!
column2: 你为什么就不能让我走掉？！

column1: And be left defenseless? I think not.
column2: 然后变得毫无防备？我可不干。

column1: How petty. Take it and leave me be.
column2: 真小气。拿走，别烦我。

column1: I will never be anyone's fool again!
column2: 我绝不再当任何人的傻瓜！

column1: I've no wish to die. Let us see where this goes.
column2: 我可不想死。看看这会走到哪儿吧。

column1: If you're satisfied.
column2: 你要是满意了。

column1: Well then, pleased to be along. Where are we headed?
column2: 那好，能跟着很高兴。我们去哪儿？

column1: Sorry, I'm... finding it a little difficult to walk away. I worked here years ago, you see. Made some good friends here. Lost some good friends here too. I guess it's the closest thing to home I've had since leaving Tsarath. Hell, maybe even since before leaving it. Damned ogres.
column2: 抱歉，我……发现有点难以就这么走开。你看，多年前我在这儿干过。在这儿交过一些好朋友。也在这儿失去过一些好朋友。自从离开察拉思，这大概是我最接近家的地方。见鬼，也许离开之前都没有更像家的。该死的食人魔。

column1: Yes? Is there something you needed?
column2: 嗯？你需要点什么吗？

column1: Really now? You did save my hide, so I am inclined to take you up on that. Provided you have some use for a meat wall like me, of course.
column2: 真的？你确实救了我这条命，所以我倾向于答应。当然，前提是你用得上我这种肉墙。

column1: Well if you're going to change your mind, be quick about it. I won't be staying here reminiscing forever.
column2: 你要是改主意，就快点。我不会永远待在这儿回忆下去。

column1:
Did I ever tell you what happened with me? With Rangda, with Krade, and everything?

Rangda was my wife. 

Most orc men don't get to have a wife at all on account of us having so few women, but there I was getting married with a proper shot at kids and everything. 

I felt like the luckiest orc in the world.

|Of course, Rangda, she doesn't want kids. 

She's an orc through-and-through, that one, violent and impulsive as any of us. 

She wants to join the military, even though women aren't allowed. She doesn't care though, and she runs off to training camp with her boobs strapped down, and what can I do? 

We can't afford to be locking women up, so anything she does, I get the knocks for, and we both know it. 

|Well that's just what happens. Eventually someone finds out she's been lying and she gets booted. Everyone knows damn well it isn't my fault, but that's the law, and when you're an orc who wants a wife, you learn to be very good at following the law. 

Well, they decided to make an example out of her case, and they sent me way out here to Lukatt. 

Forever. 

I spent my entire life being the perfect orc so I'd get picked by a nice lady and get to have some cute little orc babies, and it wasn't good for nothing. 

Just a damn lie. 

|We're all branded here, but mine didn't even hurt. I knew it meant that worthless lie of a life was over, and I was glad to see it go.

Of course, it turns out the whole prison thing is just a damn lie too. They just throw us in this pit knowing we can never leave and hope that we'll kill each other. 

Well, once I got out of my bonds, I stumbled into a labour commune in the foothills, and those men took me in and treated me with more respect than I ever got back home. 

Can you imagine? My phony family gone in an instant, and I find a new, better one in a place that's supposed to be nothing but scumbags.

|Well, people came and people went and before I knew it, I'd been there longer than anybody else. 

They started calling me the foreman and lookin' up to me, and I looked out for 'em right back. Those guys were my everything to me. 

Krade was the mess sergeant at the camp, and he'd been on Lukatt almost as long as I had. 

Always fussing over the boys getting enough to eat and after them to wash their socks. He was a good guy, and we were close. 

|Yeah, I know what you're thinking, and yeah, it kinda was like that, but it was more than just finding a warm place to cram it. 

He would listen to me talk and just... really listen. He cared about what I wanted, not just about what he wanted from me, and he made me feel things I didn't think I deserved. 

I loved that guy. When he died in that accident... well we lost people in accidents all the time, but I missed him. Still do. 

|I got no idea why I felt like you needed to know this. 

Maybe it's because I'm starting to feel close to you too. 

Anyway, go on to bed, it's my turn for fire watch. 

And check your stash when you got a minute. I left you a little something.
column2:
我跟你说过我的事吗？Rangda 的事，Krade 的事，还有那一切？

Rangda 是我的妻子。

大多数兽人男人根本娶不到妻子，因为我们的女人太少。可我那时结了婚，正经有了生孩子的机会，什么都有了。

我觉得自己是世界上最幸运的兽人。

|当然，Rangda 她不想要孩子。

她是个彻头彻尾的兽人，跟我们任何一个一样暴戾，一样冲动。

她想参军，尽管女人不许。她不管，把奶子勒平，跑去了训练营。我能怎么办？

我们关不起女人，所以她干什么，挨打的都是我，这我们俩都清楚。

|结果正是这样。终于有人发现她一直在撒谎，她被开除了。谁都他妈清楚那不是我的错，可法律就是这样。一个想要妻子的兽人，会学会把法律守得非常好。

他们决定拿她的案子做个典型，把我远远送到了这儿，送到卢卡特。

永远。

我花了一辈子做个完美的兽人，好被一位好女人挑中，生几个可爱的小兽人，到头来屁用没有。

只是个该死的谎言。

|我们在这儿都烙了印，可我的甚至不疼。我知道那意味着那种一文不值的谎言人生结束了，我巴不得它结束。

当然，结果整座监狱也只是个该死的谎言。他们把我们扔进这个坑，知道我们永远出不去，巴望着我们自相残杀。

等我挣开身上的绳子，我一头撞进了山脚下的一座劳作公社。那些人收留了我，给我的尊重比我在老家得到的还多。

你能想象吗？我那个假家庭一眨眼就没了，我却在一个本该全是人渣的地方，找到了一个新的、更好的家。

|人来了又走，不知不觉我在那儿待得比谁都久。

他们开始叫我工头，也敬着我，我也反过来照应他们。那些人就是我的全部。

Krade 是营地里管伙食的军士，他在卢卡特待的时间几乎跟我一样长。

他总操心弟兄们吃饱没有，还追着他们去洗袜子。他是个好人，我们很亲近。

|是啊，我知道你在想什么，是啊，确实有那么点意思，可又不只是找个暖和的地方把鸡巴塞进去。

他会听我说话，而且……是真的在听。他在乎我想要什么，而不只是他想从我身上得到什么。他让我生出一些我觉得自己不配有的感觉。

我爱那个人。他死在那场事故里的时候……唉，事故里我们一直在死人，可我想念他。现在也还想。

|我不知道自己为什么觉得你该知道这些。

也许是因为我开始觉得跟你也亲近了。

总之，去睡吧，轮到我守火了。

有空看看你的存货。我给你留了点东西。

column1:
Got a sec?"

Paul settles his huge body on the floor near the fire, stretching his legs out and relaxing. His clothes are tattered, and he is marred with scratches and dirt, but his eyes sparkle softly in the light, and his woodsman's beard is slashed open with a broad smile.

"This one-on-one thing is like a tradition, right? I come find you and spill all my secrets, talk about my tragic past and then handshake or hug or something and we're friends forever?"

Paul laughs.

|"Well, let's see how I do. I was born on this island, as far as I know. No burn on my neck or nothin', but I never really lived anyplace that had a law to break in the first place. Talking to some of these guys, I'm sure I've done worse than them. Never thought much of it, to be honest. You do what you have to do to get by, right?

It's true though that I've always preferred honest work to hurting people, so maybe that's worth something to ya. I mean, hurting someone is work too, isn't it? Why be the source of all that suffering when you could just lend each other a hand and get a better deal out of the whole works?

I get that you guys don't like this place. It can be a rough ride, sometimes, even if it is my home. 

|I'm having fun with it all, though. I usually just mind my business, do my work, and bugger off. Never really loaned my axe to something so important to so many people, and it feels good to be looked up to for reasons other than just my height, you know?

This might have started as just a little adventure, but I like you, and I hope we can call each other friends. "

Without warning, Paul extends one of his huge arms around you and pulls you close against him in a momentary hug.

"Thanks for having me on.
column2:
有空吗？”

Paul 在火堆旁的地上坐下，那副巨大的身躯把腿伸开，放松下来。他的衣服破烂，身上带着抓痕和泥土，可眼睛在火光里柔柔地发亮，樵夫的大胡子被一个宽阔的笑容从中豁开。

“这种一对一，算是个传统，对吧？我来找你，把秘密一股脑倒出来，讲讲我悲惨的过去，然后握个手、抱一下什么的，我们就永远是朋友了？”

Paul 笑了。

|“那我就看看我讲得怎么样。就我所知，我生在这座岛上。脖子上没烙印，啥也没有，可我从来没在一个有法可犯的地方真正生活过。跟这儿这些人聊过，我肯定干过比他们更糟的事。老实说，我从没怎么当回事。为了过日子，该干什么就干什么，对吧？

话又说回来，比起伤人，我确实一直更喜欢老实干活，所以这也许对你还值点什么。我是说，伤人也是干活，不是吗？能互相搭把手，从整桩事里换到更好的结果，何必自己去当那一切苦的源头？

我明白你们不喜欢这地方。有时候确实难熬，哪怕这儿是我的家。 

|不过我对这一切玩得挺开心。我通常只管自己的事，干完自己的活，然后就闪人。从来没把我的斧子借给一件对这么多人这么要紧的事，被人高看，不是光因为我个子高，这感觉不错，你懂吧？

这也许一开始只是一场小冒险，可我喜欢你，希望我们可以互相称作朋友。”

毫无预兆，Paul 伸出一条巨大的胳膊揽住你，把你拉进怀里，短暂地抱了一下。

“谢谢你让我留下。

column1:
Hey, wanna hear something funny? It's about the thing that got me sent out here to this rock."

Peregrine sits down beside you, his eyes hidden beneath his bandana and his crooked smile cracking his face practically in half. 

"So I'm a burglar. You know that, and I've never tried to hide it. Not much point, is there? For what it's worth, I never burgled anyone who couldn't stand to be taken down a few pegs. 

Mostly by accident, mind you. Hard-working poor folks ain't got much worth taking, and if you take from someone who has more than he knows what to do with, sometimes he doesn't even notice. Those ones are the best. 

|Anyway, my habit of taking bites out of big fish meant I sometimes pissed off people with some power. A merchant here, a senator there. Most of 'em just went to the guards, and then a little birdie would tell me to lay low for a while, and I would, and in a few weeks it would blow over and I'd be back in business. 

If a guy is a halfway decent burglar, you make enough coin on one job that you don't have to do it very often, so there's lots of time for the trail to cool off. You cut your hair, run some distractions, and you stay ahead of the curve. 

Choose the right targets, and sometimes even the guard doesn't want you to get caught. It's a special kind of warm and fuzzy stealing from someone everybody hates. 

|Well the last job I did before this mess, I hit this one mansion owned by one of the noble houses. The place was all dark, so I thought nobody was home, and I worked my magic and got inside, clean as you please. 

I scrapped together a decent parcel of souvenirs and was getting ready to make my escape when I heard something in the house. 

I probably should have just made my getaway immediately, but the noise was strange, and I was curious. 

|I found a door half-opened, and when I looked inside, there in the romantic candlelight is goddamn Senator Malcolm, up to his eyebrows in the thighs of a strapping orcish manservant. 

I think that orc's haft was the first honest thing that ever passed through old Malkie's lips. 

|I stared just a little too long, and the servant saw me. I ran for it, and I got away, but Malkie went into panic mode, started throwing money around, and all my usual contacts in the guard went silent. 

I think one of 'em sold me out, but it hardly matters. Point is, Malkie was terrified I would tell someone what I saw and ruin his reputation, as if he needed any help. 

|If you went through the court, you know how it is. 

They give you a chance to speak, but it hardly matters, then they brand you and lock you up. 

If you pissed off just the right person, and they want to make extra special sure that you'll never open your yap, then they ship you out here. 

They probably should've cut my tongue, right?"

|Peregrine laughs a bit before standing up. 

"Anyway, that's all. Now if something bad ever happens to me, you'll have to be the one to tell Malkie's wife all about his romantic adventures, aye? Someone's gotta do it.

Maybe it wasn't as funny as I thought, but it felt good to finally tell someone."

Peregrine claps you on the shoulder, and gives you a warm smile and a rare glimpse of his blue eyes.

"Thanks.
column2:
嘿，想听件好笑的吗？就是那件把我送到这块石头上来的事。”

Peregrine 在你身边坐下，眼睛藏在头巾底下，那抹歪笑几乎把他的脸咧成两半。 

“所以我是个入室盗贼。你知道，我也从没想藏过。藏着也没什么意思，对吧？不管怎么说，我偷的人，都是经得起被杀杀威风的。 

当然，这多半是碰巧。卖力干活的穷人没什么值得拿的，要是你偷一个钱多得不知道怎么花的人，有时候他甚至不会发现。那种最好。 

|总之，我这从大鱼身上咬一口的习惯，意味着我有时会惹毛有权有势的人。这儿一个商人，那儿一个参议员。他们大多数只是去找卫兵，然后就会有只小鸟告诉我先躲一阵，我就躲，过几个星期风头过去，我又重新开张。 

一个人要是入室行窃还算凑合，一票就挣够钱，不用经常干，所以有的是时间让踪迹凉下来。你把头发剪了，布置些障眼法，始终抢在前头。 

目标挑对了，有时候连卫兵都不想让你被抓住。偷一个谁都恨的人，有种特别的暖乎乎。 

|唉，出这摊乱子之前我干的最后一票，我进了一座贵族世家的宅子。那地方一片漆黑，我以为没人在家，我使上老本事，进去得干干净净，随你怎么说。 

我胡乱凑出一包还像样的纪念品，正准备开溜，忽然听见宅子里有动静。 

我大概该立刻就跑，可那声音很怪，我又好奇。 

|我发现一扇门半开着，往里一看，浪漫的烛光下，该死的参议员 Malcolm 正把脸埋进一个壮实兽人男仆的大腿之间，连眉毛都陷进去了。 

我觉得，那根兽人的鸡巴是老 Malkie 嘴唇间经过的第一件诚实的东西。 

|我多看了那么一小会儿，那个仆人看见我了。我撒腿就跑，也跑掉了，可 Malkie 慌了神，开始到处撒钱，我在卫兵里那些常联络的人全都不吭声了。 

我觉得其中有一个出卖了我，不过这无所谓。关键是，Malkie 怕得要死，怕我把看见的事告诉别人，毁了他的名声，好像这名声还用得着别人帮忙才会坏似的。 

|你要是上过法庭，就知道是怎么回事。 

他们给你一个说话的机会，可这无所谓，然后给你烙上印，把你关起来。 

要是你正好得罪了那个人，而他们想特别、特别地确保你再也不会张开那张嘴，就把你送到这儿来。 

他们大概该把我的舌头割了，对吧？”

|Peregrine 笑了一下，然后站起来。 

“总之就这些。要是以后我出了什么事，就得由你去把 Malkie 那些浪漫奇遇通通告诉他老婆了，是吧？总得有人去说。

也许没我想的那么好笑，可终于告诉了某个人，感觉不错。”

Peregrine 拍了拍你的肩膀，给你一个温暖的笑，还难得让你瞥见他的蓝眼睛。

“谢了。

column1:
I know you aren't from Tsarath, so you don't know how things work there, but women have it pretty crappy. There are hardly any of us, and we need to have a lot of kids in order to keep numbers up. They don't force us, not technically, but they keep us out of anything that might get us hurt or killed. 

I always wanted to be a warrior, or an adventurer, but I couldn't get anyone to sell me a sword, let alone teach me to use it.

When the men started courting, as I knew they would, I started thinking that maybe I should just put the dream to rest. Settle down and have kids, live the cushy life I was handed. 

|I even really liked one of them, big mean-looking orc named Nazar. He was everything I wanted to be. Strong, deadly. You should've seen him handle a sword. 

Well, I married him, and he was great. When I asked him to teach me how to use a sword like he did, he was so happy. I think he was excited that I was interested in something he could do. He was a great teacher, too.

For a while, things were good. The sword was a distraction, and I managed to forget that I was still in that gilded cage. Eventually I got restless, though, and decided to go to the military training camp. Nazar begged me not to go, he said I'd get caught, but I had to follow my heart. I took a man's name, put on bulky clothes, and left. 

|For a few weeks it was fine. I was doing well, and the sword techniques Nazar had taught me were getting me noticed. In hindsight, getting noticed was the worst thing that could've happened. One of the sergeants started to suspect that I might be a woman, and he outed me in front of everybody. I was thrown out and sent home.

The next day they came and took Nazar away. I was being tried for identity fraud, and he was my collateral. The trial barely took any time at all, and they found me guilty. I had embarassed them, so they decided to make an example out of my situation, and they sent him here, to Lukatt, and told me to go home and find a new husband. 

I was furious. Nazar had nothing to do with it, he didn't deserve to be punished for what I had done, but there was nothing I could do. 

|Within a year I had remarried. The new man I picked was a foppish thing I chose because I thought he couldn't be bothered to lay with me. He often had men stay the night with him, and I would sleep alone and dream of coming here to find Nazar and set him free so we could be together again. 

Well a few months ago, the opportunity came up. There was an orc man who had been posing as a woman and having illicit encounters with some of the noble merchants. When he was found out, it came crashing down on him hard, and he was all lined up to be shipped out here too. 

I pulled a few strings and made a switch. He actually does look a lot like a woman, so this time passing was easy. 

He went to my estate and presumably lives like a pampered lady with my husband, and I came here in tatters to find the husband I never forgot.

|Whether all that is worth it... I don't know. I came here looking for either a reunion or for closure. Still sorting it all out.

I have you to thank for the opportunity.

Now, go rest. It's another busy day tomorrow.
column2:
我知道你不是从察拉思来的，所以你不知道那儿的规矩，可女人的日子挺烂。我们几乎没几个，还得生很多孩子，才能把人数维持住。他们不强迫我们，严格说不算，可他们不让我们碰任何可能让我们受伤或者送命的事。 

我一直想当个战士，或者冒险者，可我找不到任何人肯卖给我一把剑，更别说教我怎么用。

男人们开始来求爱的时候，我知道他们会来，我便开始想，也许该把这个梦埋了。安定下来，生孩子，过他们递到我手里的那种安逸日子。 

|我甚至真的喜欢过其中一个，一个看着很凶的大块头兽人，名叫 Nazar。他就是我想成为的一切。强壮，致命。你真该看看他怎么使剑。 

于是，我嫁给了他，他很好。我求他教我像他那样用剑，他高兴极了。我想，他是兴奋，因为我对他会的事感兴趣。他也是个很好的老师。

有一阵，日子过得挺好。剑让我分了心，我设法忘掉自己还在那只镀金的笼子里。可后来我又待不住了，决定去军训营。Nazar 求我别去，他说我会被抓住，可我得听自己的心。我顶了个男人的名字，穿上肥大的衣服，走了。 

|头几个星期还好。我干得不错，Nazar 教我的剑术让人注意到了我。事后看来，被人注意到是可能发生的最糟的事。有个军士开始怀疑我可能是个女人，当众揭穿我是女人。我被赶出军营，送回了家。

第二天他们来把 Nazar 带走了。我因身份欺诈受审，而他是我的抵押品。审判几乎没花什么时间，他们判我有罪。我让他们丢了脸，所以他们决定拿我这事来做个样子，把他送到这儿，送到卢卡特，叫我回家再找个丈夫。 

我气疯了。Nazar 跟这件事毫无关系，他不该为我做的事受罚，可我什么也做不了。 

|不到一年，我又嫁了人。我挑的这个新人是个娘娘腔的货色，我选他，是因为我觉得他懒得跟我上床。他经常留男人过夜，我就一个人睡，梦见来这儿找到 Nazar，放他自由，我们又能在一起。 

几个月前，机会来了。有个兽人男人一直扮成女人，跟一些贵族商人暗中苟合。他一被揭穿，事情就狠狠砸在他身上，他也排上了被送到这儿来的队。 

我托了关系，把我们掉了包。他其实看起来真的很像女人，所以这回蒙混过关很容易。 

他去了我的庄园，大概正跟我丈夫过着被宠着的贵妇日子，而我一身破烂地来到这儿，找我从没忘记的那个丈夫。

|这一切值不值得……我不知道。我来这儿，要么是为了重逢，要么是为了一个了断。还在慢慢理清楚。

能有这个机会，我得谢你。

现在去休息吧。明天又是忙碌的一天。

column1:
A moment first, if you please. 

You have boldly met each of my expectations, and you have been a bottomless draught of pleasure. I am fortunate to have met you.

I thought long and hard on how to best show my appreciation for this, and perhaps it is trite, but I have wrought you a gift. It is simple, but it is a token of my affection, and indeed of my loyalty.

Now, lay with me near the fire awhile. Tonight, I've the greatest of need for you.
column2:
请先容我片刻。 

你大胆地满足了我的每一个期待，你是一杯怎么喝也喝不尽的欢愉。能遇见你，是我的幸事。

我长久地、认真地想过该如何最好地表达这份感激。也许这有些俗套，可我为你打造了一件礼物。它简单，却是我情意的信物，也实在是我忠诚的信物。

现在，到火边来与我交合片刻。今夜，我对你的渴求无以复加。

column1: Have you considered what you will do when all your battles are won? Will I still have a means to vie for your attention once this is done? I find myself rather distressed at the thought of it. Ah, pay me no mind.

column1:
It's nice to be able to take a few minutes and kick your feet out, huh? 

When I first got here, I thought it would be a constant struggle to survive, that I'd have a short, miserable life, and never be able to relax again. 

Funny how things don't turn out the way you think they will. 

I mean, who could've guessed that this island would be such a shit-show, right? 

|Not that it makes all that much difference for me, really. 

I mean, Lukatt is as good as anywhere else. 

I kept company with worse people than this before getting shipped out, so it's just the same shit in a different pile."

Rosaline stares into the fire for a moment, her bright smile gradually fading from her face, as she chooses her next mouthful of words. 

|"I was trained to be an assassin, you know. Can you imagine anything so stupid? 

Well, when I was a little girl I didn't think it was stupid. 

I came from a big family, and a poor one, so the day I saw the dancers' troupe come to town, and I told my parents that I wanted to be one, I was shocked when they said yes. 

Of course, my parents must've known that the dancers were something darker, that they would take little girls away and change them. 

I'm pretty sure they even paid my parents, thinking about it now, but at the time I was just a little girl having her wish come true.

|And to be sure, they did teach me how to dance. 

It wasn't until I was thirteen that I learned we would sometimes have to kill people.

Lots of girls were horrified when they found out, but not me. 

There was something romantic, I think, about the idea of being beautiful and alluring and also ridding the world of dangerous, evil people. 

I took to my training eagerly, and I was good at it, for a while.

|Eventually though, I started asking questions they didn't like. 

You see, I wasn't going to be ridding the world of dangerous people per se - I was going to be killing whoever was on their list. 

I had no way of knowing if those people actually deserved to die or not. 

Even the people who gave me the orders didn't know why. 

We were just expected to... to do it.

|I wasn't going to have any of that. 

I ran away, and I've been running for years. 

They don't let you leave, you see, so if you stay in one place for too long, they find you. 

And of course, they eventually did find me, and they pulled some strings to ship me out here, probably to scare the other girls into obedience. 

I guess even they didn't know what sort of place this really is.

|Well, screw them. 

I'm freer as a convict than I ever was as a dancer anyway, so it feels like a trade up. 

And you, well, we've kicked some asses, but because we had to, or because we wanted to, not because someone told us to, and that difference is everything to me."

Rosaline stands up, her cheerful smile creeping back across her face as she turns to go.

"I guess I'm just trying to say thanks.

“能有几分钟把脚一伸歇歇，真不错，对吧？

我刚到这儿的时候，以为会一刻不停地挣扎求生，以为自己这条命又短又惨，再也放松不了。

有意思，事情总不会照你想的来。

我是说，谁猜得到这岛会是这么一场狗屎闹剧，对吧？

|倒也不是说这对我有多大分别，真的。

我是说，卢卡特不比别的地方差。

被送走之前，我结交过比这帮人更糟的，所以不过是换了堆的同一摊屎。”

Rosaline 盯着火看了一会儿，明亮的笑容渐渐从脸上褪去，她斟酌着下一句要说出口的话。

|“你知道吗，我是被训练来当刺客的。你能想象还有比这更蠢的吗？

唉，我还是个小女孩的时候，可不觉得这有多蠢。

我家人口多，又穷，所以那天我看见舞团进城，跟父母说我想当其中一个，他们居然答应了，我震惊极了。

当然，我父母一定知道那些舞者更阴暗，知道他们会把小女孩带走，把她们变成别的样子。

我现在回想，相当确定他们甚至给了我父母钱，可那时候我只是个愿望成真的小女孩。

|而且说真的，他们确实教过我跳舞。

直到十三岁，我才知道我们有时得杀人。

好多女孩知道以后都吓坏了，我没有。

又美丽又勾人，还能把危险的、邪恶的人从这世上除掉，我觉得这想法里有种浪漫。

我迫不及待地投入训练，而且有一阵子，我做得很好。

|可到后来，我开始问他们不爱听的问题。

你看，我要除掉的并不是危险的人本身——我要杀的是他们名单上的任何人。

我根本没法知道那些人到底该不该死。

连给我下命令的人都不知道为什么。

他们只是指望我们……去做。

|这种事我才不干。

我跑了，而且跑了好多年。

他们不许你离开，你明白的，所以你要是在一个地方待得太久，他们就会找到你。

当然，他们最后还是找到了我，托关系把我送到这儿来，大概是想把别的女孩吓得乖乖听话。

我猜连他们自己也不知道这地方究竟是什么样。

|去他们妈的。

反正我当罪犯比当初当舞者更自由，所以感觉像是赚到了。

而你呢，嗯，我们也干翻过一些人，可那是因为我们不得不，或者因为我们想这么干，不是因为有人叫我们干，这个区别对我就是一切。”

Rosaline 站起身，转身要走的时候，那副快活的笑容又悄悄爬回她脸上。

“我想我只是想说声谢谢。”

column1:
Have you got a moment? 

I've been hearing sordid rumours flying around about me, and how I came to be here. I thought I'd take the opportunity to set the record straight with you before you ended up hearing who-knows-what from God-knows-who."

Shapiro sits down by the fireside and smooths his robe out across his lap before continuing, stroking his beard thoughtfully.

"I was a professor at the academy of sorcery in Crest, and part of that position is devoting a certain amount of time toward research, developing new ways to use magic. There are many procedures to follow, of course, and much paperwork to file. Too much, if you ask me. 

|Most of my peers worked on flashy applications, but I didn't care to follow their lead. I worked on subtler things, ways to affect people. Charms, enchantments, curses, and such things. 

It's a fascinating field, but I'll get carried away if I talk about it, so you'll have to forgive me if I skip the details for the time being. 

In any event, some of my students took a great interest in my private work, and I began collaborating with a number of them. Some of them even volunteered to be personally experimented upon. 

This was, of course, against the rules of the academy, but we were so steeped in our work that it barely registered. 

|We did that for a few months, and things were going well. I was on the verge of several useful new formulae, and the students were engaging and enthusiastic. 

Then one of them died. We have no idea why or how, but one day, she simply died. There's no way it could have been the magic, I'm sure of it, but the other students began to panic. 

One of them went to the administrative board and reported what we'd been doing. 

Once that started, a whole inquisition opened up. The students all spoke against me at the hearings, and I was thrown into prison, branded as a charlatan, and shipped out here. 

|I didn't kill that girl, do you understand? Our experiments on her were concluded months prior to her death, and even if it had been the magic, she volunteered... begged even, to be the subject of those experiments. 

She was an intelligent adult woman capable of making her own decisions, and she understood that there could be risks. All of the other students endured similar experimentation with no ill effects. We were not dabbling in deadly arcana.

Truthfully, I suspected foul play by one of the other students, but I had scant proof of anything, and I knew that bringing that up in the hearings would only serve to drive myself upon the stake further. 

|So there you have it. Believe me or don't, that is the tale of Shapiro the wicked Charlatan, straight from his own mouth. When you hear the rumours, as you surely will, I trust you'll do me the courtesy of at least remembering what I've said. 

You know, just speaking of this has me quite sharp to edit some of the formulae I can still remember. Let me take fire watch, if you will, since I'll be awake anyway. 

And thank you for listening. You're fairer to me than I am used to, and it does not go unnoticed.

“你有一会儿空吗？

我听见四处在传关于我的肮脏谣言，还有我是怎么到这儿来的。我想趁你从天知道谁那儿听见天知道什么之前，跟你把事情说清楚。”

Shapiro 在火边坐下，把长袍在膝上抹平，这才继续说下去，若有所思地抚着胡子。

“我曾是克雷斯特法术学院的一名教授。这个职位有一部分，是要拨出一定时间做研究，开发使用魔力的新方法。当然有许多程序要遵守，还有大堆文书要归档。要我说，实在太多了。

|我大多数同行都在做花哨的应用，我却不想跟他们走。我做的是更精细的东西，影响人的办法。魅惑、附魔、诅咒，诸如此类。

这领域迷人得很，可我一开口就会收不住，所以请你原谅我眼下略过细节。

总之，有些学生对我的私人研究非常感兴趣，我开始和其中一些人合作。有几个甚至自愿亲自当实验对象。

这当然违反学院的规矩，可我们埋头在工作里，这事几乎没进脑子。

|我们这样干了几个月，事情进展顺利。我眼看就要得到好几条有用的新公式，学生们也投入，又有热情。

然后他们当中一个死了。我们不知道为什么，也不知道是怎么回事，可有一天，她就这么死了。这绝不可能是魔力造成的，我确定，可其他学生开始恐慌。

其中一个人去了院务会，把我们做的事报告了上去。

这一开了头，一场大审讯就展开了。听证会上学生们全都说我的不是，我被关进监狱，按江湖骗子的罪名烙了印，然后送到这儿来。

|那个女孩不是我杀的，你明白吗？我们对她的实验在她死前几个月就结束了，就算真是魔力的缘故，也是她自愿的……甚至是求着要当那些实验的对象。

她是个有头脑的成年女人，能自己拿主意，也明白可能会有风险。其他学生全都经受了类似的实验，没有任何不良后果。我们并不是在玩弄致命的奥术。

说实话，我怀疑是另一个学生下的手，可我证据少得可怜，而且我知道，在听证会上提起这个，只会把我更狠地推向火刑柱。

|所以就是这些。信不信由你，这就是邪恶的江湖骗子 Shapiro 亲口讲出的故事。等你听见那些谣言——你肯定会听见——我相信你至少会给我这个面子，记住我说过的话。

你知道，光是说起这些，我就急着想改一改我还记得的那些公式。这班守夜让我来吧，如果你愿意，反正我也睡不着。

谢谢你愿意听。你待我比我一向受到的更公平，这我看在眼里。”

column2: 遇上一个懂得怎样文明交谈的人，有多让人耳目一新，我说不出来，而且我当然找得到更糟的同伴。也许你愿意考虑……把我们的交往再延长一些？

column1: Hello, stranger. To what do I owe the pleasure?
column2: 你好，陌生人。不知何等荣幸，得以见你？

column1: Why yes, of course. Who wouldn't want me along. Do you have proper arrangements made?
column2: 当然愿意。谁会不想带着我。该有的安排，你做好了吗？

column1: Well, you'd best put your affairs in order first. Do come and find me later.
column2: 那你最好先把自己的事情料理妥当。回头再来找我。

column1:
Who would have thought such fine company could be found on such a wretched rock? Ever since joining you, I've found myself... enthralled by your manner of leadership. I found it curious at first, but I am beginning to understand. 

Know that I intend to remain for as long as you will have me. 

Take this, a small token of my esteem, and think of me whenever your eyes come upon it. Know that your company I treasure.
column2:
谁能想到，在这么一块凄惨的破石头上，竟能遇见这么好的同伴？自从加入你以来，我发现自己……被你领导的方式迷住了。起初我只觉得好奇，可我开始明白了。

你要知道，只要你还肯要我，我就打算留下来。

收下这个吧，一份小小的敬意。每当你的目光落在它上面，就想想我。你要知道，与你为伴，是我所珍惜的。

column1: I realize how difficult it must be to lead a group this large all alone, so I have been trying to do my part. Some of the company you keep could well do with a lesson in civility, and really, who better to give it to them?
column2: 我明白，独自带领这么一大群人有多难，所以我一直在尽自己的一份力。你身边有些人，确实该上一堂礼仪课，再说，还有谁比我更适合来教？

column1: That wouldn't do at all. I beg you to reconsider.
column2: 那可万万使不得。求你重新考虑。

column1: It is always a delight to see you.
column2: 见到你永远是一件乐事。

column1: That was cruel of you. I'll need a moment to dry my eyes.
column2: 你这可太残忍了。我得花一会儿把眼泪擦干。

column1: I was so close! Curse you!
column2: 我就差一点点！诅咒你！

column1: I don't care who you are or what you did, as long as you deal with me in honest coin. I'll give you a fairer shake than any trader in Crest ever did.
column2: 我不在乎你是谁，也不在乎你做过什么，只要你拿老实钱跟我做买卖。我给你的公道，比克雷斯特任何一个商贩都多。

column1: Even convicts need supplies.
column2: 就算是罪犯，也需要补给。

column1: This is just a stopover as I make some rounds to a few other places. Get what you need before I go.
column2: 我这只是路过，还要再到几个地方转转。我走之前，把你要的拿上。

column1: I know my way around the outdoors, and the wilds of Lukatt are no different from the wilds anywhere else. Still, it is nice to sleep in a camp every once in a while.
column2: 野外我熟悉，卢卡特的荒野跟别处的荒野也没什么不同。不过，偶尔能在营地里睡上一觉，还是挺好的。

column1: Care for some spoils from the wilds?
column2: 想来点荒野里的收获吗？

column1: I'll be heading out in the morning. Maybe my travels will bring me back here. Maybe not.
column2: 我早上就出发。也许我的路还会把我带回这儿。也许不会。

column1: You aren't going to win.
column2: 你赢不了的。

column1: This doesn't end well for you.
column2: 你不会有好下场。

column1: That seems important.
column2: 那好像很重要。

column1: I wasn't fast enough.
column2: 我不够快。

column1: Don't worry, we'll... we'll do something!
column2: 别担心，我们……我们会做点什么的！

column1: Hmm. Nothing.
column2: 嗯。没什么。

column1: Maybe.
column2: 也许。

column1: We shouldn't be here!
column2: 我们不该待在这儿！

column1: I see.. so much death!
column2: 我看见了……这么多死亡！

column1: We'll be fine. Trust me.
column2: 我们会没事的。相信我。

column1: Today isn't the day for that.
column2: 今天不是干这个的时候。

column1: You're not helping.
column2: 你这不是在帮忙。

column1: Just focus!
column2: 专心点！

column1: You could have done better.
column2: 你本可以做得更好。

column1: What a waste.
column2: 真是浪费。

column1: It's a shame that none of the books we'll find here will be anything resembling recent. Near as I can tell, the last piece of print I found was at least a hundred years old. Just a guess, of course.
column2: 可惜，我们在这儿能找到的书，没有一本像是近年的。就我判断，我找到的最后一件印刷品至少有一百年了。当然，只是猜测。

column1: Oh, that's rather surprising. Are you sure?
column2: 哦，这可相当意外。你确定吗？

column1: Good day to you.
column2: 祝你日安。

column1: I see. Well don't do anything rash, now.
column2: 我明白了。那眼下可别鲁莽行事。

column1: Well perhaps I'll head back to the archive, then. Wish me luck.
column2: 那我也许该回档案室去了。祝我好运吧。

column1: You are remarkably strong!
column2: 你强得惊人！

column1: Wouldn't that be tidy? No, I think not!
column2: 那样岂不省事？不，我可不这么想！

column1: I am beaten, then. Take it and leave me in peace!
column2: 那我是败了。拿去吧，让我清静！

column1: Aren't I prisoner enough already?
column2: 我当囚犯还当得不够吗？

column1: I've little choice, it seems. Perchance you will be interesting.
column2: 看来我没什么选择。说不定你会挺有意思。

column1: Very well, the archive is yours.
column2: 好吧，档案室是你的了。

column1: Yes, marvellous! I'm sure you have plenty of interesting tales to tell.
column2: 对，妙极了！我肯定你有不少有趣的故事可讲。

column1: I've been in this archive for months. I could survive here indefinitely, I suppose, but I admit it's been growing somewhat tedious, and I'm not sure what I will do if my health fails or I become injured. Perhaps it's time for a change of pace.
column2: 我在这座档案室里待了有几个月了。我想我可以一直在这儿活下去，可我承认，这日子越来越乏味了，而且我不知道要是身体不行了，或者受了伤，我该怎么办。也许是时候换个节奏了。

column1: That book is quite a shock, I must say. Did you find it in the locked room?
column2: 那本书相当惊人，我得说。你是在锁着的房间里找到它的吗？

column1: You know, I was just thinking the same thing! It would be grand to have someone to talk to.
column2: 你知道吗，我刚才也在想同样的事！有个人可以说说话就太好了。

column1: Well that is a shame. I suppose I will stay here until I figure out what to do next.
column2: 那可真遗憾。我想我会留在这儿，直到想好下一步做什么。

column1:
Are you available for a moment? I'd like a word. "

Vankan sits down, smoothing his kilt over his lap. He strokes his beard idly while staring into the flickering firelight.

"I haven't told you this yet, because it tends to freak people out, but I see things. Flashes of things. Flashes of you. Hell, it's what got me sent out here to this island in the first place. 

When I first realized that the things I see are real, I thought it was my obligation to help people, try to warn them about the flashes I saw, save them from the pain of their misfortunes if I could. And I could, so I tried.

|At first I was a novelty. People would come and visit the orc with the third eye, listen to me prattle on as I sifted through pictures of maybes and mights. People thought I was an entertainer, so I even made some money. I wasn't going to say no.

Well, I guess a bunch of people started realizing that I was telling the truth, that my flashes were real, and they started getting scared of me. People weren't coming to me anymore, and all of a sudden I wasn't helping anyone. 

It was that, more than the money, you know. I mean, could you stand by and let something awful happen to a bystander if you had the power to stop it? Wouldn't that feel just awful?

So... I tried.

|I tried so hard, that I became THAT guy. I was the orc standing in town square, with the crazed look in his eye, screaming doom because I was constantly bombarded with these images of rotten things happening to everybody who walked past. 

They would ignore me, and the dreadful things would happen, and I would feel awful for not stopping it, and I would try harder. 

They arrested me a few times, just put me in a cell with the drunks, assuming that I was a raving lunatic. Maybe I was, maybe I am. It's so hard to tell sometimes. 

|I kept doing it though, and I was so numb to the things I was actually saying, that one day I said it to someone powerful. A magistrate, I think. I barely remember. 

I told him to rush home, or he would never see his wife and daughter again, that they would be snatched from him. He scoffed at me, but of course I was right. They were taken by kidnappers and held ransom. 

He got them back and caught the men responsible, and then he asked them if I was involved with them. They, of course, tried to pin the whole thing on me. They rounded me up and put me on trial for kidnapping.

|Thankfully, I had enough of a reputation that it was fairly easy to convince them that I was just insane, and not actually dangerous. That magistrate though, he wasn't satisfied. 

He convinced the court that I was too much of a threat to be allowed to stay, and talked them into giving me a one-way trip to Lukatt. 

Sorta like everyone else, right?

|I've since decided that it's best to keep my flashes to myself. The more I ignore them, the smaller they get. Maybe it's just me looking into a place I'm not meant to look, after all. 

As for my flashes of you, I had a flash that there wouldn't be any soup left if you don't go now, so I came out to fire watch a little early. Go on, or you'll miss it. 

And thanks for listening. You've been good to me and I wanted you to know it's appreciated.
column2:
“你这会儿有空吗？我想跟你说句话。”

Vankan 坐下来，把苏格兰裙在膝上抚平。他漫不经心地抚着胡子，盯着摇曳的火光。

“我还没告诉过你，因为这往往会把人吓到，可我能看见一些东西。闪现的东西。你的闪现。见鬼，我就是因为这个才被送到这座岛上来的。

我第一次明白自己看见的是真的时候，觉得有义务帮人，试着警告他们我看见的那些闪现，只要我能，就让他们免于不幸带来的痛苦。而我能，所以我试了。

|起初我是个稀罕物。人们会来看这个长着第三只眼的兽人，听我一边从那些也许、可能的画面里翻拣，一边唠叨个没完。他们觉得我是个卖艺的，所以我甚至赚了些钱。这种事我不会拒绝。

后来吧，我猜有好多人开始明白我说的是真话，我的闪现是真的，他们就开始怕我。人们不再来找我，一下子我就谁也帮不上了。

你知道，让我放不下的是这个，不是钱。我是说，要是你有能力阻止，你能袖手旁观，让可怕的事发生在一个旁人身上吗？那岂不是难受得要命？

所以……我试了。

|我试得太用力，结果就成了那号人。我就是站在镇广场上的那个兽人，眼里带着疯相，尖叫着喊末日将至，因为每个走过的人身上将要发生的那些烂事，画面不停地砸到我身上。

他们不理我，可怕的事照样发生，我因为没能阻止而难受，于是试得更狠。

他们抓过我几次，不过是把我和醉鬼关在一间牢房里，当我是个胡言乱语的疯子。也许我当时是，也许我现在也是。有时候真的很难说。

|可我还是继续，而且我对自己实际说出口的话已经麻木了，直到有一天，我对一个有权势的人说了。一个地方法官，我想。我几乎记不清了。

我叫他赶紧回家，不然他就再也见不到妻子和女儿了，她们会被从他身边抢走。他朝我冷笑，可我当然是对的。她们被绑匪劫走，扣为人质勒索赎金。

他把她们救了回来，抓住了下手的人，然后问他们我是不是跟他们一伙。他们当然试图把整件事都推到我身上。他们把我抓起来，以绑架罪送上了法庭。

|幸好我的名声够大，很容易让他们相信我只是疯了，并不是真的危险。可那个地方法官并不满意。

他说服法庭，说我的威胁太大，不能允许我留下，又劝他们把我单程送到卢卡特。

跟其他人差不多，对吧？

|从那以后我认定，这些闪现最好自己藏着。我越不理它们，它们就越小。也许说到底，不过是我在看一个我不该看的地方。

至于我看见的你，我闪到一幕：你要是现在不去，汤就没了，所以我提前一点出来守夜。快去吧，不然你就赶不上了。

谢谢你听我说。你待我很好，我想让你知道，我很感激。”

column1: I love what we've done with this place. It's positively bustling! Well, compared to what it was like before we got here, I mean.
column2: 我喜欢我们把这儿弄成的样子。简直热闹极了！嗯，我是说，跟我们来之前比。

column1: Is this because of that incident with the soup? I apologized already, didn't I?
column2: 是因为汤那档子事吗？我已经道过歉了，不是吗？

column1: Looking for me? Well, here I am!
column2: 在找我吗？好啊，我在这儿！

column1: You don't have to go rubbing it in my face. I already said I was sorry.
column2: 你不必拿这个往我脸上揉。我已经说了对不起了。

column1: You really mean it, don't you? Fine then, I'll go, and I'll be taking my books with me!
column2: 你是来真的，对吧？那好，我走，我的书也带走！

column1: I knew this was going to be a trap. I just knew it.
column2: 我就知道这会是个圈套。我就是知道。

column1: Thanks again.
column2: 再次谢谢。

column1: We'll just pick up our stuff and be on our way. Thank you.
column2: 我们把东西捡起来就上路。谢谢你。

column1: No problem.
column2: 没问题。

column1: That is a very weird smell.
column2: 这味道怪得很。

column1: That's it, we're dead.
column2: 完了，我们死定了。

column1: We aren't gonna make it!
column2: 我们撑不过去了！

column1: This is great, I ain't been around this many people since forever! A few of 'em have given me funny looks because of... well you know why. Nobody's given me any real grief though, and that's something.  Anyway, was there something you needed, or you just come by to fraternize? I'm good either way.
column2: 太好了，我好久没跟这么多人待一块儿了！有几个人看我的眼神怪怪的，因为……唉，你知道为什么。不过没人真正找我麻烦，这就算不错。总之，你是有事找我，还是过来跟我热乎的？我都行。

column1: Good to see you.
column2: 见到你真好。

column1: Naw, I didn't think so. You'd miss me anyway.
column2: 才不，我就知道你不会。反正你会想我的。

column1: Dammit, you're strong.
column2: 该死，你可真强。

column1: Hey, screw you, I need that!
column2: 嘿，去你妈的，我需要那个！

column1: What a day this is turning out to be, eh? Guess we're partners now!
column2: 今儿这天可真够瞧的，是吧？看来咱们现在是搭档了！

column1: I really appreciate your help, and I appreciate your taking the time to have an earnest discussion with me. You're a good sort of person, the sort of person this island could use more of.
column2: 我真的很感激你的帮助，也感激你肯花时间跟我认真谈一谈。你是那种好人，这种人这座岛上该再多几个。

column1: Thanks again. I'm gonna double-check my supplies and my route before heading out.
column2: 再谢一次。出发前我再核对一遍补给和路线。

column1: Hmm. You know it's not a terrible idea. Based on what we talked about, you'd probably be a safer bet than the people I was going to look for anyhow.
column2: 嗯。你知道，这主意也不算太糟。就咱们谈过的那些来看，你大概总比我本来要去找的那些人更稳妥。

column1: Well it's a nice idea, but yeah, probably not good to change plans on something like that so suddenly. Take care.
column2: 嗯，主意是挺好，不过嘛，在这种事上这么突然改计划，大概不太好。保重。

column1:
When we got on that damn lift, I admit I did not see this coming. 

I was heading off to find a commune of other lycanthropes at a place called Hayill. 

I'd heard it was a halfway decent place to live, where nobody gives you flak for letting it hang out. 

And you know, maybe I'll still go there when all this is done, but for now I think I'm content to stay on. 

You got a way of bringing people together. You know it, and we all do too. 

Whatever you do, it's gonna be big, and I wanna be there to see it. 

|I... erm... well I made you something, last time I had a day off. 

It ain't worth much maybe, but I wanted to do something to say thank you. 

I put it in the stash, so take a look when you get a chance. 

And... thanks again.
column2:
咱们坐上那该死的升降机时，我承认，我可没料到会变成这样。

我当时正要去一个叫海伊尔的地方，找其他狼人族的公社。

我听说那儿还算能住人，没人会因为你把真身露出来而找你麻烦。

而且你知道，等这一切结束了，也许我还是会去那儿，可眼下我觉得留下来也挺满足。

你有办法把大家聚到一起。你知道这一点，我们也都知道。

不管你要干的是什么，都一定会是件大事，我想在场看着。

|我……呃……就是，上次我休息的时候，给你做了个东西。

也许不值钱，可我想做点什么，来跟你说声谢谢。

我把它放进储物里了，你有空就看一眼。

还有……再谢一次。

column1: I love living like this. Struggling for survival might be difficult, but it's.. "real", you know? There's nothing pretentious or complicated about it. Definitely something a guy could get used to.
column2: 我就爱这么过。为活下去而拼命也许不容易，可这……“真实”，你懂吧？没什么装腔作势，也不复杂。这绝对是男人能过惯的日子。

column1: Aww, don't say that to me now! Am I really that bad?
column2: 哎呀，这会儿别这么说！我真有那么糟吗？

column1: I see. I guess I should've known better than to get comfortable.
column2: 明白了。我早该知道，不该这么快就安下心来。

column1: See anything you want? You got the coin, and it's all yours.
column2: 有看中的吗？你有钱，看上的就归你。

column1: Got some stuff for sale here!
column2: 这儿有东西卖！

column1: Alright then. See you next time, if there is a next time.
column2: 那好吧。下次见，要是还有下次的话。

column1: Line up for the reaping!
column2: 排好队，等着被收割！

column1: You fools know not who you oppose.
column2: 你们这些蠢货，不知自己对抗的是何人。

column1: There, Master.
column2: 在那儿，主人。

column1: I see something.
column2: 我看到东西了。

column1: Impressive.
column2: 了不起。

column1: That may be a setback.
column2: 这或许是个挫折。

column1: I see nothing.
column2: 我什么也没看见。

column1: Nothing of note.
column2: 没什么值得注意的。

column1: Formidable indeed. Most interesting.
column2: 确实可畏。有意思极了。

column1: Destroy me if you can!
column2: 有本事就毁灭我！

column1: The master is not yet finished with you.
column2: 主人还没有跟你了结。

column1: You do not have permission to die.
column2: 你没有死去的许可。

column1: You are a coward and a fool.
column2: 你是个懦夫，也是个蠢货。

column1: Spare me your sniveling.
column2: 别跟我哭哭啼啼。

column1: We do not need that one, Master.
column2: 我们不需要那一个，主人。

column1: Worthless pawn.
column2: 一文不值的棋子。

column1: I am here to serve in any capacity you require of me. I will be your bodyguard and your advisor at the bare minimum. I will also defend any... fodder you acquire along the way. Your possessions and your pawns are also my charge. The contract you have forged will be honoured.
column2: 我在此以你所要求的任何身份侍奉。最低限度，我会做你的保镖和顾问。我也会保护你沿途收来的任何……炮灰。你的财物和你的棋子，同样由我看管。你所缔结的契约将被信守。

column1: Though you are free to release me from the contract, you do understand that releasing me will not negate your obligation.
column2: 你虽可把我从契约中释放，但你应当明白，释放我并不会取消你的义务。

column1: Yes, Master?
column2: 是，主人？

column1: I thought not. Why throw away a lifetime of service when you have already paid for the privelege?
column2: 我料到你不会。既已为这份特权付过代价，何必扔掉一生的侍奉？

column1: Then you are more the fool. I will, as they say, see you in hell, Maledicus.
column2: 那你便更是个蠢货。那么，如他们所说，地狱里见，咒师。

column1:
You are making excellent progress, Master.

Whatever seed you sow upon this island, the weight of your actions shall undoubtedly be felt for ages yet to come."

Zantanak sits down and gazes into the fire. His face seems, for a moment, almost human.

"It has been long since I planted my feet upon the soil of the mortal world. I had forgotten how... intoxicating it can be. 

Perhaps I've more acquired a taste for it over the centuries. 

|The strangest thing I find is that I am mimicking human mannerisms more often. 

I heard the others talking about me, as they often do. They oft whisper their fear of me to one another, but this time, they were laughing, saying that I was finally learning how to blend in. 

Perhaps they were right. 

In any case, it will be easier to command an army of fools who feel more at ease than ones who feel less so. 

I encouraged it, and will continue to do so."

|Zantanak wrinkles his nose and stands up. 

"I am even imitating the troublesome human tendancy to run my mouth for no useful reason, it seems.

The real reason I came to see you was to inform you that I have been granted additional power to serve you.

I have bound it within a fetish and left it among your possessions.
column2:
你的进展极为出色，主人。

无论你在这座岛上播下何种种子，你所作所为的分量，无疑都将在此后漫长的岁月里被感受到。”

Zantanak 坐下，凝视着火。有那么一瞬，他的脸几乎像是人类。

“我已经很久没有把脚踩上凡人世界的土地了。我忘了这可以多么……令人沉醉。

也许几个世纪下来，我倒是越发品出了其中的滋味。

|我发现最奇怪的是，我越来越常在模仿人类的举止。

我听见别人议论我，他们经常如此。他们时常彼此低声诉说对我的恐惧，可这一次，他们在笑，说我终于在学着怎么融入。

也许他们说得对。

不管怎样，指挥一群更觉得自在的蠢货，总比指挥一群觉得不那么自在的要容易。

我鼓励了这件事，并且会继续这么做。”

|Zantanak 皱了皱鼻子，站起身来。

“看来我甚至在模仿人类那种毫无用处也要喋喋不休的讨厌毛病。

我来见你的真正原因，是告知你：我已被授予额外的力量来侍奉你。

我已将它封入一件咒物，留在你的财物之中。

column1: This place is not properly suitable as a base of operations, but there is precious little to choose from here. I would recommend that we find someplace imposing, a veritable fortress from which we may strike terror into the hearts of your foes. If it is your pleasure, of course.
column2: 这地方并不真正适合作为行动基地，可这里实在没什么可选的。我建议我们寻一处气势逼人的所在，一座名副其实的要塞，好从那里把恐惧打进你敌人的心里。当然，若你愿意。

column1: If you terminate my contract now, your end must still be upheld. You understand this?
column2: 若你现在终止我的契约，你这一方仍须履行。这一点你明白吗？

column1: Whatever you need, Master.
column2: 无论你需要什么，主人。

column1: You had best take full advantage of my service while it is still available to you.
column2: 你最好趁我的侍奉还用得上，把它用足。

column1: Then farewell, Maledicus. I will see you again, far sooner than you may like.
column2: 那么别了，咒师。我会再见到你，而且远比你乐意的要快。

column1: ...well, despite his recklessness, he is a dear friend of mine. We were pastors in a village church, back home.\nI fear for his safety, though. He has lost his way in recent months.
column2: ……嗯，尽管他行事鲁莽，他仍是我的好友。我们从前在家乡的一座乡村教堂里一起当牧师。\n不过我担心他的安危。近几个月来，他迷失了方向。
