column1: Well, get your ass gone then, and don't even think of starting trouble. You'd be surprised how ferociously these giants will defend folks to know how to share.
column2: 那你就滚蛋，想都别想惹事。这些巨人护起懂得分享的人来有多凶，你绝对想不到。

column1: Well, that was interesting. Does that make me officially a whore now too? Add it to the list, I guess.
column2: 嗯，挺有意思。这算不算我也正式成了婊子？再加上一条吧，我想。

column1: What am I gonna do if he's the
column2: 要是他就是那个，我该怎么办

column1: What the hell is taking him so long anyway? I hate it when my clients are late.
column2: 他到底他妈的磨蹭什么？我讨厌客人迟到。

column1: What you want to hire me? Long-term? You'll have to pay me better than that tight-ass Madame, not that it would be very difficult. I want 1000$ for the first week. We can talk more after that. Deal?
column2: 什么，你想雇我？长期的？你得给得比那个抠门鸨母多，不过这也不是什么难事。第一周我要1000$。之后再谈。成交？

column1: Who am I booked with? Oh, I'm booked with Rugal again. I asked for him this time. He was fantastic!
column2: 我约的是谁？哦，又约了 Rugal。这次是我点的他。他太棒了！

column1: Why don't you strip off, and we'll see if I can give you your money's worth
column2: 你把衣服脱了，咱们看看我能不能让你这钱花得值。

column1: Wow, I bet this place has tits for days! We have some time to kill, don't we? A few hours?
column2: 哇，我打赌这地方的奶子够看好几天！咱们有的是时间可消，对吧？几个小时？

column1: Yeah, just like that. You're very good at this game.
column2: 对，就是这样。你这游戏玩得真好。

column1: Yeah, that's right, you big boy! Put both your hands on it and play with it.
column2: 对，就是这样，你这大男孩！两只手都放上去，玩它。

column1: Yep.
column2: 就是。

column1: Yes, just relax. Close your eyes, and just let me do everything.
column2: 是的，放松就好。闭上眼睛，什么都交给我。

column1: Yo, nice to see you. You ain't my client, are you? Well, come on in anyway, and keep your voice down if you please.
column2: 哟，见到你真好。你不是我的客人吧？嗯，反正进来吧，请把声音放轻。

column1: You can't be seriously thinking of patronizing this demeaning hogsty? Just using these women for your momentary pleasure?
column2: 你不会真想光顾这个有辱人格的猪圈吧？就为了一时快活，利用这些女人？

column1: You know, they pay the giants in sex? They tried to pay me that way too, as if it's something I could eat. I demanded food and money, and they got all pissy with me.
column2: 你知道吗，他们用性爱给那些巨人付酬？他们也想这么付我，好像那是我能吃的东西似的。我要了食物和钱，他们就对我一肚子火。

column1: You like rope? I know a thing or two about that, you know. Used to work as a sailor between jobs.
column2: 你喜欢绳子？这东西我还懂两下，知道吧。以前干活的空当当过水手。

column1: You like that, don't you?
column2: 你喜欢这样，对吧？

column1: You might want to watch yourself. Places like these, it's rare that there ain't someone with blood on his breath. I'd know.
column2: 你最好小心点。这种地方，嘴里带着血腥气的人少不了。我清楚。

column1: You will not be disappointed. Close the door and lay down.
column2: 你不会失望的。关上门，躺下。

column1: You've come to the right woman. Come in, sit down. Relax.
column2: 你找对女人了。进来，坐下。放松。

column1: You've need of a diversion, Master? Well, by all means. I will stand guard and ensure your chosen whore does not attempt to harm you.
column2: 你需要消遣吗，主人？那好，但凭你吩咐。我会站岗，确保你选中的婊子不会试图伤害你。

column1: with the Ettins in order to get them to stand guard like that. Which unlucky girl do you think gets that job?
column2: 和那些双头巨人，好让他们那样站岗。你觉得哪个倒霉的姑娘会摊上这差事？

column1: Back home, Evans had taken quite an interest in dark magic. This is hardly abnormal, as priests are often called upon to combat such magicks, but I believe he became infatuated with his studies, and began to dabble in the practice of the very arts he was trained to oppose.
column2: 在家乡，Evans 对黑暗魔法产生了相当浓的兴趣。这算不上反常，因为牧师常常被召去对抗这类魔法，可我相信他迷恋上了自己的研究，开始亲手涉猎他受训去反对的那些技艺。

column1: Curse my foolishness. If only I hadn't lost my emblem, I'm sure I'd be able to unravel this sorcery.
column2: 都怪我这份愚蠢。要是我没弄丢徽记，我肯定能破解这道巫术。

column1: Evans seemed unshaken by these events. When we arrived on Lukatt, his activities became bolder, less restricted. We found an abandoned building for shelter, and we hadn't much choice but to stay there.
column2: 这些事似乎没能撼动 Evans。我们抵达卢卡特之后，他的行动变得更大胆，也更不受约束。我们找了一栋废弃的建筑容身，除此之外也没有多少选择，只能留在那儿。

column1: He lost his way, somewhere down the line... but he was a good man. I should have done more to help him back on the right path. These past few months could have gone entirely differently.
column2: 他在后来的某一段路上迷失了……可他是个好人。我本该再多做些，帮他回到正路。过去这几个月，本来可以完全不一样。

column1: He... he wasn't?
column2: 他……他不在？

column1: Here, I want you to have this. It used to belong to him, but it might prove useful to you. Please take it as a token of my thanks. And please, keep my emblem. I don't have any more use for it.
column2: 来，这个给你。它原来是他的，可也许对你有用。请收下，权当我的谢意。还有，请留着我的徽记。我已经用不上它了。

column1: His emblem feels strange to me, so I dared not use it, but now that you've brought mine, I can dispel the barrier around this wall. Please stand back.
column2: 他的徽记给我一种怪异的感觉，所以我不敢用。可现在你把我的带来了，我可以驱散围着这堵墙的屏障。请退后。

column1: I am pastor Nikolai. Although, the 'pastor' part doesn't hold much meaning now.
column2: 我是牧师 Nikolai。不过，“牧师”这个身份现在已经没什么意义了。

column1: I beg of you, please, tell me what you saw.
column2: 我恳求你，请告诉我你看见了什么。

column1: I found Evans' emblem and his robes here. He is inside, of that I am certain.
column2: 我在这儿找到了 Evans 的徽记和他的长袍。他在里面，这一点我可以肯定。

column1: I know that I have no business asking this of you, but please... take my emblem, and find Evans.
column2: 我知道我没有立场求你这件事，可是……请带上我的徽记，去找 Evans。

column1: I must bid you farewll for now. but I hope that we get to meet again.
column2: 此刻我必须向你道别。不过希望我们还能再见。

column1: I see... I am unsure whether to be relieved or not.\nPlease forgive me, I was mistaken.
column2: 我明白了……我不确定该不该感到宽慰。\n请原谅我，是我弄错了。

column1: I'm not sure what to do from here. Perhaps I ought to find somewhere to sleep, and allow recent events to settle in my mind.
column2: 我不知道从这儿该怎么办。也许我该找个地方睡觉，让近来这些事在心里慢慢沉淀。

column1: I've been looking for my associate, Evans, for the past few weeks, and I believe I've managed to track him down. I am most certain that he has been taken inside this strange building.
column2: 过去几周我一直在找我的同僚 Evans，我相信我已经循着踪迹找到他了。我非常确定，他被带进了这栋奇怪的建筑里。

column1: If I had any strength remaining, I would aid you without question. I am no use to you in my current state.
column2: 我要是还剩一点力气，一定会毫不犹豫帮你。以我现在的状态，我对你毫无用处。

column1: It became far too dangerous to stay in that place, and I couldn't bring myself to harm Evans. I felt safer with the idea of taking my chances elsewhere... I wrote Evans a parting letter, and left him to his own devices.
column2: 继续留在那个地方变得太危险了，而我又下不了手伤害 Evans。我觉得去别处碰碰运气更安全……我给 Evans 写了一封告别信，就任他去了。

column1: It seems I've much searching yet to do. Forgive me, I have troubled you enough. Goodbye...
column2: 看来我要找的还多着呢。原谅我，已经太打扰你了。再见……

column1: Months passed, and Evans eventually began to open portals into dark places, inviting tiny devils to come through. Tiny though they were, it took all of my strength, and that of the other pastors, to banish them.
column2: 几个月过去了，Evans 终于开始打开通往黑暗之地的门户，邀请小恶魔穿过来。它们尽管微小，驱逐它们却耗尽了我和其他牧师全部的力气。

column1: My only regret in all of this is that I disappointed you.
column2: 在这一切之中，我唯一的遗憾，就是让你失望了。

column1: Nikolai! My brother. I sensed the power of your emblem.\nI hoped that you would find this place!
column2: Nikolai！我的兄弟。我感应到了你徽记的力量。\n我一直希望你会找到这个地方！

column1: No. No...
column2: 不。不……

column1: Oh! You startled me. I was so engrossed in studying this wall, I didn't hear you step up.
column2: 哦！你吓了我一跳。我研究这堵墙太入神，没听见你走过来。

column1: Oh...
Once you see the beauty of this side, however, I am certain you will understand. The florid chaos! Remarkable!
column2: 不过，一旦你看见这一侧的美，我肯定你会明白。那繁丽的混沌！真是非凡！

column1: Originally, we wanted to turn that abandoned building into a sanctuary for anyone who was struggling with life on the island, but we couldn't even make a start.
column2: 起初，我们想把那栋废弃的建筑变成一座庇护所，收留任何在岛上艰难度日的人，可我们连开头都没能做成。

column1: Please tell me, was Evans down there?
column2: 请告诉我，Evans 在下面吗？

column1: Thank you. I'm surprised you didn't sell it, but perhaps that's just me being cynical. We met a while ago near that old, run-down cottage, didn't we? I should have introduced myself then.
column2: 谢谢你。你没把它卖掉，我有些意外，不过也许只是我把人想得太坏。我们前些时候在那栋破旧的小屋附近见过，对吧？我那时就该自我介绍的。

column1: The other pastors and I did all we could to keep his gaze turned toward the light, but it was of little use. One of our congregation somehow learned of his dabblings, and all eight of our parish were put on trial for Malediction.
column2: 我和别的牧师竭尽全力，想让他的目光转向光明，可几乎没有用。我们会众里不知怎么有人得知了他的涉猎，于是我们教区的八个人全被送上法庭，罪名是诅咒。

column1: The seductive power of the dark arts must be greater even than I imagined. How could such a kind and virtuous man become so corrupted? I have no answers.
column2: 黑暗技艺的诱惑之力，一定比我想象的还要大。如此善良正直的人，怎么会堕落成这样？我没有答案。

column1: There is a magic circle etched onto its surface, and it's an exact match for the ones that Evans liked to draw in his journal. I noticed the same magic circle painted on the floor in that old cottage.
column2: 它的表面上刻着一个魔法阵，跟 Evans 喜欢画在日记里的那些分毫不差。我注意到那栋旧小屋的地板上也画着同样的魔法阵。

column1: There is something suspicious about this wall, don't you think?\nI would like to get inside and investigate, but I can't dispel the magic force protecting it.
column2: 这堵墙有些可疑，你不觉得吗？\n我想进去调查，可我驱散不了保护它的那股魔力。

column1: This wall...
column2: 这堵墙……

column1: Urgh... I did not expect such a violent reaction.\nI have... well overstrained myself.
column2: 呃……我没料到反应会这么剧烈。\n我……实在是用力过了头。

column1: Wait, that's...
column2: 等等，那是……

column1: Was that a cowardly thing to do? Perhaps. I am no killer though, and he was my friend. I thought perhaps I could find a way to put some sense into him, if I only had enough distance to collect my thoughts.
column2: 那样做是懦弱吗？也许是。不过我不是杀手，而且他是我的朋友。我想，只要离得够远，能让我理清思绪，也许就能找到办法让他恢复理智。

column1: We have been apart for too long. Come to me, my dear brother!
column2: 我们分开得太久了。到我这儿来，我亲爱的兄弟！

column1: What else must lie down there...
column2: 下面究竟还有什么……

column1: When I eventually returned, I found that everyone had taken their belongings and left. I kept wondering whether Evans had managed to turn himself around, and if the others were safe. I've been looking for any signs of them since. And so, that brings me to where I am now.
column2: 等我终于回去，发现所有人都收拾了东西离开了。我一直在想，Evans 有没有迷途知返，其他人是否安全。从那以后我就在寻找他们的任何踪迹。于是，这就到了我现在所在的地方。

column1: You have my sincere gratitude for granting Evans his final rest. There was nothing more to be done, and the Evans I knew would have wanted it this way.
column2: 你让 Evans 得到了最后的安息，我由衷感激。已经没有别的办法了，我认识的那个 Evans 也会希望如此。

column1: You've returned!
column2: 你回来了！

column1: ... No? Well, maybe some other time. The offer shall remain open should you find yourself stuck here for too much longer.
column2: ……不？那好吧，也许换个时候。要是你在这儿困得太久，这个提议依然作数。

column1: Browse at your leisure, only keep the noise down, and don't carry lit torches near the books, please and thank you.
column2: 请随意翻阅，只是把声音放轻，也别拿着点燃的火把靠近书，拜托了，谢谢。

column1: Fine, you can have the key. One didn't want it anyway.
column2: 行，钥匙给你。反正本人也不想要。

column1: Greetings! I am in your debt for removing that dreadful apparition from my lecture hall.
column2: 你好！你把那可怕的幻影从我的讲堂里除掉了，我欠你一份人情。

column1: I got in trouble for yelling a profanity at the librarian. It was worth it.
column2: 我因为对图书管理员吼了句脏话，惹上了麻烦。值了。

column1: I say! Stop making obscene gestures towards me at once!
column2: 我说！立刻停止对我做下流手势！

column1: I say, what was that ruckus just now? One is trying to read about the Great Turnip Shortage, you know.
column2: 我说，刚才那阵喧闹是怎么回事？本人正在读大芜菁短缺的事，知道吗。

column1: Oh, do you need to get into the supply closet?
column2: 哦，你要进储藏间吗？

column1: So! Have you have come to listen to my lectures? I cover an extensive range of subjects.
column2: 那么！你是来听我讲课的吗？我讲授的科目范围很广。

column1: That Bogeyman has been rearranging our books and being a general nuisance for a long time, now. Thank you for getting rid of it.
column2: 那只夜魔好长时间一直在重新摆我们的书，总体上就是个麻烦。谢谢你把它除掉。

column1: The professor usually keeps the key on his desk. However, since monsters started appearing, he's given it to one of the senior students for safe keeping.
column2: 教授通常把钥匙放在书桌上。不过，自从怪物开始出现，他就把它交给一名高年级学生保管了。

column1: The seniors are usually in the private study area, behind the library reception desk.
column2: 高年级学生通常在图书馆接待台后面的私人自修区。

column1: The supply closet key? Yes, one has it right here, but why should one give it to you?
column2: 储藏间的钥匙？是的，本人这儿就有，可本人凭什么给你？

column1: There have been many of its ilk lurking around here as of late, and I am stumped as to how they manage to get in. This place is meant to be a peaceful safe haven, protected from the outside world.
column2: 近来有不少同类在这附近潜伏，我实在想不通它们是怎么进来的。这地方本该是一处安宁的避风港，与外界隔绝。

column1: Today's lecture is an introduction to stenography!
column2: 今天的讲座是速记入门！

column1: You're new here, correct? You should talk to the professor--he's in the lecture hall just up ahead. He'll help you get settled in.
column2: 你是新来的，对吧？你该去跟教授谈谈——他就在前面不远的讲堂里。他会帮你安顿下来。

column1: Blast
column2: 施法

column1: Dodge
column2: 闪避

column2: 格斗

column2: 守护

column2: 狩猎

column1: The exit is that way. I hope you're up to it.
column2: 出口在那边。希望你应付得了。

column1: Ward
column2: 护佑

column1: You can press and hold F1 to get extra information on most screens. Give it a try here, and again after you leave.
column2: 在大多数界面上，你可以按住 F1 查看额外信息。在这里试一次，离开后再试一次。

column1: , it says. He is... a living part of the island, who allows life or death, prosperity or suffering, only at his whim. That's rather bleak, isn't it?
column2: ，书上是这么说的。他是……这座岛活着的一部分，生或死、繁荣或苦难，全凭他一念。这可真够阴郁的，不是吗？

column1: A few spells, handwritten by a mage, it seems. It might be part of a larger volume, but it should be useful on its own.
column2: 几道法术，看来是一位法师手写的。它也许是更大一卷里的一部分，但单独拿来也应该有用。

column1: Ah yes, here we are. Most of it is lost, but I've managed to pick out enough to get a vague idea.
column2: 啊，对，就是这儿。大部分都佚失了，但我辨认出的已经够形成一个模糊的概念。

column1: Aside from that, if you'd like me to look at anything unusual, I'd love a chance to give it a once over.
column2: 除此之外，要是你想让我看看什么不寻常的东西，我很乐意有机会过目一遍。

column1: Forget
column2: 忘掉

column1:
Gloried one in Sunken Sea,
 Lord Leviathan is he.
Hear our Voices, Dry Above
Echo Through the Brine our Love.
column2:
荣耀者在沉没之海，
 主 Leviathan 即是他。
听我们的声音，干燥的上方，
回响穿过卤水，我们的爱。

column1: Halex ends up being neither Lux nor Pox, but something more like Arcus, the most basic magic used by trainees. It is, however, a violent spell, causing a large, damaging explosion on its target.
column2: Halex 到头来既不是 Lux，也不是 Pox，而更接近 Arcus，也就是学徒使用的最基础的魔法。不过，它是个暴烈的法术，会在目标身上造成一场伤害巨大的爆炸。

column1: I am trying to discover if there is an original, core version. Call it a pet project if you will.
column2: 我正在查明是否存在一个最初的核心版本。你愿意的话，不妨称之为我的私人小项目。

column1: I can feel the power in this book without even reading it! Though, that's strange. All the pages are there, but it still seems incomplete. I wonder what's missing.
column2: 我甚至不用读，就能感觉到这本书里的力量！不过这就怪了。书页都在，可它还是显得不完整。不知缺的是什么。

column1: I have never seen someone who dared put words such as these to print.
column2: 我从没见过有人敢把这样的语句付印。

column1: I've also noticed that all of the copies I've found are slightly different, almost as though every printer made unique changes.
column2: 我也注意到，我找到的每一本都略有出入，几乎像是每个印刷工都做了各自的改动。

column1: I've several books that make reference to this one, but never imagined that I would actually see it. I'm almost disappointed. I expected something... grander, perhaps.
column2: 我有好几本书提到过这一本，却从没想过真能见到。我几乎有些失望。我以为会……更宏伟些，也许。

column1: If there really is some connection between Leviathan and the monarchy of Lukatt, you may find more information somewhere inside the caldera.
column2: 如果 Leviathan 和卢卡特的王室之间真有关联，你也许能在破火山口里面的某处找到更多信息。

column1: If you are skilled enough to know the secrets of Arximum, you can expand the explosion of Halex even further. Fearsome indeed.
column2: 你要是本事够，懂得 Arximum 的秘密，就能把 Halex 的爆炸扩得更大。着实可怖。

column1: If you change your mind, I would still like to buy it, but we'll negotiate a more reasonable price.
column2: 你要是改了主意，我还是想买，不过咱们会谈一个更合理的价钱。

column1: If you come across any copies of the Sumptuous Garden, bring them to me and I will give you a good price for them.
column2: 你若遇见《奢华花园》的任何副本，带给我，我会出个好价。

column1: If you ever run into large hordes of zombies or skeletons, Solaris will make short work of them, exploding one and catching many others in the blast.
column2: 如果你遇上大群的僵尸或骷髅，Solaris 能迅速解决他们，引爆其中一个，再让爆炸波及另外许多。

column1: It appears to be a series of prayers and rituals devoted to a being called Leviathan. What's more, it appears that these rituals and prayers are reserved only for royalty. Curious.
column2: 这似乎是一系列献给名为 Leviathan 的存在的祈祷与仪式。而且，这些仪式和祈祷看来只保留给王室。耐人寻味。

column1: It is very badly damaged, but with any luck, a bit of catalyst will bring the ink residue out enough for us to read it. I'm sure I have some around here somewhere. Give me a moment.
column2: 它损坏得非常厉害，不过运气好的话，一点催化剂就能让残留墨迹显出足够我们阅读的程度。我肯定附近什么地方有一些。稍等我一下。

column1: It's a bit hard to make out most of this. Seems to be excerpts from a spellbook. It might be more useful if you could find more of them and compile them.
column2: 这上面大半都难以辨认。似乎是一本法术书的摘录。你要是能找到更多，并把它们汇编起来，也许更有用。

column1: It's a... pillow book, I guess you'd say. Very common, I've noticed.
column2: 这是……一本春宫书，我想你会这么叫它。很常见，我注意到了。

column1: It's exceedingly common, I've noticed.
column2: 极其常见，我注意到了。

column1: Lux is the magic of light, and of the thundering heavens. You could use this to gift your allies with heavenly grace, or daze your enemies. Demons and undead fear it, as I understand.
column2: Lux 是光的魔法，也是雷鸣天界的魔法。你可以用它把天界的优雅赐予盟友，或使敌人眩晕。据我所知，恶魔和亡灵都惧怕它。

column1: Max is the magic of chaos and destruction. With this your allies' attacks will throw enemies off-balance, or you could inflict pain that limits the effectiveness of healing. Shapeshifters and innocents are especially vulnerable.
column2: Max 是混乱与毁灭的魔法。有了它，盟友的攻击会让敌人失去平衡，你也可以施加剧痛，限制治疗的效果。变形者和无辜者尤其脆弱。

column1: Nix is the magic of eldritch mystery and transformation. With this book, you could improve your allies' spells, or pin your enemies beneath a magic nexus. Works especially well against demons and animals, I'm told.
column2: Nix 是诡秘与变化的魔法。有了这本书，你可以强化盟友的法术，或用一道魔法连结把敌人钉在下面。听说对恶魔和动物尤其有效。

column1: No matter. Halex was... an experiment of sorts. An attempt to weave Lux and Pox together in a harmonious way. Whether or not the experiment was a success is perhaps up for some debate.
column2: 无妨。Halex 曾是……某种实验。一次把 Lux 和 Pox 和谐地编织在一起的尝试。实验算不算成功，也许还说不准。

column1: No... no you're right. What was I thinking? That's an absurd price for any book. Thank you.
column2: 不……不，你说得对。我刚才是怎么想的？任何书出这个价都荒唐。谢谢你。

column1: Oh hello again. Have you found any books for me?
column2: 哦，又见面了。你找到什么书给我了吗？

column1: Oh, goodness. Where did you find this? The spells on these pages feel almost as though they are trying to cast themselves, like they need only the slightest push.
column2: 哦，天哪。你是在哪儿找到这个的？这些书页上的法术几乎像是要自己施放，仿佛只需轻轻一推。

column1: Oh, magnificent! I'll warrant that this is more than you'd get from any other vendor! Thank you again!
column2: 哦，妙极了！我敢说，这比你在任何别的商贩那儿能拿到的都多！再次谢谢你！

column1: Pox is the magic of death and pestilence. It can cloak your allies in oily shadows, making them hard to see, or infect your enemies with withering poison. Animals and innocents particularly fear it.
column2: Pox 是死亡与瘟疫的魔法。它能用油腻的暗影笼罩你的盟友，让他们难以被看见，或用枯萎的毒素感染你的敌人。动物和无辜者尤其惧怕它。

column1: Rex is the magic of life and wild, animal power. You can use this to improve your allies' physical attacks, or to impede your enemies' movements. Effective against undead and shapeshifters especially.
column2: Rex 是生命与狂野兽力的魔法。你可以用它强化盟友的物理攻击，或阻碍敌人的行动。对亡灵和变形者尤其有效。

column1: Solaris harnesses the power of the sun. To most creatures, this simply means violent flames, but with undead creatures such as zombies or vampires, the results are especially violent.
column2: Solaris 驾驭太阳的力量。对大多数生物来说，这不过是暴烈的火焰，但对僵尸或吸血鬼这样的亡灵，结果尤其暴烈。

column1: Something you may find interesting is that, unlike other large-area magic, Halex does not cause lesser damage to those further from the blast point. If you target the most magic-vulnerable enemy in a group, its magic-resistant fellows will be injured just as badly.
column2: 有一点你也许会感兴趣：和其他大范围魔法不同，Halex 并不会让离爆炸点更远的目标受到更轻的伤害。如果你瞄准一群敌人里最不耐魔法的那个，它那些抗魔的同伴也会伤得一样重。

column1: Surely it would be illegal in many places for me to buy this book. I could, however, give you a gift of 12000$ if you just forget it on the table here.
column2: 我要买下这本书，在许多地方肯定是违法的。不过，只要你把它忘在这儿的桌子上，我可以赠你 12000$。

column1: The rest of the book, I'm afraid, is well-ruined, but disturbing as that was, I'm glad to have had the opportunity to see it. Let me give you a little something for the privilege.
column2: 这本书余下的部分，恐怕是彻底毁了。尽管刚才那样令人不安，我还是很高兴有机会见到它。容我为这份荣幸给你一点小意思。

column1: The royal castle, or some other place where the royal family might have spent time would be your best bet.
column2: 王城，或是王室可能逗留过的其他地方，会是你最好的选择。

column1: The verses in this book are dark indeed, insane prayers to alien gods. There's also a name - Fastad. If I recall he was once a minister in the old government. This would be a fairly scandalous find if that government were still in operation.
column2: 这本书里的诗句着实阴暗，是献给异界诸神的疯狂祈祷。还有一个名字——Fastad。如果我记得没错，他曾是旧政府的一位大臣。假如那个政府还在，这个发现足以成为一桩丑闻。

column1: There are bandits and worse swarming the ruins of the noble manors and the slums of the capital, but if you're lucky, you might find something they overlooked. After all, bandits care more for gold than for print.
column2: 贵族庄园的废墟和首都的贫民窟里挤满了强盗，还有更糟的东西，但你要是走运，也许能找到他们看漏的东西。毕竟，强盗在乎金子，远胜过在乎印刷品。

column1: This Leviathan is the
column2: 这个 Leviathan 就是

column1: This author! This is the one who wrote The Sumptuous Garden! I'd recognize this writing style anywhere. Something is different, though. Sumptuous Garden seems positively prudish compared to the depravity described here!
column2: 这个作者！写《奢华花园》的就是这个人！这种文风我到哪儿都认得。不过有点不一样。比起这儿描写的荒淫，《奢华花园》简直显得正经得拘谨！

column1: This is interesting. I can't say I understand all of this, but there are clearly some glimpses of mad genius here. A few holes still, but if you can close them, you'll have an object of real power.
column2: 这很有意思。我不敢说自己全懂了，但这里分明能窥见几分疯狂的天才。还有几处缺口，你若能补上，便会得到一件真正有力量的东西。

column1: Welcome, welcome! You don't look like the sort to spend a lot of money on books, so I'll ask straight away. Have you ever seen a copy of a book called 'Sumptuous Garden'?
column2: 欢迎，欢迎！你看着不像是会花大钱买书的人，所以我就开门见山。你见过一本叫《奢华花园》的书吗？

column1: Wha... where on earth did you find such a thing? Remarkable! It must be centuries old.
column2: 什……你到底是在哪儿找到这种东西的？了不起！它一定有好几百年了。

column1: What on earth is this? The Commanding Oak? Let's have a look then.
column2: 这到底是什么？《号令橡木》？那咱们看看。

column1: Yes, I would still very much like to buy the book if you are willing to part with it. My offer is 4000$.
column2: 是的，你若愿意割爱，我仍然非常想买下这本书。我出 4000$。

column1: Another way, ye will not find. The forest covers its secrets in shame.
column2: 另一条路，你们是找不到的。森林羞耻地掩盖着它的秘密。

column1: Furthermore, the supplies we're supposed to be getting in haven't showed up. How am I supposed to mix potions without reagents?
column2: 另外，我们本该收到的补给还没到。没有试剂，我怎么调配药水？

column1: Go and witness the horror! It shall be engraved upon your very soul!
column2: 去见证那恐怖吧！它将铭刻在你的灵魂上！

column1: I euthanized four patients today. Even if we come up with a viable treatment for the plague tomorrow, some of these people are already too far gone to survive. We are running out of places to put the bodies.
column2: 我今天对四名病人实施了安乐死。就算明天就能做出可行的瘟疫疗法，这些人里有的也已经没救了。我们快没地方放尸体了。

column1: I hope that the researchers at the capital are having better luck than we are. By now, all of the doctors are infected as well, myself included, and at the rate things are progressing, we will all be dead before finding a cure. I must have faith that Her Majesty will find a way to save us.
column2: 我希望首都的研究者比我们运气更好。如今所有医生也都感染了，包括我自己。照这个速度，我们会在找到治愈之法以前全部死去。我必须相信，女王陛下会找到拯救我们的办法。

column1: I may be able to fashion regenerative talismans as a stopgap, but we do not have the resources to create enough for all of the victims. I believe these would best be used to preserve the lives of myself and the other researchers, in the interest of continuing our work to find a cure.
column2: 我也许能制作再生护符应急，但我们没有资源给所有受害者都做够。我认为这些最好用来保住我和其余研究者的命，以便继续寻找治愈之法。

column1: I yet linger in order to remember, for if I forget, the mem'ry be lost. Heed me, travelers! If wish ye a way through the wood, witness my suff'ring! Remember in my stead, that I might sleep. Do this, and I will show you the way through.
column2: 我还留在这里，是为了记住。我若忘了，记忆便不复存在。听我说，旅人们！你们若想有一条穿过林子的路，就见证我的苦难！替我记住，好让我能够安息。如此，我便指给你们穿过去的路。

column1: Magical treatment appears to be effective in the earliest stages of infection, before damage has been done to the body, but once ulcers have appeared, the spells do little but slow it down.
column2: 魔法治疗在感染最初阶段、身体尚未受损时似乎有效，可一旦出现溃疡，法术除了延缓病程，就几乎没用了。

column1: Make sure that you check the refugees. If any of them got ahold of a key, we could have a break in quarantine, and I don't need to tell you how bad that would be.
column2: 务必去检查那些难民。他们要是有人弄到了钥匙，隔离就可能被突破，那会有多糟，不用我告诉你。

column1: Medicinal treatment is not making progress. I thought the previous treatment was more effective at halting symptoms, but overall survivability was not improved. I will try a new mixture tomorrow, but I am running out of ideas.
column2: 药物疗法没有进展。我原以为之前的疗法更能遏止症状，但总的存活率并没有提高。明天我会试一种新的配方，可我快没主意了。

column1: Quarantine Zone
column2: 隔离区

column1: Six subjects undergoing experimentation all died. Purging magic seemed effective in the short term, but symptoms reappeared within a few hours. Will gather more volunteers tomorrow.
column2: 六名实验对象全部死亡。净化魔法在短期内似乎有效，但几个小时后症状又出现了。明天再召集更多志愿者。

column1: The forest grows tight 'round this place, choking the pain, choking the mem'ry of what transpired.
column2: 森林在这地方四周越长越紧，扼住痛苦，扼住曾经发生之事的记忆。

column1: Hey! Keep it down in there! I'm trying to organize some paperwork and you're making it really hard to concentrate!
column2: 嘿！里面小声点！我在整理文书，你们让我根本没法集中精神！

column1: Hmm... confiscate it, and throw them in the dungeon.\nI'll decide what to with them later.
column2: 嗯……没收，把他们扔进地牢。\n我以后再决定怎么处置他们。

column1: Now, if you want to keep yourself in one piece, stay where you are with your arms up. You are severely outnumbered.
column2: 现在，你要想留个全尸，就原地待着，双手举起。你们寡不敌众。

column1: Oh heck... well, we'll keep them in the dungeon for now, anyway.\nI'll decide what to with them later.
column2: 哦，见鬼……好吧，反正先把他们关在地牢里。\n我以后再决定怎么处置他们。

column1: Ooh-hoo-hoo! There's a nice handful of gold here, miss!
column2: 哦呵呵！这儿有好一把金子呢，小姐！

column1: There's nothin' 'ere really worth takin', miss...
column2: 这儿其实没什么值得拿的，小姐……

column1: They're trying to escape! Get them!
column2: 他们想逃！抓住他们！

column1: Well, I'm almost impressed anyway. We really need something better than that old tree to hide the entrance to our base...
column2: 行吧，我倒还是有点佩服。我们真该找个比那棵老树强的东西，把基地入口遮住……

column1: Well, well. I am impressed that you managed to find our little hideaway.
column2: 哟，哟。你们能找到我们这个小窝，我挺佩服。

column1: What the hell is going on in there?!
column2: 里面到底他妈的怎么回事？！

column1:
The treasure's gone and all is taken
My sack filled with wonderous loot
And now it's time to move my bacon
Off I go, it's time to scoot!
column2:
宝藏没了，全被拿走。
我的袋子塞满了奇妙的赃物。
现在该挪动我的屁股。
我走啦，是时候开溜！

column1: And allow you to roam free to spread your wickedness as you please? No, demon! You shall be put down where you stand, in the name of God!
column2: 还让你随意游走，随心散播邪恶？不，恶魔！你将就地被诛，以上帝之名！

column1: And only newly born. Imagine the power, had he been allowed to mature! Such a waste.
column2: 而且才刚刚降生。想想看，若容他长成，那力量该有多大！真是浪费。

column1: And so you force my first moments to be violent? So be it, then.
column2: 所以你们非要我降生的第一刻便是暴力？那就如此吧。

column1: By our righteous hand, you are banished, demon! Trouble this realm no more!
column2: 凭我们正义之手，你被放逐了，恶魔！勿再扰乱此界！

column1: Good. I thank you.
column2: 很好。我感谢你。

column1: I have been reborn. Move aside, and I shall leave you in peace.
column2: 我已经重生。让开，我便让你们安宁。

column1: I've cleared out the other room and pulled up the floor so I can begin my dig in earnest. I don't know what I'll find down there, but my gut tells me this is what I need to do.
column2: 我清出了另一个房间，把地板掀了，可以认真开挖了。我不知道下面有什么，可我的直觉说，这就是我该做的事。

column1: I've hit some kind of brickwork. A ruin? I can't really tell, and I don't really care. I just know that I need to get inside, no matter what.
column2: 我挖到了一种砖砌的东西。废墟？我也说不清，而且我也不在乎。我只知道我必须进去，不管付出什么。

column1: It's much clearer here. I need to keep going down. I just wish I knew why.
column2: 这里清楚多了。我得继续往下。我只希望自己知道为什么。

column1: Such a magnificent form! Burn his shape into your mind, Master, for that is the glory that one day awaits you as well!
column2: 何等壮丽的形体！把他的形貌烙进你的脑海，主人，因为那份荣耀有朝一日也同样等待着你！

column1: You. I heard your footsteps echoing through the darkness. How long... how long have I been here?
column2: 你。我听见你的脚步在黑暗中回响。多久了……我在这儿多久了？

column1: Greed
column2: 贪婪

column1: They're after the Fang! Stop them, you fools!
column2: 他们是冲着尖牙来的！拦住他们，你们这群蠢货！

column1: Anyway, go back to sleep. See you in the morning.
column2: 总之，回去接着睡。早上见。

column1: Aww, come on, you've gotta be kidding me, piece of goddamn junk!
column2: 哎呀，得了吧，你他妈在逗我吧，这天杀的破烂！

column1: Be Careful
column2: 小心点

column1: Boss, my bed's trashed. There's no place for me to sleep.
column2: 老大，我的床废了。我没地方睡。

column1: Boss, these beds ain't all that big. I don't know if we're both gonna fit.
column2: 老大，这些床没多大。我不知道咱俩挤不挤得下。

column1: Boss... are you sure? You've been sleeping on the ground just as much as I have.
column2: 老大……你确定？你睡地上的次数不比我少。

column1: Come here and get in with me, and keep it down.
column2: 过来跟我挤，小声点。

column1: Don't Go
column2: 别走

column1: Fuck, I am soaked! This place had better be dry!
column2: 操，我湿透了！这地方最好是干的！

column1: Fuck. I guess I'll just keep watch until morning.
column2: 操。看来我只能守到早上了。

column1: Hey, this place has beds and everything. Looks nice and dry too!
column2: 嘿，这地方有床，啥都有。看着还挺干爽！

column1: I ain't slept in a bed in months! I'm lookin' forward to this!
column2: 我好几个月没在床上睡过了！我可盼着这一下呢！

column1: I don't think there's anything to worry about. Nothing's leaving home in this weather.
column2: 我觉得没什么好担心的。这种天气，没什么会出门。

column1: I'm just going to keep watch. No way I'm getting back to sleep now. See you in the morning, I guess.
column2: 我去守着就行。这下反正睡不着了。早上见吧，我想。

column1: Just hurry up while it's still warm.
column2: 趁还热乎，赶紧的。

column1: Keep it Down
column2: 小声点

column1: Right, whatever.
column2: 行，随便。

column1: Share my Bed
column2: 一起睡

column1: Take my Bed
column2: 床给你

column1: Thanks, boss. That means a lot.
column2: 谢了，老大。这对我很重要。

column1: We'll squeeze. Come on, nobody's sleeping on the floor tonight.
column2: 挤一挤。来，今晚谁也不许睡地板。

column1: Yeah, fine, just cold and cranky.
column2: 嗯，没事，就是又冷又窝火。

column1: You okay?
column2: 你没事吧？

column1: You take this bed. I'll keep watch.
column2: 你睡这张床。我来守夜。

column1: You're the best. Thanks.
column2: 你最棒了。谢谢。

column1: As a show of gratitude, let me offer you this piece of advice: stay clear of the center of the caldera, if you can. It houses the richest ruins, but far more powerful beings than you compete for them. T'would be better for you to skirt the rim, if wend you eastward.
column2: 为表谢意，容我献上一句忠告：若能避开，便离破火山口的中心远些。那里有最富庶的废墟，但争夺它们的存在远比你们强大。你们若往东去，最好贴着边缘绕行。

column1: His castle is in the mountains, should you wish an audience. Perhaps, if he is of a kind mood, he will grant you leave to pass. Perhaps not. It is for him to decide.
column2: 他的城堡在群山之中，你们若想谒见的话。也许他心情和善，便会准许你们通过。也许不会。这由他决定。

column1: Magnificent! I am bound to his service no longer!
column2: 太好了！我再也不必受缚为他效力了！

column1: Now, I must go, for I am Lord of my own hunt, and you have earned the right to keep your blood! Bon soir!
column2: 现在我该走了。我已是自己狩猎的领主，而你们赢得了保住自己鲜血的权利！Bon soir！

column1: Now, leave.
column2: 现在，离开。

column1: Turn back, warmblood. This road is owned by Lord Frico, and he suffers no trespassers.
column2: 回头吧，热血者。这条路是 Frico 领主的，他不容擅闯者。

column1: You! You are the ones who have slain Lord Frico! I can yet smell his blood upon you.
column2: 你们！你们就是杀死 Frico 领主的人！我还能在你们身上闻到他的血。

column1: A.B.\nThe People's Scoundrel
column2: A.B.\n人民的恶棍

column1: A.R.\nWhose Coffin Lies Empty
column2: A.R.\n棺中空无一人

column1: F.C.\nThe Unquiet Pen
column2: F.C.\n不宁之笔

column1: G.K. \nGloriously Defiant
column2: G.K. \n光荣不屈

column1: K.S.\nMother and Scholar
column2: K.S.\n母亲与学者

column1: Little Hariett\nWho Never had a Chance to Grow Up
column2: 小 Hariett\n从未有机会长大

column1: R.W.\nThe Brave Woman who Charged Ahead
column2: R.W.\n冲锋在前的勇敢女人

column1: S.E.\nWho Glorified the Flesh of Man
column2: S.E.\n颂扬人之血肉者

column1: Argh, I knew I should have poisoned the fountain! I won't be making THAT mistake again.
column2: 啊，我就知道该给喷泉下毒的！那种错我绝不再犯了。

column1: Find me in the next room if you ain't afraid to get a little blood on you.
column2: 你要是不怕沾上点血，就到下一个房间来找我。

column1: Freshened up are we? Good, there's no more time to waste!
column2: 清爽了？很好，没时间再浪费了！

column1: How do you figure you get as far as you do? Is it because you are strong, or is it because you gather strong people around you?
column2: 你觉得自己能走到这一步，是因为什么？是因为你强，还是因为你身边聚了一群强的人？

column1: I can either reward you with fantastic riches, or with ancient and secret knowledge. What'll it be?
column2: 我可以奖你惊人的财富，也可以奖你古老而隐秘的知识。你要哪样？

column1: I'm expecting a good fight. Don't disappoint.
column2: 我指望一场精彩的打斗。别让我失望。

column1: In order to make sure our well-paying spectators get to see the best fights, I'll be making this all interactive-like, and changing the fight depending on your answer. Fun, right?
column2: 为了让那些出手阔绰的观众看到最精彩的打斗，我会把这弄成互动的，并按你的回答改变这场战斗。好玩吧？

column1: It's not all bad though, right? I mean, you've got some valuable stuff on you, and now that you're half-dead and I've already seen all your moves, well... I won't even break a sweat. Goodnight,
column2: 不过也不全是坏事，对吧？我是说，你身上带着点值钱的东西，现在你又半死不活，你的招式我也看光了，嗯……我连汗都不用出。晚安，

column1: Listen, you little shit, these profits are mine! You wiped out all of my biggest money-makers in the space of an hour! Nobody comes to an arena with no monsters in it! I'm ruined, and it's all your fault!
column2: 听着，你这小杂种，这些利润是我的！你一个钟头之内就把我那些最大的摇钱树全灭了！没人会来一座没有怪物的竞技场！我毁了，全是你的错！

column1: Nobody's got this far in quite a long time. Lookin' like you actually have a shot at the prize. That's great. Wonderful.
column2: 好久没人走到这一步了。看着你还真有机会拿到奖。真好。太棒了。

column1: Not bad! Let's keep up the pressure.
column2: 不错！继续加压。

column1: Now, tell me how you would rather relax. Being surrounded with the faces of familiar people or being left alone with your thoughts in silence?
column2: 现在告诉我，你更想怎么放松。身边围满熟面孔，还是在寂静中独自与自己的念头相处？

column1: Oh, its you again. Thought you had me dead didn't you. Well, I'm not that easy to kill, I'll have you know. And though it pains me to let you in through here again, I am finding less adventurers willing to run this gauntlet. Well, the show must go on, have at thee.
column2: 哦，又是你。你以为把我弄死了，是吧。告诉你，我可没那么好杀。虽然再放你从这儿进来让我心痛，可愿意闯这道关的冒险者，我发现是越来越少了。好吧，戏还得演，放马过来。

column1: Once you're in, though, you're in until you're either dead or out the other end, so if you're too scared, best you turn that delicate frame around and step out of here.
column2: 不过一旦进来，就得待到要么咽气，要么从另一头出去。所以你要是太害怕，最好掉转你那副娇贵的身板，从这儿走出去。

column1: Oops, it looks like I wasn't able to get more monsters for that challenge. Oh well, I guess this one's on me. Please proceed to the next room.
column2: 哎呀，看来那场挑战我没能再搞到更多怪物。好吧，这次算我的。请移步下一个房间。

column1: Perfect! Ladies and gentlemen, I give you our champions! And champions... your reward!
column2: 完美！女士们，先生们，我为各位呈上我们的冠军！冠军们……这是你们的奖赏！

column1: So, here we go! What do you think is more important for a fighter? To be tough as hell, or to be flexible and adaptable?
column2: 那么，开始吧！你觉得对一个斗士来说，什么更重要？硬得要死，还是灵活、善于应变？

column1: Try not to die too fast. I paid good money for this.
column2: 死得别太快。这我花了不少钱。

column1: Welcome to my arena, adventurers. I run a little business here you might be interested in. It's real simple. People pay to watch a good fight. You fight, and win, and you get a cut of the coin. Great, right?
column2: 欢迎来到我的竞技场，冒险者们。我在这儿做点小生意，你们也许会感兴趣。特别简单。人们花钱看一场精彩的打斗。你们打，打赢了，就能分到一份钱。很棒，对吧？

column1: Well, look at you. Made it all the way to the end, didn't you? And as promised, your amazingly valuable reward! Now if you noticed a theme here, I'm gonna give you a choice on your prize.
column2: 瞧瞧你们。一路走到头了，对吧？而且说到做到，你们那价值惊人的奖赏！要是你们看出来了这里的主题，我就让你们选奖品。

column1: What is more important to you personally? Having a strong body, or a being well-known?
column2: 对你个人而言，什么更重要？拥有强壮的身体，还是广为人知？

column1: What sounds like a better place to spend all your riches when you win the jackpot? A cool boreal plateau or a warm beach?
column2: 等你中了头奖，把全部财富花在哪儿听起来更好？凉爽的寒带高原，还是温暖的海滩？

column1: You're stronger than you look. The crowd is most impressed. Now, though, it's time to get real.
column2: 你比看起来更强。观众佩服得很。不过现在，该来真的了。

column1: You're the one who's competing? Maybe I should change my bets.
column2: 参赛的是你？也许我该改改赌注。

column1: Oh God, not more sahaguin! Don't let them get me!
column2: 上帝啊，怎么又是沙华鱼人！别让他们抓到我！

column1: Got through all them zombers did ya? Cute.
column2: 那些僵尸你都闯过来啦？真可爱。

column1: Hold on, I smell blood. A lot of it. Something else, too...
column2: 等一下，我闻到血了。很多血。还有别的什么……

column1: I gotta wait here till someone wants to go, so tell me if you're in.
column2: 我得在这儿等到有人想上路，你要是去就告诉我。

column1: Lucky fer you, Frico and I, we're real good. You wanna see Frico, I can get you in. Hell, it's why good old Byrne is here, to guide folks like you to his frilly magnificence.
column2: 算你走运，我跟 Frico 关系铁得很。你想见 Frico，我能把你弄进去。见鬼，老 Byrne 在这儿，就是为了把你们这样的人领到他那位花里胡哨的阁下跟前。

column1: Storm shelter
column2: 风暴庇护所

column1: There's a leech somewhere nearby. A vampire. Be on guard.
column2: 附近有条水蛭。一个吸血鬼。当心。

column1: Well, I won't mess with you. If you're takin' this road, you must be headin' east, right? Frico controls the pass headin' that way.
column2: 好吧，我不招惹你。你要是走这条路，准是往东，对吧？往那边去的关口归 Frico 管。

column1: What do you want?
column2: “你想干什么？”

column1: What?
column2: “什么？”

column1: Did you hear that?
column2: “你听见了吗？”

column1: Right.
Shall we?
column2: “来吧？”

column1: Fine.
What do you think?
column2: “你觉得呢？”

column1: ...well, despite his recklessness, he is a dear friend of mine. We were pastors in a village church, back home.\nI fear for his safety, though. He has lost his way in recent months.
column2: “……嗯，尽管他行事鲁莽，他仍是我的好友。我们从前在家乡的一座乡村教堂里一起当牧师。\n不过我担心他的安危。近几个月来，他迷失了方向。”

column1: Forgive me, I've kept you for long enough, and I must keep looking elsewhere.\nBlessings upon you, and a safe journey, wherever it is you're heading.
column2: “原谅我，我耽搁你够久了，还得去别处继续找。\n祝福你，无论你前往何处，一路平安。”

column1: He wears a set of robes similar to mine.\nDoes the emblem on my mantle look familiar at all?
column2: “他穿着一套与我相似的长袍。\n我斗篷上的纹章，你看着眼熟吗？”

column1: Oh! Excuse me, but have you seen a man named Evans\non your travels? He's...
column2: “哦！打扰一下，请问你在旅途中\n见过一个叫 Evans 的男人吗？他……”

column1: Well, I suppose it is unlikely that you would have come across him. He could be anywhere by now.
column2: “唉，我觉得你遇见过他的可能性不大。到现在，他可能在任何地方。”

column1: You have seen the magic circle inside that old\nrun-down cottage, haven't you? It's a design he often used, so I'm sure he's been here, but it seems the trail is somewhat cold.
column2: “你看见那座又老又破的\n小屋里面的魔法阵了吧？那是他常用的图案，所以我肯定他来过这儿，不过踪迹已经淡了。”

column1: Butchered six cows today. Would take on more work, but teaching my eldest boys to do it slows me down.
column2: “今天宰了六头牛。本来还能再接活，可教那几个大儿子学着干，把我拖慢了。”

column1: I can't even teach my boys to be good fighters, since my pa never bothered to teach me. I saved up all that money so I could send my boys to any academy they wanted, and Kam wants to go to military school. His brothers will probably all follow him. Even my boys don't need me.
column2: “我连把儿子们教成好战士都做不到，因为我爹从来就懒得教我。我攒下那么多钱，好送儿子们去任何他们想去的学院，而 Kam 想上军校。他的兄弟们大概全都会跟着他。连我的儿子们也不需要我了。”

column1: I hate stupid girls
column2: “我讨厌蠢女孩。”

column1: I was so happy when our second daughter was born, but my husband became depressed. He thinks that I won't have any more children with him now that we've had two girls.
column2: “我们第二个女儿出生的时候，我高兴极了，可我丈夫却消沉了。他觉得既然已经有了两个女孩，我就不会再给他生了。”

column1: I'm just a useless orc now.
column2: “我现在不过是个没用的兽人。”

column1: Or, maybe it's just me slowing down. Now that we've got two girls, my wife gets a generous stipend from the county every month. It's far more money than I ever make in a month, so my work no longer makes a difference. She doesn't need me anymore.
column2: “又或者，只是我自己慢了下来。如今我们有了两个女孩，我妻子每个月都能从郡里领到一笔丰厚的津贴。那比我一个月能挣到的多得多，所以我干的活再也无关紧要。她不再需要我了。”

column1: That fool man. Doesn't he know by now how much I love him and our army of little boys? I'll have as many children as he'll bless me with. I couldn't be happier.
column2: “那个傻男人。他到现在还不知道我有多爱他、有多爱我们那一大队小男孩吗？他肯赐我多少孩子，我就生多少。我已经幸福得不能再幸福了。”

column1: Everyone else wait outside. This is going to be messy.
column2: “其他人都在外面等着。这下要弄得很脏。”

column1: Finally alone. Anything you want to say before we get started?
column2: “终于就咱们俩了。开始之前，你还有什么想说的吗？”

column1: I hope you're ready for this.
column2: “希望你准备好了。”

column1: I know they're all out there waiting for us but I don't even care. I've waited more than twenty years for this moment. They can wait another hour.
column2: “我知道他们全在外面等着我们，可我根本不在乎。这一刻我等了二十多年。他们再等一个钟头也没关系。”

column1: I've been wanting to tear your clothes off with my teeth ever since we got finished with Frico and your heart started beating again. I'm done waiting.
column2: “从咱们把 Frico 解决掉、你的心又开始跳起来那时候起，我就想用牙把你的衣服撕掉。我等够了。”

column1: No, it can't.
column2: “不，不能。”

column1: That's it, I can't take this anymore.
column2: “够了，我再也忍不了了。”

column1: Ugh, fine. Just get it out of your system so you can focus for once.
column2: “呃，行吧。把你这股劲泄掉，你就能难得专心一回。”

column1: Uh oh. What is it now?
column2: “糟了。又怎么了？”

column1: Wait, what? Right now? Can't it wait until later?
column2: “等等，什么？就现在？不能等以后吗？”

column1: Yeah. Ever since you cured me, and all the feelings came rushing back, I've been lookin' forward to this.
column2: “对。从你把我治好、那些感觉全涌回来之后，我就一直盼着这个。”

column1: Arpa, our newest line, offers service to the southern ports of the Coldforge region as well as the breathtaking north shore of the Blackglass mountains, where many of our island's world-famous natural springs attract throngs of visitors annually.
column2: “阿尔帕是我们最新的线路，通往冷锻地区的南部港口，以及黑璃山脉那令人屏息的北岸。那里有我们这座岛上许多举世闻名的天然温泉，每年吸引成群结队的访客。”

column1: Food! Food! Bring me everything you've got!
column2: “吃的！吃的！把你们有的全给我拿来！”

column1: In fact, with regular use, the inside of the tunnels remain smooth, straight, and clean, and the only maintenance the culture requires is on either end of the tunnel, in order to prevent it from growing too far into the outside environment.
column2: “事实上，只要经常使用，隧道内部就会保持光滑、笔直、洁净，而这团培养体唯一需要的维护是在隧道两端，以防它过多地长到外界环境里去。”

column1: In order to keep the culture moist and alive, enclosed conditions were necessary, so the transit system was established fully  underground where the culture is able to regulate its own environmental needs.
column2: “为使培养体保持湿润与存活，必须有封闭的环境，因此运输系统完全建在地下，培养体在那里能够自行调节自身所需的环境。”

column1: Planning a trip with the Royal Transit System has never been easier. Fast, comfortable, and affordable, offering access to all major destinations in Lukatt!
column2: “借助皇家运输系统规划行程，从未如此轻松。迅速、舒适、价格实惠，可抵达卢卡特的所有主要目的地！”

column1: Remember that all tickets include complimentary refreshments and an in-transit meal. For dining car hours, please ask your concierge.
column2: “请记住，所有车票都包含免费茶点，以及一份途中餐食。餐车的开放时间，请询问您的礼宾员。”

column1: Royal Transit System
column2: “皇家运输系统”

column1: So, the next time you travel, put your feet up and travel with us, your friendly Royal Transit System. See you soon!
column2: “所以，下次出行，把脚一搁，与我们同行，您亲切的皇家运输系统。回头见！”

column1: The Arkasin line offers service to the midland destinations in the Knightwood area as well as to the scenic Pagewood, with close access to shipping ports bound for Tsarath and a ready sampling of coastal life.
column2: “阿卡辛线通往骑士林一带的中部目的地，以及风景优美的侍从林，紧邻驶往察拉思的航运港口，也可就近领略沿岸的生活。”

column1: The Klarthus line was established for easy connections to the historic Yaksteppe area, where our island's traditions began many years ago, and the popular Forfshire region, where the scenic beaches attract thousands every year.
column2: “克拉图斯线的设立，是为了便捷连接历史悠久的牦牛草原地区——我们这座岛的传统许多年前便发源于此——以及广受欢迎的福夫郡地区，那里风景优美的海滩每年吸引数千人。”

column1: The Royal Transit System was established under the enlightened rule of King Naczer II. Court researchers experimented with culturing the remarkable phenomenon commonly called Primordial Ooze.
column2: “皇家运输系统建立于国王 Naczer 二世的开明统治之下。宫廷的研究者曾试验培养这种俗称原初软泥的非凡现象。”

column1: The Zias line is the longest of our transit lines, clocking in at just over eight hours, and it offers service to both the popular markets of Whetners, and the Knavewood region, where many of our greatest artisans practice their crafts.
column2: “齐亚斯线是我们最长的运输线路，全程刚过八小时，通往广受欢迎的惠特纳市场，以及无赖林地区，我们许多最杰出的工匠在那里施展手艺。”

column1: The Zosark line is currently under construction, and promises to expand our transit network even further, putting the whole of our beautiful island easily within your reach.
column2: “佐萨克线目前正在修建，并承诺把我们的运输网络扩展得更远，让我们这座美丽岛屿的全境都轻易变得触手可及。”

column1: The extraordinary properties of this ooze also prompt it to grow its own support structures in the form of ribs, so the tunnel actively prevents its own collapse.
column2: “这种软泥的非凡特性还会促使它长出形如肋骨的支撑结构，因此隧道会主动防止自身坍塌。”

column1: The length of the Arpa line is approximately six and one-half hours, so find a seat and make yourself comfortable! For our Gold Seal ticket holders, your private cabins are waiting!
column2: “阿尔帕线全程大约六个半小时，所以找个座位，让自己舒服些！持有我们金印车票的旅客，您的私人包厢已在等候！”

column1: The ooze was known to cover large continuous surfaces if left undisturbed, and has no stomach, but a powerful muscular swallowing mechanism in order to spread food across as much of its surface as possible.
column2: “众所周知，这种软泥若不受打扰，便会覆盖大片连续的表面。它没有胃，却有一套强有力的肌肉吞咽机制，好把食物尽量摊到自己更多的表面上。”

column1: The original line, Chrun, offers service to the King's Caldera for an exciting day in the big city, and Bracewind to relax in the peace and natural beauty of our island's southernmost destination.
column2: “最初的线路克伦，通往国王破火山口，供人在大城里度过刺激的一天；也通往布雷斯温德，让人在我们这座岛最南端的目的地，于宁静与自然之美中放松。”

column1: Welcome to the Arpa line of the Royal Transit System. We're here to ensure that your journey is as comfortable and relaxing as possible, so please ask one of our friendly staff members if you need anything or have any questions.
column2: “欢迎乘坐皇家运输系统的阿尔帕线。我们在此确保您的旅程尽可能舒适、轻松，若有任何需要或疑问，请询问我们亲切的工作人员。”

column1: When applied to the inside of a tunnel and appropriately stimulated by scent and tactile cues, the large culture 'swallows' in a particular direction, providing labour-free movement to the trains.
column2: “当它被敷在隧道内壁，并受到气味与触觉信号的适当刺激时，这大团培养体便会朝特定方向“吞咽”，从而为列车提供无需劳作的移动。”

column1: Whew. I couldn't eat another bite!
column2: “呼。我再也吃不下一口了！”

column1: ... well this is not what I was expecting, but it's certainly diverting, I'll give you that. I feel like I shouldn't be reading it with you standing here, however, so I'll just hold on to that for later. Thank you, I think. Let me give you a little something for it.
column2: “……嗯，这可不是我所料想的，不过确实挺能解闷，这点我承认。可你站在这儿，我觉得不该当着你的面读，所以我先留着，以后再看。谢谢你，大概吧。让我为它给你一点小东西。”

column1: ? I've never heard of this book. Let's see...
column2: “？我从没听说过这本书。让我看看……”

column1: Anyway, if you do find your way into that room, let me know what you find. You can have it of course, but I am terribly curious.
column2: “总之，你要是真进了那间屋子，告诉我你找到了什么。东西当然归你，可我实在好奇得厉害。”

column1: I'm Vankan, by the way. I'll just hang out here, if you don't mind. This place is the best shelter I've found so far, and there are enough books to keep me reading for the rest of my life. And, who knows? Maybe I'll discover something truly amazing!
column2: “对了，我是 Vankan。你不介意的话，我就在这儿待着。这是我到目前为止找到的最好的遮蔽处，而且书够我读一辈子。还有，谁知道呢？也许我会发现真正惊人的东西！”

column1: It's a shame all of these books are historical. As much as I love plumbing the depths of history, it would be nice to read something frivolous for a change.
column2: “可惜这些书全是历史。我虽然那么爱往历史的深处钻，可换换口味，读点轻浮的也不错。”

column1: Korolf flexed his rough hewn abs and Milde found herself being guided to her soft bed by the sheer force of Korolf's undulating midsection. She parted her thighs in anticipation, exposing the soft, green petals of her... oh.
column2: “Korolf 绷紧他那粗凿出来的腹肌，Milde 发现自己光凭 Korolf 那起伏腰腹的力量，就被引到了柔软的床上。她满怀期待地分开大腿，露出自己那柔软的绿色花瓣……哦。”

column1: Looters? Not much valuable here, unless you're looking for history. Found some particularly interesting material regarding the fall of the old kingdom. I've already read it all, of course. Take a look, and don't mind me. I sleep here but I make no real claim to the building.
column2: “掠夺者？这儿没什么值钱的，除非你找的是历史。我发现了一些关于旧王国覆灭的特别有意思的材料。当然，我已经全部读过了。你看看吧，不用管我。我睡在这儿，可并不真把这栋建筑当成我的。”

column1: Oh, if you have your heart set on looting, there is that locked room over there, I suppose. I haven't found a key, so I have no idea what's inside. If you think you can get in, go ahead.
column2: “哦，你要是铁了心要搜刮，那边倒是有一间上了锁的屋子，我想。我没找到钥匙，所以不知道里面是什么。你觉得自己进得去，就去吧。”

column1: Probably not though.
column2: “不过多半进不去。”

column1: The Burntfoot March
column2: “《Burntfoot进军》”

column1: The Sumptuous Garden
column2: “《奢华花园》”

column1: Afterward, I will quit this estate for good, and start my new life with my beloved by my side.
column2: “在那之后，我将永远离开这座庄园，与我的爱人并肩开始新生活。”

column1: Carrots,\nParsnips.
column2: “胡萝卜，\n欧洲防风。”

column1: Cellar
column2: “地窖”

column1: Crimson Peony,\nDwarf Rhododendron,\nRoyal Amethyst.
column2: “绯红牡丹，\n矮生杜鹃，\n皇家紫晶。”

column1: I know who is behind it. He has always wanted her for himself, and he is the only one in this estate with enough skill to unravel my enchantment without destroying it outright.
column2: “我知道是谁干的。他一直想把她据为己有，而这座庄园里只有他技艺够高，能拆解我的附魔，又不把它彻底毁掉。”

column1: I want revenge, but now is not the time. Instead, I will focus on creating a new gem for my sweetheart. One even better than before--one more becoming of her sweetness and innocence.
column2: “我想复仇，可现在还不是时候。我要转而专心为心上人做一颗新宝石。一颗比从前还好的——一颗更配得上她的甜美与纯真。”

column1: It feels rather soon, but I have decided I shall propose to her on the night of the Summer festival. We have both subtly confessed our feelings for each other, so time is of the essence. I must find a nice suit, and practice what I shall say to her.
column2: “虽然觉得有些早，可我已经决定，要在夏日节的夜里向她求婚。我们都已含蓄地向彼此表露过心意，所以时间紧迫。我得找一套体面的礼服，还得练习要对她说的话。”

column1: Pantry
column2: “食品间”

column1: Spring Greens,\nKale,\nCauliflower.
column2: “春季青菜，\n羽衣甘蓝，\n花椰菜。”

column1: Summer Festival
column2: “夏日节”

column1: Sweet Potatoes.
column2: “甘薯。”

column1: This time, however, I shall take precautions. Tonight, after everyone is asleep, I will sneak outside through the cellar and hide the gem in the old well. If I used the back door, they would hear the wretched thing groaning for certain.
column2: “不过这一次，我会预先防范。今夜等所有人都睡了，我要从地窖溜出去，把宝石藏进那口老井。我要是走后门，他们铁定听得见那可恶的东西在呻吟。”

column1: Today is the last weekend before the Summer festival. I've checked on the new gem nearly every night since I hid it, and nobody seems to suspect anything. Now, I can finally focus my efforts on the revenge I have been waiting for so patiently. He will learn to regret crossing me.
column2: “今天是夏日节前的最后一个周末。自从藏起那颗新宝石，我几乎每晚都去查看，似乎谁也没有起疑。现在，我终于可以把精力放到我耐心等待已久的复仇上了。他会学会后悔与我作对。”

column1: Today, I discovered that someone has tampered with the engagement ruby I had toiled over these past months. The clear, brilliant, pinkish-red shimmer it once had is gone. It is now filled with cracks, and has turned a dull, cloudy red. I feel sick and angry just looking at it.
column2: “今天，我发现有人动了我这几个月来辛苦做成的订婚红宝石。它曾有的那种清澈、灿烂的粉红光泽已经不见了。如今它布满裂痕，变成了暗淡浑浊的红色。我只是看着它，就觉得恶心，而且愤怒。”

column1: Today, I have finally succeeded in creating an engagement present for my beloved. An enchanted red ruby, transmuted from a mere chunk of glass. Whenever I hold it, it instills a feeling of warmth and comfort. I hope that she will keep it close to her, and think of me.
column2: “今天，我终于成功做出了给爱人的订婚礼物。一颗附了魔的红宝石，由不过一块玻璃转化而来。每当我握住它，它就注入温暖与安慰的感觉。我希望她把它带在身边，并且想到我。”

column1: Today, I have finished a new gem to give to my sweetheart. A simple, pure white crystal. It shines with a calming blue glow. I confess I could have used this myself when I discovered that blackguard's tampering.
column2: “今天，我完成了一颗要送给心上人的新宝石。一颗简单的纯白水晶。它闪着令人平静的蓝光。我承认，发现那个恶棍动手脚的时候，我自己倒用得上这个。”

column1: Until the eve before the Summer festival, the gem shall lay hidden beneath the grounds of this estate, out of anyone else's reach. I will keep the cellar key hidden in the spare room until then.
column2: “在夏日节前夜到来之前，这颗宝石将一直藏在这座庄园的地底，任何其他人都够不着。在那之前，我会把地窖的钥匙藏在空房间里。”

column1: A woman who rages against the unfairness of the whole world. What's one more beast to her? Her rage will serve you well, but she is dangerous in more ways than that. She understands nothing, and will be the doom of her entire people. Let her bring doom elsewhere.
column2: “一个愤恨整个世界之不公的女人。对她来说，再多一头野兽又算什么？她的怒火会为你派上大用场，可她的危险远不止于此。她什么都不懂，而且会成为她整个族群的末日。让她把末日带到别处去吧。”

column1: Ah, tatters and skin, it's a timeless look, and I do like my would-be heroes wearing as little as possible. That one's fun, but I'm not certain he really has the ferocity you're going to need here. I'd say that you must know something here I don't, but frankly that's not possible.
column2: “啊，破布和皮肉，真是永不过时的打扮，而我确实喜欢我那些准英雄穿得越少越好。那个挺好玩，可我不太确定他真有你在这儿需要的凶性。我本想说，你一定知道些我所不知道的，可坦白讲，那是不可能的。”

column1: Ah, your loyal servant, of course. He hates your guts, you know. Good thing he's cosmically bound by contract and all that. He'll be useful fodder in the fight at least. Still, it would've been better if you had summoned me instead. I at least know how to have fun.
column2: “啊，你忠诚的仆人，当然。他恨你入骨，这你知道。好在他被契约在宇宙层面上绑死了，诸如此类。至少在这场战斗里，他会是有用的炮灰。不过，你当时要是召唤的是我，还会更好。我起码知道怎么找乐子。”

column1: All my life I have prepared for this moment. You, divine beast, have a place waiting on the edge of my blade!
column2: “我一生都在为这一刻做准备。你，神兽，我的刀锋上有你的位置！”

column1: And what would an epic final confrontation be without a manipulative, heartless sorcerer? There's a man who feels nothing but cold fascination, who pays more attention to the patterns of his killing magic than to the screams that follow it. He'll probably be useful.
column2: “一场史诗般的最终对决，怎么能少了一个善于操纵、无情的巫师？有这么一个人，心中除了冰冷的迷恋一无所有，他对自己杀戮魔法的纹路，比对随之而来的惨叫更加上心。他大概会有用。”

column1: Are you really certain that bringing the batty old doomsayer to face down a literal and actual divine beast is a good idea? He seems as liable to kneel and worship as to fight. Then again, once you've seen him, maybe you'll want to kneel and worship too. It's been known to happen.
column2: “你真的确定，把那个神神叨叨的老末日预言者带来，面对一头字面意义上、实实在在的神兽，是个好主意吗？他跪下来崇拜，和动手开战，可能性一样大。不过话说回来，等你见到他，也许你也会想跪下崇拜。这种事是发生过的。”

column1: Are you serious? That one may be eager to prove himself to you but at heart, he is a worker, not a warrior. Are you quite certain it is a good idea to let him use this particular crucial moment as an opportunity to build on his broken self-esteem?
column2: “你是认真的？那一位也许急着向你证明自己，可他骨子里是个干活的，不是战士。你真的确定，让他拿这个特别关键的时刻当机会，往他破碎的自尊上再垒一层，是个好主意吗？”

column1: Are you surprised to see me? This place is further removed from the rules of your world than most, so I can briefly manifest enough to make my voice heard. To you, anyway.
column2: “见到我，你惊讶吗？这地方比大多数地方都更远离你们世界的规则，所以我能短暂显形，好让我的声音被听见。反正，对你是这样。”

column1: At least I'll have a grand grave. To die in the tomb of King Chevre is no small thing. Better still to be buried with my brothers, though.
column2: “至少我会有一座气派的坟墓。死在国王 Chevre 的陵墓里，可不是小事。不过，要是能和我的兄弟们埋在一起，那就更好了。”

column1: Does that one even know what he wants? Do you think so indecisive a creature could give you a decisive edge in a war against a holy engine of fury? I can only guess at the leaps of your mind to think that this was a sound tactical decision, and I am frankly finding doubt at your odds of success.
column2: “那一位究竟知道自己想要什么吗？你觉得一个如此优柔寡断的生物，能在对抗一具神圣怒火引擎的战争中给你决定性的优势吗？你竟把这当作一个稳妥的战术决定，我只能猜测你的心思跳了多远，而坦白说，我开始怀疑你成功的胜算。”

column1: Excellent. The chains hold strong, and slaying him should be simple. Once he lies dead, you will be free to leave the island by sea. Let us be done with it.
column2: “很好。锁链绑得很牢，杀掉他应当很简单。一旦他倒下死去，你就可以从海上离开这座岛。我们把这事了结吧。”

column1: For as long as you remain on this island and work toward building a kingdom, you will have serendipitous fortune and health, as will your successors. Five-hundred years' worth, as promised, and then the crown is mine. Let's get started, shall we?
column2: “只要你留在这座岛上，并致力于建立一个王国，你就会拥有不期而至的好运与健康，你的继承者也一样。如所承诺的，五百年的分量，然后王冠归我。我们开始吧，好吗？”

column1: For five hundred years, you and your kin shall know my protection, and I shall heed your voice when I am called. This I do willingly, and then, I shall depart for places darker.
column2: “五百年间，你和你的血亲都将得到我的保护，我被召唤时也会听从你的声音。此事我心甘情愿，然后，我将前往更黑暗的地方。”

column1: For now, though, I must rest a fortnight's slumber at least. Please, go, and carry with you my thanks. I will see you soon.
column2: “不过眼下，我至少必须沉睡两周。请走吧，并带上我的感谢。我很快会再见到你。”

column1: Fresh-faced youth is likely to end up dashed upon the floor in a place like this. He's enthusiastic and grows a decent enough beard, but one way or another, this place will probably scar him for life. Don't be surprised if he's useless afterwards, even if he survives.
column2: “这种稚嫩的年轻人，在这种地方多半会落得个摔碎在地上的下场。他有热情，胡子也长得还算可以，可不管怎样，这地方大概会给他留下一辈子的伤疤。就算他活下来，事后变成废物，也别惊讶。”

column1: He's incredible. I wish we didn't have to fight him, but, such is our lot, and I will not hold back. I shall crash the moon into the ocean and see which of us holds!
column2: “他不可思议。我希望我们不必跟他打，可这就是我们的命，我不会留手。我要把月亮砸进海里，看看我们谁撑得住！”

column1: Hear my warning. Do not try to reason with Leviathan. I am married into the royal family and he would heed me not. He is no creature of reason, but one of passion and godly rage, and he is himself the source of much of our island's suffering.
column2: “听我的警告。不要试图跟 Leviathan 讲道理。我虽与王室结亲，他也不会听我的。他不是讲道理的生物，而是激情与神怒的生物，而他本人正是这座岛上许多苦难的根源。”

column1: Here's one with a special hatred for The Sunken Lord! Oh, I can just smell the lust for revenge leaking out his pores! I wonder what he would offer me in exchange for my dark blessing? A portion of that lust for myself, perhaps? No matter. Ensure he does not kill Leviathan. I need him alive.
column2: “这儿有一个对沉没领主怀着特殊仇恨的！哦，我简直能闻到复仇的欲念从他的毛孔里渗出来！不知道他会拿出什么来换我的黑暗祝福？把他那份欲念分我一些，也许？无所谓。确保他不要杀死 Leviathan。我需要他活着。”

column1: I am Maxim Spartill, Lord Consort of Her Royal Highness Queen Glamig Cosova of Lukatt, and I am slain.
column2: “我是 Maxim Spartill，卢卡特女王殿下 Glamig Cosova 的王夫，而我已被杀死。”

column1: I am truly sorry, Lord Leviathan. Your greatness is outmatched only by your fury, and that fury cannot be left unchecked. Pray go peacefully.
column2: “我真的很抱歉，Leviathan 领主。您的伟大唯有您的怒火能够超越，而这怒火不能放任不管。请您平静地去吧。”

column1: I came here at my Lady Wife's bidding, to try and broker a deal with Leviathan, a divine creature that dwells 'neath our island. There are many centuries of history between the royal family and he, and we thought to seek his aid.
column2: “我奉夫人之命来到这里，想与 Leviathan 谈成一笔交易。他是栖居在我们这座岛之下的神兽。王室与他之间有许多个世纪的历史，我们本想求他援助。”

column1: I cannot say whether you are defiant or simply incapable, but it scarcely matters. You have put an end to a unique and beautiful creature who frankly had more of a right to exist than you do. And for what? The short, furtive life of a fugitive?
column2: “我说不准你是存心违抗，还是纯粹做不到，但这几乎无关紧要。你终结了一个独一无二的美丽生灵，坦白讲，他比你更有资格存在。为了什么？一个逃犯那短暂而鬼祟的一生？”

column1: I have disturbed the delicate harmony of the holy chains, and as such, they will crumble when struck. The chains are anchored at fifteen points throughout this temple. Destroy those, and he will be able to slip free of the remaining chain on his own.
column2: “我扰乱了圣链精妙的和谐，因此它们一被击中就会崩碎。锁链在这座神殿中锚定于十五处。毁掉那些锚点，他就能自己挣脱剩下的锁链。”

column1: I have tried to speak with him, to inform him of our plan and spare you the rigors of combat, but the chains dull my voice. He knows only rage, hears no reason, and he will lash out at every turn. Break his arms if you must, but leave him alive.
column2: “我试过与他说话，把我们的计划告知他，免得你们经受苦战，可锁链让我的声音发闷。他只知道怒火，听不进道理，而且会处处暴起。若不得已，打断他的手臂，但留他一命。”

column1: I see. Well, I suppose that's the best team you could put together, given the circumstances. It will have to do. \nNow, enough chit-chat.
column2: “我明白了。嗯，就眼下的情形，这大概是你能凑出来的最好的队伍。将就吧。\n好了，闲话少说。”

column1: I understand that I have harmed you and killed many others, that I have injured this island that I love. You have repaid my savagery with kindness and mercy. I am humbled, utterly.
column2: “我明白自己伤害了你，也杀死了许多其他人，我伤害了我所爱的这座岛。你们以善意和仁慈回报了我的残暴。我卑微至极。”

column1: I'll be watching.
column2: “我会看着的。”

column1: I, however, have many reasons. Clear the noise, and let us make him listen.
column2: “我却有许多理由。把杂音清掉，让我们迫使他听进去。”

column1: If you enter here, do it to destroy him. I drew his blood myself, so I am certain he can be slain. Alas, my fellows were cut down, and I was mortally wounded. There is little more I can do but pen this warning with my final hours.
column2: “如果你进入这里，就为了毁灭他而来。我亲手让他流过血，所以我确信他能被杀死。可惜，我的同伴都被砍倒，我自己也受了致命伤。在最后的几个时辰里，我除了写下这则警告，几乎什么也做不了。”

column1: Leviathan. You killed Maxim, and his revenge is long overdue! Slip back into the deep, and never return!
column2: “Leviathan。你杀了 Maxim，他的复仇早该讨还了！滚回深海，永远别再回来！”

column1: Mayhap Fastad's endeavor will bear sweeter fruit. Mine tastes only of blood.
column2: “兴许 Fastad 的事业会结出更甜的果实。我的，尝起来只有血。”

column1: My brother. I saw you only weeks ago, and now to find you like this, hundreds of years slain.
column2: “我的兄弟。几周前我才见过你，如今却发现你是这副模样，已经死了数百年。”

column1: Now here's an interesting choice. Oh don't fret, she can't see me either, but I bet she is itching insufferably right about now. I'm also not sure how you managed to convince a pretend servant of god to turn her weapon against a legitimate one, but good job on that. Take advantage of her conviction. That's about all she'll be good for.
column2: “现在倒是个有意思的选择。哦，别紧张，她也看不见我，不过我打赌她这会儿正痒得受不了。我也不知道你是怎么说服一个装出来的神仆，让她把武器转向一个真正的神仆的，不过干得漂亮。利用她的信念吧。她也就这点用处。”

column1: Now there's a solid choice! Bring the relic who should never have been here in the first place. He is meant to be ages dead already, so if he dies, nothing is lost, and if he brings you victory, so much the better. This tells me you're someone with an eye for managing risk. Good! I like that.
column2: “这才是个扎实的选择！把那个根本不该出现在这儿的老古董带来。他本该在很久以前就已经死了，所以他死了也没什么损失；他若给你带来胜利，那就更好。这说明你是个懂得拿捏风险的人。很好！我喜欢。”

column1: Now there's a solid choice, the dancing assassin! She did tell you she's an assassin, right? Lots of tricks up her sleeve, and up her skirt too, no doubt. I suspect she'll serve well in this fight, but you'd best not trust her. Who knows what she'll do when the danger's past?
column2: “这才是个扎实的选择，那个跳舞的刺客！她告诉过你她是刺客，对吧？袖子里藏着不少花样，裙子底下想必也有。我猜这场战斗里她会很好用，但你最好别信任她。谁知道危险过去之后她会做什么？”

column1: Of all goblins, you had to choose that one, the one with the literal addiction to jewelry? Even if he makes a name for himself in this battle, it will be a name unsung both by his kind and by yours. He knows this. Do you think his heart is really in this fight? Can you afford to take that chance?
column2: “所有哥布林里，你偏要选那一个，那个对珠宝简直上了瘾的？就算他在这场战斗里闯出了名号，那也是他的同类和你的同类都不会传唱的名字。他自己清楚。你觉得他的心真在这场战斗上吗？你担得起冒这个险吗？”

column1: Of course it had to be a giant fish. Why wouldn't it be a giant fish? Just... just don't leave me alone, okay? I can't die here, not like this!
column2: “当然了，非得是条巨型鱼。怎么会不是条巨型鱼呢？就……就别把我一个人丢下，好吗？我不能死在这儿，不能死成这样！”

column1: Oh to raise arms against you Lord Leviathan! I would have been your disciple if not for such rage!
column2: “哦，竟要举兵对抗您，Leviathan 领主！若不是这样的怒火，我本会成为您的门徒！”

column1: Oh, fuck me! We really gotta fight this thing? This ain't gonna be fun, boys and girls.
column2: “哦，我操！咱们真得跟这玩意儿打？这可不会好玩，兄弟们，姑娘们。”

column1: Oh, goodness. He doesn't look comfortable. Or happy to see us, for that matter. We're in it now.
column2: “哦，天哪。他看起来不太舒服。再说，也不像乐意见到我们。我们这下陷进去了。”

column1: Once all of the anchors are broken, I will be able to speak clearly with him, soothe his rage, and negotiate our terms.
column2: “一旦所有锚点都被破坏，我就能清楚地与他说话，抚平他的怒火，并交涉我们的条件。”

column1: Pff, he don't look so tough. I can still smell his blood, still hear his heart, and if he's got a heart, then it can be cut out. Come lay down for your end, you damn eel.
column2: “呸，他看着也没多厉害。我还闻得到他的血，听得到他的心跳，他既然有心脏，就能被挖出来。过来躺下领死吧，你这该死的鳗鱼。”

column1: Shame he had such trouble thinking outside of his tiny little box. He could not reason with Leviathan because he could offer Leviathan no reason to listen.
column2: “可惜他很难跳出自己那只小小的盒子去想。他无法跟 Leviathan 讲道理，因为他给不出任何理由让 Leviathan 听。”

column1: So this is what's left of the fabled hero, Maxim Spartill? I'd have liked to meet him. I understand that in life he was powerful, beautiful, and charismatic.
column2: “所以这就是传说中的英雄 Maxim Spartill 留下的东西？我倒想见见他。我听说他生前强大、美丽，又富有魅力。”

column1: Sorry, Daddy, but you're not doing the world any favors the way you are now. If it's gotta be you or us, it's gonna be you!
column2: “对不起，爸爸，可你现在这副样子，对这世界没什么好处。要是非得在你和我们之间选，那就得是你！”

column1: Such a magnificent creature! I'm rather dismayed that we'll have to destroy it.
column2: “多么壮丽的生物！想到我们不得不毁掉它，我相当沮丧。”

column1: Take your freedom then, since you desire it so badly, and leave the island to mourn its father. \n\nHe will stir the seas nevermore.
column2: “那就拿走你的自由吧，既然你如此渴望，让这座岛去哀悼它的父亲。\n\n他再也不会搅动大海。”

column1: The Left-Leaning Monster? Interesting choice, though I'd have expected someone with such a violent reputation to be a bit more violent. He might not be as useful as you'd think, unless you're planning to hide behind him.
column2: “往左歪的怪物？有意思的选择，不过我本以为名声这么暴戾的人会再暴戾一点。他也许没你想的那么有用，除非你打算躲在他身后。”

column1: The Muffin Mage. \nReally? You didn't want someone with a little more arcane fire in the belly? Maybe you just have a hardon for making things difficult? I suppose he'll at least taste good when Leviathan eats him.
column2: “松饼法师。\n真的？你就不想要个肚子里奥术之火更旺一点的人？还是你对把事情搞难就硬得不行？我猜 Leviathan 吃他的时候，味道至少还不差。”

column1: The best things about wild, axe-swinging barbarians are the deep belly-laughing when the fight is over, the drinking and the sweat and the skin when the fire is low, the warmth that burns behind the violence. This one is none of those things. She might win the fight for you, but she isn't your friend.
column2: “狂野的、挥斧的野蛮人最妙的地方，是战斗结束后从肚子深处笑出来，是火光低下来时的酒、汗和肌肤，是暴力背后烧着的那股暖意。这一个，哪样都不是。她也许能替你赢得战斗，但她不是你的朋友。”

column1: The dead cannot be assuaged, but to you, I shall attempt to make amends. I am bound no longer, and I'll dare not subject myself to such bonds again, but I will bequeath this island to you, and for a time, I shall stir the seas to your favor.
column2: “死者无法安抚，但对你，我愿试着弥补。我不再受缚，也不敢再让自己套上那样的束缚，但我会把这座岛遗赠给你，并且在一段时间里，为你搅动大海。”

column1: The men I brought were skilled individually, but there was no bond of trust between us, and Leviathan tossed us aside easily. I wish Luc and Fastad had been here. I always felt like the three of us could accomplish anything together.
column2: “我带来的那些人各自都有本事，可我们之间没有信任的纽带，Leviathan 轻易就把我们甩开了。真希望 Luc 和 Fastad 当时在场。我一直觉得，我们三个在一起什么都办得到。”

column1: This is a divine beast? What a bitter disappointment. I'll slay this one no different than a thousand others I've slain.
column2: “这就是神兽？真是苦涩的失望。杀这一只，和我杀过的另外一千只没什么两样。”

column1: This one'll be a story for the kids I'll never get to have! The day Daddy took down the biggest boss of the sea!
column2: “这会成为我这辈子也生不出来的孩子们的故事！爸爸打倒海里最大的头目那天！”

column1: Ugh, are you still dragging that thing around? You know that zombies are supposed to be temporary, right? It stinks, and you should get rid of it. Though, come to think of it, bringing it in here probably will be getting rid of it, so... good job!
column2: “呃，你还拖着那东西？你知道僵尸应该是临时的，对吧？它发臭，你该把它处理掉。不过转念一想，把它带进来大概就是在处理掉它，所以……干得好！”

column1: Well damn, that's a big boy. How many steaks you think we'll get out of that?
column2: “该死，这家伙可真大。你觉得能从他身上割出多少块牛排？”

column1: Well shit, he definitely looks like he lifts. I suppose pulling against divine chains for centuries will do that to a guy.
column2: “我操，他看着确实像天天举铁。我猜对着圣链拉了几百年，谁都会练成这样。”

column1: Well this is disappointing. A common burglar. He does have an uncommonly nice body though, so I suppose I can't fault you for wanting him along, but you might have done better to let the pretty ones wait outside while you take care of the real work. It would be a shame if he ends up broken. You might want to use him later.
column2: “嗯，真让人失望。一个普通的入室窃贼。不过他的身子倒是少见地好，所以你想带上他，我想也不能怪你，可你也许该让这些好看的在外面等着，自己去干真正的活。他要是被弄坏了就太可惜。你以后也许还想用他。”

column1: Well, win or lose it's been quite a trip. I'd really prefer win though, so sorry big guy, but you're going down!
column2: “好吧，赢也好输也好，这一趟可真够意思。不过我实在更想赢，所以抱歉了，大家伙，你要倒下了！”

column1: What a brutal disappointment. That brand you wear is a pale shade next to the crime you have just committed. Is mercy truly so far outside of your understanding?
column2: “多么残酷的失望。你身上那道烙印，比起你刚刚犯下的罪，简直淡得不值一提。仁慈真的如此远在你的理解之外吗？”

column1: What a perverted destination this road holds. I wanted to keep decent people safe, and now I must war against a creature of God? Heaven help us all.
column2: “这条路通向的终点何等扭曲。我想保护正派的人，现在却必须与上帝的造物开战？愿上天帮助我们所有人。”

column1: While I approve of giants in general, you could've chosen one more battle-minded. Leviathan is not some towering oak to be felled by the hands of a scruffy, overmuscled labourer, though that does conjure an interesting mental picture. You'd best be sure his axe is sharp enough, or you'll fall beside him.
column2: “巨人我大体是赞成的，可你本可以选一个更一心想打仗的。Leviathan 不是一棵高耸的橡树，能被一个邋遢、肌肉鼓胀的苦力亲手放倒，尽管那画面想起来倒挺有意思。你最好确认他的斧子够锋利，不然你会倒在他旁边。”

column1: Who has more rage at the servants of god than a cursed child of blood and darkness? The bitter unfairness of it all must be positively bursting inside his cold, dead chest. If he survives this, he'll probably fancy himself the most powerful vampire on the island. Maybe he'll even be right.
column2: “对神的仆从，还有谁比一个被诅咒的血与黑暗之子更有怒火？这一切苦涩的不公，一定正在他那冰冷的、死掉的胸腔里炸开。他若能活过这一关，大概会自以为是岛上最强的吸血鬼。也许他还真说对了。”

column1: Why did I let you drag me into this? I should've just found somewhere warm and dry and... well it's too late for that, I guess. Let's get this over with.
column2: “我为什么要让你把我拖进这摊事？我本该找个又暖又干的地方，然后……好吧，现在说这个太晚了，我想。咱们把这事了结吧。”

column1: Yes, that's right, my Leviathan. Breathe out your rage and relax. You must be so very tired.
column2: “对，就是这样，我的 Leviathan。把怒火呼出去，放松。你一定已经累极了。”

column1: You know, he's curiously attractive for a fish man. Wasn't expecting that. Too bad about the whole murderous rage thing, that really makes it hard to focus on the positives. Sorry, pops.
column2: “你知道吗，作为鱼人，他出奇地诱人。没想到。可惜那一整套杀戮狂怒，实在让人很难盯着优点看。抱歉了，老爹。”

column1: You're really pulling out all the stops by bringing the werewolf, aren't you? He's certainly got spit and rage enough, and I can well-appreciate a man whose body betrays his love of base indulgence. Hopefully your victory is more important than his own pleasure in this case.
column2: “你把狼人都带来了，真是手段用尽了，是不是？他那股冲劲和怒火倒是够足，而一个身体出卖了自己对低级纵欲之爱的男人，我也相当欣赏。希望这一次，你的胜利比他自己的快感更要紧。”

column1: You're the one who denies me the open sea, denies me my freedom! No more, beast! Today we are taking it back!
column2: “就是你不让我去开阔的大海，不给我自由！到此为止，野兽！今天我们把它夺回来！”

column1: You, who sundered my chains. Come and stand before me. You've nothing to fear.
column2: “你，斩断我锁链的人。过来，站到我面前。你没什么好怕的。”

column1: Your companions can't see me or hear me, but that is a choice rather than a limitation. I understand that making a deal with a devil is something one might wish to keep... private. Let's see who you've decided to bring along.
column2: “你的同伴看不见我，也听不见我，但那是选择，不是限制。我明白，与魔鬼做交易这种事，人也许希望保持……私密。让我看看你决定带了谁来。”

column1: Your quest is mine, Max. I will see this made right, and then I will see you put to rest. Wait for me.
column2: “你的使命就是我的使命，Max。我会看着这件事被纠正，然后看着你安息。等我。”

column1: Blood for Power
column2: “以血换力量”

column1: ... I mean...
A favor?
column2: “帮个忙？”

column1: And I don't want to.
column2: “而且我不想。”

column1: Anyway, what's this about Leftie? Has he been bothering you?
column2: “总之，Leftie 是怎么回事？他一直在烦你吗？”

column1: But I can see that I'm going to change my mind, so do it anyway.
column2: “可我看得出自己会改主意，所以还是做吧。”

column1: Do me a favor, Vankan?
column2: “帮我个忙，Vankan？”

column1: Do you think I should tell him?
column2: “你觉得我该告诉他吗？”

column1: Don't want to? It's your fault for putting the idea in my head.
column2: “不想？怪你自己把这念头塞进我脑子里。”

column1: Good, you came. I really, really need-
column2: “好，你来了。我真的、真的需要——”

column1: He told me that night he committed buggery, rape, two murders, arson, and cannibalism. It was really hard for him to say it all.
column2: “他告诉我，那天夜里他犯了鸡奸、强奸、两起谋杀、纵火，还有食人。他要把这些全都说出来，真的很难。”

column1: Here I am.
column2: “我来了。”

column1: His memory of that night is fragmented, incomplete, and patched with lazy guesses. He believes himself a horror so that he has someone close by to blame. To do otherwise would nurture a helpless rage, and of that he is more afraid.
column2: “他对那一夜的记忆支离破碎，并不完整，还用偷懒的猜测补上了洞。他相信自己是个恐怖的人，这样身边就有个可以责怪的人。若不如此，只会养成一种无助的狂怒，而他更怕的是那个。”

column1: I cannot help but notice. And there is more, besides.
column2: “我没法不注意到。而且除此之外，还有更多。”

column1: I cannot say for certain what occurred there, but I am confident that only a single life was taken by his hand that night. The other life was taken by the woman. I suspect that some of the other details are wrong as well.
column2: “我不能确定那里究竟发生了什么，但我有把握，那一夜死在他手里的只有一条命。另一条命是那个女人取走的。我怀疑其他一些细节也不对。”

column1: I do apologize if my letter gave you the wrong idea.
column2: “若我的信让你产生了误会，我确实道歉。”

column1: I don't really know. I just know that I was supposed to meet with you tonight, and we were meant to talk about Leftie. It feels like we've accomplished something, so perhaps that's it.
column2: “我其实并不知道。我只知道今晚该来见你，我们该谈谈 Leftie。感觉像是我们已经做成了什么，也许就是这样。”

column1: I don't see...
column2: “我看不见……”

column1: I just thought that note meant that you wanted to...
column2: “我只是以为那张条子的意思是你想……”

column1: I know that he told you about the person he killed, and he thinks about it almost constantly.
column2: “我知道他把自己杀的那个人告诉了你，而且他几乎时时刻刻都在想这件事。”

column1: I may not see everything, but what I see is the truth. Pray, what else did he say?
column2: “我也许看不见全部，但我看见的是真相。请问，他还说了什么？”

column1: I really need to talk to you about Leftie.
column2: “我真的需要跟你谈谈 Leftie。”

column1: I see.
column2: “我明白了。”

column1: I understand that you've become quite fond of clandestine encounters. You should come and find me when you wake.
column2: “我知道你已经相当喜欢秘密幽会了。你醒来的时候，应该来找我。”

column1: I'm going back to bed. Thanks for the information.
column2: “我回去睡觉了。谢谢你告诉我这些。”

column1: It's Leftie's business, but if you've already got half of the picture...
column2: “这是 Leftie 的事，不过你既然已经知道了一半……”

column1: It's fine, Vankan. I was jumping to conclusions.
column2: “没关系，Vankan。是我妄下结论了。”

column1: More? What do you mean?
column2: “还有？什么意思？”

column1: Nobody else will come this way tonight. We should be fine.
column2: “今晚不会再有别人从这边来。我们应该没事。”

column1: Not as such. I know that the two of you shared an intimate evening, whatever that entailed. That's not really a concern of mine, but ever since then, he thinks of you often, and intensely.
column2: “也不完全是。我知道你们两个共度了一个亲密的夜晚，无论那一晚包含了什么。那其实不是我要管的，可从那以后，他常常想起你，而且想得很强烈。”

column1: Of course. I'll be along in a few minutes.
column2: “当然。我过几分钟就到。”

column1: Oh my. That's...
column2: “哦，天哪。这……”

column1: Oh no, wait, there's something...
column2: “哦不，等等，还有……”

column1: Oh!
Oh.
Rest Stop. \n\nFree for all travellers, courtesy of the Gracious Lord Frico.
column2: “歇脚处。\n\n对所有旅人免费，承蒙仁慈的 Frico 领主惠赐。”

column1: Seems clear.
column2: “看来很清楚。”

column1: So he thinks, but I assure you, he did not.
column2: “他是这么以为的，但我向你保证，他并没有。”

column1: Someday, perhaps, but not now. The visions of the madman are hardly compelling proof besides. Leftie loves you because you accepted his flaws. He doesn't need absolution, not really.
column2: “也许有一天，但不是现在。况且，疯子的幻视也算不上有力的证据。Leftie 爱你，是因为你接受了他的缺陷。他并不需要赦免，并不是真的需要。”

column1: The next hour? I'm not sure I can be that specific, but I'll try.
column2: “下一个小时？我不确定自己能具体到那个地步，但我会试试。”

column1: Try really hard to look into my future, will you? Specifically the next hour or so.
column2: “拼命看看我的未来，好吗？具体就是接下来一个小时左右。”

column1: Wait, the person? Leftie told me he killed two people.
column2: “等等，那个人？Leftie 告诉我他杀了两个人。”

column1: Well, there you have it. Make yourselves comfortable.
column2: “好了，就是这样。你们把身子放舒服。”

column1: Well, this has been interesting. That was what you wanted to talk to me about?
column2: “嗯，这倒挺有意思。你想跟我说的就是这个？”

column1: Yes! Yes. It is my fault.
column2: “是！是的。是我的错。”

column1: You seem disappointed.
column2: “你看起来很失望。”

column1: Fastad, what have you done?
column2: “Fastad，你做了什么？”

column1: Forgive me. I believe you speak the truth, and I doubt you have the answers.
column2: “原谅我。我相信你说的是真话，我也怀疑你并没有答案。”

column1: I took this place behind bars willingly, to absolve my Queen of wrongdoing, but I never expected to be chained by the stuff of time itself. It is... disconcerting.
column2: “我自愿走进铁栏之后，好洗清我的女王的罪责，却从未料到捆住我的会是时间本身。这……令人不安。”

column1: My name is Luc Beauregard, former Knight-Captain in service of Her Royal Highness Queen Glamig Cosova. I guess none of that matters anymore though. My title was stripped when I came here, and now my kingdom and my world are gone. The bastard would have been kinder to let me die forgotten, as was my lot.
column2: “我名叫 Luc Beauregard，曾是侍奉女王殿下 Glamig Cosova 的骑士队长。不过我想这些都已经无所谓了。我来到这里时，头衔就被剥掉了，如今我的王国和我的世界都已不在。那个混蛋若肯让我死去、被人遗忘，那本就是我的命，反倒更仁慈。”

column1: She is dead then. Long dead, if you are to be believed, along with Fastad and everyone else. I... why was I spared? What did that lunatic hope to accomplish by shielding me from the passage of time?
column2: “那么她死了。若你的话可信，已经死了很久，Fastad 和所有其他人也一样。我……为什么独独放过我？那个疯子把我从时间的流逝中护住，究竟想达成什么？”

column1: Still... I never did care much for giving up. Perhaps I'll venture forth to see what is left of the world I know. I'm afraid I have nothing to offer you as reward for releasing me, so I pray my thanks will suffice.
column2: “尽管如此……我向来不太喜欢放弃。也许我会出去看看，我所认识的世界还剩下什么。恐怕我没有什么可以作为释放我的酬谢给你，但愿我的感谢就够了。”

column1: Time graces ungrateful mortals with its touch everlong. How dare you presume to demand it bend to your whims! Yours is an endeavor most forbidden, and your punishment is death!
column2: “时间以其触碰，永世恩泽那些不知感恩的凡人。你竟敢妄求它屈从你的任性！你所为之事最为禁忌，你的惩罚就是死亡！”

column1: You... you are not Fastad. Who are you? What is going on? What happened to him?
column2: “你……你不是 Fastad。你是谁？这是怎么回事？他怎么样了？”

column1: A corruption from beneath the earth has come to feed on the heart of this forest, and we were not strong enough to stop it. The monks who tended the temple, and the dryads who were their friends, all have fallen.
column2: “一股来自地底的腐化前来吞噬这片森林的心脏，而我们不够强，没能阻止它。照料神殿的僧侣，以及与他们为友的树精，全都倒下了。”

column1: Begone, stranger. The temple is fallen, and there is nothing of beauty left.
column2: “退去吧，陌生人。神殿已经陷落，美丽的东西一点儿也不剩了。”

column1: Even its destruction, though, makes way for new life. The end meets the beginning, and life continues. This is the rhythm of the verdant vein.
column2: “可即便毁灭，也为新生让开了路。终结遇见开始，生命仍在继续。这就是翠绿魔脉的节律。”

column1: Foolish flower! See what your treachery has wrought!
column2: “愚蠢的花！看看你的背叛酿成了什么！”

column1: I alone was spared, and only so I could ward away travelers like you. Please, you must leave. Only the stone survives. At least this way, the corruption will spread no further.
column2: “只有我被留下，而且只是为了把你这样的旅人挡在外面。请你离开。只有石头还在。至少这样，腐化不会再蔓延。”

column1: Now suffer, as I have suffered, and perish!
column2: “现在受苦吧，如我受过的苦，然后灭亡！”

column1: Only the stone survives.
column2: “只有石头还在。”

column1: Suffer, as I have suffered, and perish!
column2: “受苦吧，如我受过的苦，然后灭亡！”

column1: Take then my first and surest seed. Hold my rhythm inside of you, and know forever the gratitude of my wood.
column2: “那么，收下我第一颗、也最稳妥的种子。把我的节律持在你体内，永远知晓我这片林木的感激。”

column1: Take what is left of my power. This forest needs it no longer.
column2: “拿走我剩下的力量。这片森林不再需要它了。”

column1: This place, this forest, it is mine! Ye who dare to challenge my stronghold are naught but dry leaves before a tide of flame!
column2: “这地方，这片森林，是我的！汝等胆敢挑战我的据点，不过是火潮面前的枯叶！”

column1: This... do you truly walk with the blessing of the mountains themselves? You then, may stand a chance. Please, destroy the corruption inside, and put an end to all those who fell to it. I will open the way for you!
