column2: “这……你真的带着群山本身的祝福在行走？那么你，也许还有机会。请毁掉里面的腐化，了结所有沦陷于它的人。我会为你打开道路！”

column1: Though I am this day fallen, your victory clears way for my seed to rise again. It will take time, but the new forest will devour this corruption as the corruption has devoured me. This is the rhythm of the verdant vein.
column2: “尽管我今日倒下，你的胜利为我的种子再度升起清开了路。这需要时间，但新的森林会吞噬这腐化，正如这腐化吞噬了我。这就是翠绿魔脉的节律。”

column1: You who have come to avenge this forest. Stand with pride before me, that I may honour your wounds as you have honored mine.
column2: “前来为这片森林复仇的你。骄傲地站到我面前，好让我荣耀你的伤口，正如你荣耀了我的。”

column1: You who have come to cleanse this blight. You seek to save this forest, but it is beyond saving.
column2: “前来净化这场枯萎的你。你想拯救这片森林，可它已经救不回来了。”

column1: Finally, I am free!
column2: “我终于自由了！”

column1: A cage. I really don't like the look of this place. We'd best finish what we need to do and move on.
column2: “一个笼子。我真不喜欢这地方看着的样子。我们最好把要做的事做完，然后走。”

column1: Anyway, thanks. I'll get out of your way.
column2: “总之，谢谢。我就不挡你的路了。”

column1: Behind you, fool! It's a trap!
column2: “在你身后，蠢货！是陷阱！”

column1: I'm Greave. Was working at the stocks for awhile, but I couldn't continue to be a part of that farce, so I left. Did alright for a week or so, until I got lured in by these damned hags. I really should've known better.
column2: “我是 Greave。在枷场干过一阵子，可我没法继续做那场闹剧的一份子，于是离开了。大约一周还过得去，直到被这些该死的巫婆骗了进来。我真该更清楚才对。”

column1: Nice bit of work, there. I am not sure how I would've got out of that one if you hadn't come along.
column2: “干得不错。你要是没来，我真不知道自己怎么能从那一关里脱身。”

column1: Ye who dare come to the heart of my coven, slaughter my sisters, and release my animals! You will surrender your eyes and your tongues in recompense!
column2: “汝等胆敢来到我集会的核心，屠戮我的姐妹，放走我的牲畜！你们要把眼睛和舌头交出来抵偿！”

column1: You... you did it! Do you think you can get me out?
column2: “你……你做到了！你觉得能把我弄出去吗？”

column1: ... eh, sorry. You live your whole life being treated like a monster and it's hard to let go of the old habits. I know we're all in this shit boat together.
column2: “……呃，抱歉。你一辈子都被当成怪物对待，旧习惯很难放下。我知道咱们都在这条屎船上。”

column1: Alright, well you work something out with the operator then, and let me know.
column2: “行吧，那你去跟操作员商量出个办法，然后告诉我。”

column1: Anyway, sorry again for snapping at you. Don't fall off a cliff.
column2: “总之，再为刚才冲你发火道歉。别从悬崖上掉下去。”

column1: At least you'd think so. Not this asswipe though. I need to cross here, but I ain't got enough coin, and he isn't willing to do a guy a favor. I been stuck here all morning trying to figure out what to do. I guess I could climb, but it seems awful dangerous.
column2: “至少你会这么想。可这个屎货偏不。我得从这儿过去，可我的钱不够，他也不肯帮人一个忙。我整个上午都卡在这儿，想该怎么办。我想我可以爬过去，可那看起来危险得要命。”

column1: Did... you hear something just now? I could've sworn I heard something.
column2: “刚才……你听见什么了吗？我发誓自己听见了什么。”

column1: Do you see that? Are... are those people over there?
column2: “你看见那个了吗？那边……那边那些是人吗？”

column1: I guess I can hardly blame you for separating beauty from danger. Probably most people would agree with you.
column2: “我想我很难怪你把美和危险分开看。大概大多数人都会同意你。”

column1: I guess some folks are like that, and I won't say it's wrong. There are certainly some people on this island who rightly deserve to get their asses kicked.
column2: “我想有些人就是那样，我也不会说那是错的。这岛上确实有些人，屁股被踢烂也是活该。”

column1: I guess you've never had to live your life in darkness then, worrying that your neighbor might flash a smile to you by day and put a torch to you by night? It kinda gives a guy a different perspective on the world.
column2: “那我猜你从来不用在黑暗里过完这一生，担心邻居白天对你笑一笑，夜里就拿火把来烧你？这多少会让一个人对世界有不一样的看法。”

column1: I know, right? Folks like us, we're better off without all these stupid rules and taboos holding us down, snuffing us out like we're not good enough to exist. Here, if you're strong and smart, you live, and if you're weak, you die. Simple.
column2: “可不是吗？像咱们这样的人，少了那些愚蠢的规矩和禁忌压着我们、把我们掐灭，好像我们不配存在，反倒更好。在这儿，你又强又聪明就活着，你弱就死。简单。”

column1: I see something moving over there. Can you make out what that is?
column2: “我看见那边有东西在动。你能看清那是什么吗？”

column1: I'm not really surprised to hear you say that. You struck me as that sort of person. I mean, you decided to help me out, when you really didn't have to, after all. That says a lot.
column2: “听你这么说，我并不怎么意外。你给我的感觉就是那种人。我是说，你毕竟决定帮我，而你其实完全不必这么做。这说明了很多。”

column1: It's funny how you can sometimes find beauty in the most deadly things, isn't it? This island certainly has no shortage of those. Deadly things, I mean. Maybe I'm crazy for being okay with that, for taking in the beauty of it when I see it.
column2: “有时候你能在最要命的东西里找出美来，挺好笑的，不是吗？这岛上那样的东西当然不缺。我是说要命的东西。也许我能接受这一点，看见的时候还去欣赏那份美，是我疯了。”

column1: It's kinda pretty from a distance, but that was magic, wasn't it? Some desperate soul slinging the very breath of the world fighting for his life, probably. It stopped, so either he's dead or his enemies are.
column2: “从远处看还挺漂亮，可那是魔法，对吧？大概是某个绝望的灵魂，甩出世界本身的吐息，在为自己的命而战。它停了，所以要么他死了，要么他的敌人死了。”

column1: Look, I ain't running a charity here. I want that guy gone, but I can't let you ride for free.
column2: “听着，我这儿可不做慈善。我是想让那家伙滚蛋，可我不能让你免费搭乘。”

column1: Nice try, but you need the full amount. Come back when your pockets are heavier.
column2: “想得美，可你得付全额。等你口袋更沉了再来。”

column1: Of course I am. Every fight, even a fight that you think you'll win, is a chance to die. If there's no need to take that chance, then why take it? Makes no sense.
column2: “我当然是。每一场战斗，哪怕是你觉得自己会赢的战斗，都是一次送死的机会。没有必要冒这个险，为什么要冒？说不通。”

column1: Oh don't look at me like that, I'm sure you would've got your ass kicked too. I mean, being tough is one thing, but you don't just throw yourself into a fight that you can avoid. It gets things done, I'll admit, but shouldn't fighting be a last resort?
column2: “哦，别用那种眼神看我，我敢说换你也会被打得屁滚尿流。我是说，硬气是一回事，可你不能往一场本可以避开的架里冲。我承认那样能把事办成，可打架不该是最后的办法吗？”

column1: Shit really? Looks like it's my lucky day! Just let me know when you've got it squared and I'll be right behind you.
column2: “我靠，真的？看来今天走运了！等你搞定了跟我说一声，我马上跟在你后面。”

column1: Shit, those things are huge! I'm glad I didn't try to make the climb, I would've got my ass kicked. I mean, I'm strong and everything, but at the end of the day, I'm still just flesh and bones.
column2: “我靠，那些东西可真大！幸好我没试着爬上去，不然得被打得屁滚尿流。我是说，我是很壮，可说到底，我终究只是一具血肉之躯。”

column1: Single gondola fits four, 100g. Not negotiable.
column2: “单座吊厢坐四人，100g。不讲价。”

column1: The lift works, and yes it's perfectly safe. It's 500$ per trip. Pay it or climb, I don't care.
column2: “升降机是好的，而且绝对安全。单程500$。给钱，或者自己爬，我无所谓。”

column1: The place isn't too bad really, though that might be coloured by my 'life as an outcast' thing. What about you? What do you think of the great and dreadful Lukatt?
column2: “这地方其实不算太糟，不过也许是我那套“流放犯的日子”把看法染了色。你呢？你觉得这伟大又可怕的卢卡特怎么样？”

column1: Well, that's just great. Thanks for nothing.
column2: “可真行啊。多谢你，什么忙都没帮上。”

column1: Well, you've been a big help. Taking that lift shaves days off my travel time, and based on some of the stuff we saw out the window, probably weeks of recovery time too. Thanks again, and try not to get killed.
column2: “嗯，你帮了大忙。坐那趟升降机能省下我好几天的路程，再看看我们从窗户看见的那些东西，大概也能省下好几个星期的养伤时间。再谢一次，尽量别送命。”

column1: Well? Are we going or ain't we?
column2: “怎样？走还是不走？”

column1: What the hell do you want? Come to gawk at the freak?
column2: “你他妈想干什么？来看怪物的？”

column1: You know, that's mighty good of you to help a guy out. Not too often you meet someone on this island willing to do that for someone they don't know.
column2: “知道吗，你肯拉人一把，心肠可真好。在这座岛上，肯为一个不认识的人这么做的，可不常见。”

column1: You're gonna get rid of that mongrel for me? Tell you what, I should charge you extra for the cleaning I'm gonna have to do later, but you're doing me a favor. Still just 500$.
column2: “你要替我把那杂种解决掉？这么说吧，我事后还得打扫，本该跟你多要钱，可你是在帮我的忙。还是只要500$。”

column1: As... statuesque as Paul is, surely he could have more consideration for the sensibilities of bystanders.
column2: “就算 Paul……身材再像座雕塑，他也该多为旁人的感受着想吧。”

column1: Bath chamber looks clear too. I think we're good.
column2: “浴室看起来也安全。我觉得没问题了。”

column1: Come give me a scrub, Perry. I'll do you too.
column2: “过来给我搓搓，Perry。我也给你搓。”

column1: Excellent.
column2: “很好。”

column1: Glad to hear it.
column2: “听你这么说真好。”

column1: Good God, I can already hear the blood rushing. I'll have a bath later. If I go in there now, I might do something I regret.
column2: “上帝啊，我已经听见血往下冲了。我晚点再洗。要是现在进去，我可能会做出让自己后悔的事。”

column1: Great, I could do with a wash-up! It was a long, sweaty march today.
column2: “太好了，我正想洗洗！今天这一路又长又出汗。”

column1: Hah! Is that so?
column2: “哈！是吗？”

column1: Have I ever mentioned how much I love this island? \nBecause I love this island.
column2: “我有没有说过我有多爱这座岛？\n因为我爱这座岛。”

column1: He's probably already trying to figure out how to get you out of your clothes, Paul.
column2: “他多半已经在想怎么把你的衣服扒下来了，Paul。”

column1: Hey Paul, look! There are five beds. We can push two of them together for you and we'll still all get to have one!
column2: “嘿，Paul，你看！这儿有五张床。我们可以把两张拼给你，剩下的我们每人还能摊到一张！”

column1: Hey boss, did you say there's a bath chamber here?
column2: “嘿，老大，你是说这儿有间浴室？”

column1: Hey boss, you said there's a bath chamber?
column2: “嘿，老大，你说过这儿有浴室？”

column1: Hey now, I can want to see what Paul is smuggling and genuinely be concerned for his comfort at the same time. Honestly, what do you people take me for?
column2: “嘿，我既可以想看看 Paul 裤裆里走私的是什么，又可以真心关心他舒不舒服。说真的，你们把我当成什么人了？”

column1: Hey you better not use up all the water! You aren't the only one who's sweaty!
column2: “嘿，你最好别把水用光！出汗的又不只你一个！”

column1: Hey, I like being naked around people too! Why the fuck do you think I'm dressed like this?
column2: “嘿，我也喜欢光着身子跟人待在一块儿！你他妈以为我穿成这样是为什么？”

column1: Hey, that sounds really hot! I wanna see!
column2: “嘿，听起来真够色的！我想看！”

column1: Hey, what about me? Logus needs a scrub too, you know!
column2: “嘿，那我呢？Logus 也得搓搓，知道吗！”

column1: Honestly, I'm surprised you haven't talked Paul out of his shorts yet.
column2: “说真的，我还奇怪你怎么还没把 Paul 的短裤给劝下来。”

column1: I ain't perfect, sure, but if you're gonna criticize me for something, at least criticize me for something I actually did.
column2: “我当然不完美，可你要挑我的错，至少挑一件我真干过的。”

column1: I could use an extra set of hands, Peregrine.
column2: “我正需要多一双手，Peregrine。”

column1: I expect you won't mind if I join you? I could definitely do with a wash as well.
column2: “我想你不会介意我一起吧？我也确实该洗洗了。”

column1: I guess that's our evening then.
column2: “那今晚就这么定了。”

column1: I have never been readier for a bath than I am at this moment.
column2: “我这辈子从没有像此刻这么想洗澡。”

column1: I love this island. So, so much.
column2: “我爱这座岛。非常、非常爱。”

column1: I need to wash my hair so badly, I no longer care if Peregrine oggles me while I do it. Perhaps Paul will keep him distracted.
column2: “我太需要洗头了，已经不在乎 Peregrine 会不会在我洗的时候色眯眯地盯着。也许 Paul 能把他的注意力引开。”

column1: I really and sincerely want to see your caber, Paul. Please!
column2: “我是真的、真心想看看你那根大木桩，Paul。求你了！”

column1: I was worried I was going to have to smell everybody all night. I like this plan better.
column2: “我还担心要闻一晚上大家身上的味。我更喜欢这个安排。”

column1: I'll wait my turn. After all, someone has to make up for the utter lack of modesty that seems to run rampant here.
column2: “我等下一轮。毕竟，这儿廉耻缺得厉害，总得有人补上。”

column1: I'm feeling a touch lightheaded.
column2: “我有点儿头晕。”

column1: I'm going to bed.
column2: “我去睡了。”

column1: I'm not the biggest fan of water lately, but even I think a bath would hit the spot right now. Wait for me, Paul! I'll help too!
column2: “我最近不怎么喜欢水，可连我都觉得这会儿洗个澡正合适。等我，Paul！我也来帮忙！”

column1: If you're not busy, of course.
column2: “当然，要是你不忙的话。”

column1: It was a long, sweaty march today and I could use a wash-up.
column2: “今天这一路又长又出汗，我得洗洗。”

column1: Looks like it, yes.
column2: “看起来是的。”

column1: Now this brings back memories! I think a bath is exactly what I need right now.
column2: “这可勾起回忆了！我觉得我现在最需要的就是洗个澡。”

column1: Oh goodness. Did I really just see that? And they're going to bathe together? On purpose?
column2: “我的天哪。我刚才真的看见了？而且他们还要一起洗澡？是故意的？”

column1: On the one hand, it would feel a bit like crashing a private party. On the other hand, this is Peregrine we're talking about. He'll be thrilled to scrub another man down, won't he?
column2: “一方面，这有点像不请自来，闯进一场私人聚会。另一方面，我们说的是 Peregrine。能给另一个男人搓澡，他肯定乐坏了，对吧？”

column1: Peregrine! Save some water for the rest of us, alright?
column2: “Peregrine！给我们留点儿水，好吗？”

column1: Right you are! Nice of you to think of me, Peregrine.
column2: “可不是！亏你还想着我，Peregrine。”

column1: See, Peregrine? Just ask the man nicely!
column2: “看见没，Peregrine？好好跟人家说就行！”

column1: Seriously, we all stink. I just hope there's enough water to go around.
column2: “说真的，我们都臭了。我只希望水够大家用。”

column1: Shit, Perry, I ain't shy. You could'a just asked.
column2: “靠，Perry，我又不害臊。你直接问不就得了。”

column1: Sleep well, gentlemen?
column2: “睡得好吗，先生们？”

column1: Sometimes, yeah. This time I didn't say anything. I was just talking about Paul having a place to sleep that isn't dirt.
column2: “有时候是。这次我什么都没说。我只是说 Paul 能有个不是泥地的地方睡。”

column1: Sure did, chief.
column2: “当然睡好了，老大。”

column1: Thanks. Fortunately for you, I'm also incredibly humble and forgiving. The very picture of a fun-and-attention-loving rogue, really.
column2: “谢了。算你们走运，我还特别谦虚，也特别能原谅人。活脱脱就是个又爱玩、又爱出风头的流氓，真的。”

column1: That's me!
column2: “就是我！”

column1: The door looks tight. With any luck it'll still be empty.
column2: “门看起来关得很严。运气好的话，里面还是空的。”

column1: The giant is particularly powerful, so if keeping Peregrine around serves to maintain him, I suppose this behaviour is worth tolerating.
column2: “那巨人特别能打，所以如果留着 Peregrine 是为了把他稳住，我想这种行为还是值得忍的。”

column1: Ugh.
We take you for our perky little pervert. Our lovable rogue and cabin boy all rolled into one!
column2: “我们把你当成我们活泼的小变态。可爱的流氓兼船上侍童，全揉在一个人身上！”

column1: We're fortunate to have the opportunity to bathe indoors.
column2: “我们能在屋里洗澡，算是走运。”

column1: Well, I for one am glad to see my boys getting along.
column2: “就我来说，看见我的小伙子们处得来，我很高兴。”

column1: Well, you know me! I'm a people person.
column2: “你知道我的！我就喜欢跟人打交道。”

column1: Well? Is it everything you hoped for?
column2: “怎样？跟你盼的一样吗？”

column1: Yes, I'm pretty sure that's what it is.
column2: “对，我挺确定就是这么回事。”

column1: You certainly are.
column2: “你当然是。”

column1: You guys don't really do the bathing together thing, do you? Humans are so weird.
column2: “你们其实不怎么一起洗澡，对吧？人类可真怪。”

column1: You're a pervert, Peregrine, and you like to announce that you're a pervert in front of all of us. Repeatedly.
column2: “你是个变态，Peregrine，而且你喜欢当着我们所有人的面宣布自己是个变态。一遍又一遍。”

column1: You're right. Sorry, Peregrine.
column2: “你说得对。对不起，Peregrine。”

column1: Anyone caught stealing supplies will be driven out. We cannot survive if we do not work together. Thank you for understanding.
column2: “凡偷拿补给者，一律驱逐。我们若不能同心协力，便无法活命。感谢理解。”

column1:
Some build bridges made of stone, 
some of wood and some of bone,
but they whose only chance has flown
may build a bridge of gold alone.
Do you twelve-thousand pieces own?
column2:
“有人用石头造桥，
有人用木头，有人用骨头，
可那唯一机会已经飞走的，
便只能独自用黄金造桥。
你可有一万二千枚金币？”

column1: Ack! Adventurers! Monsters!
column2: “哎呀！冒险者！怪物！”

column1:
It seems my welcome's overstayed,
if I've encountered mortals.
Perchance this begs a getaway?
I'll use one of my portals!
column2:
“看来这欢迎我已待得太久，
既已撞见凡人。
也许该谋一条退路？
我便用上一扇传送门！”

column1: Ouch! I-I gotta get out of here!
column2: “哎哟！我、我得离开这儿！”

column1: Lord Maxim Spartill
column2: “领主 Maxim Spartill”

column1: Adventurers. I'm going to say this once, so listen up. Go looking for trouble here, and you'll find more than you care for. Keep your weapons to yourselves, and you'll have no problems from us.
column2: “冒险者。我只说一遍，听好了。在这儿找麻烦，你们会找来自己消受不了的。武器收好，我们就不会为难你们。”

column1: Again? I don't know how you're doing it, but I'm sure you're cheating me!
column2: “又来？我不知道你是怎么做到的，可我敢肯定你在骗我！”

column1: All's quiet. Boring, but it means no one's getting hurt.
column2: “一切都平静。无聊是无聊，可这也意味着没人受伤。”

column1: Come back when you've got more money.
column2: “等你钱多了再来。”

column1: Do you make a habit of staring at naked people?
column2: “你是不是习惯盯着裸体的人看？”

column1: Do you mind? We're in the middle of something.
column2: “介意吗？我们正忙着呢。”

column1: Don't go messing with the garden, please. It's hard to keep things growing well down here.
column2: “请别去折腾花园。在这下面把东西养好可不容易。”

column1: Excuse me.
column2: “不好意思。”

column1: Have you ever heard a Saurian sing? One of the guards has a voice that sounds like... molten stone dribbling down a mountain's quaking thighs. Shame he's so self-conscious about it.
column2: “你听过蜥蜴人唱歌吗？有个守卫的嗓音听起来像……熔岩顺着大山颤抖的大腿往下淌。可惜他自己太难为情了。”

column1: Here's your meal. I really should not have done that though, so if you want more, it's straight coin, sorry!
column2: “你的饭。我其实不该那么做，所以你还想要的话，就得老实付钱，抱歉！”

column1: I don't think that centaurs are meant to dance.
column2: “我觉得半人马本来就不该跳舞。”

column1: I hate walking on these tiles. It feels like I'm going to slip.
column2: “我讨厌走这些地砖。总觉得自己要滑倒。”

column1: I really wish they'd give us a damn folding screen or something.
column2: “我真希望他们能给我们一块该死的屏风什么的。”

column1: I'll be keeping an eye on you.
column2: “我会盯着你的。”

column1: I'm not really in the mood for an encounter right now. Please keep it down.

column2: “现在，欢迎我的孩子们进入你们的身体！”

column1: There is something wrong here. Give me a moment before you touch that thing.
column2: “这儿有些不对。碰那东西之前，先给我一点时间。”

column1: You are fortunate I was here. It would have been very bad if you had opened that book. \n\nIt has been taken care of, however. Shall we move on?
column2: “幸好有我在。你要是打开了那本书，会非常糟糕。\n\n不过已经处理好了。我们继续走？”

column1: You, however, have served me well. You will be spared my hunger, and instead I offer an honoured place at my side, so you may serve me evermore!
column2: “至于你，却把我侍奉得很好。你将免于我的饥饿，我反而赐你一个在我身侧的尊位，好让你永远侍奉我！”

column1: I miss you.
column2: “我想你。”

column1: In memory of our beloved hero, Maxim Spartill
column2: “纪念我们深爱的英雄，Maxim Spartill”

column1: Maxim. You really made a name for yourself didn't you?
column2: “Maxim。你还真闯出了名头，是不是？”

column1: A moment of weakness, perhaps.
column2: “也许是一时软弱。”

column1: A strange question coming from you. Are you taking an interest in us?
column2: “这话从你嘴里问出来可真怪。你开始对我们有兴趣了？”

column1: And I suppose you'd have begrudged him having children on account of the law you love so much?
column2: “那我猜，就凭你那么热爱的法律，你也会不许他有孩子？”

column1: And what did they think of their mother getting sent out to this rock?
column2: “那他们怎么看自己的母亲被送到这块石头上来？”

column1: Are your children also half-orcs, Moria?
column2: “你的孩子也是半兽人吗，Moria？”

column1: Don't mock me, woman. I am ever mindful of ways to contribute to my master's power. Some day I may need to breed an army of warriors. Half-orcs seem a sensible choice.
column2: “别嘲讽我，女人。我时刻想着如何为我主人增添力量。有朝一日，我也许得繁育一支战士大军。半兽人似乎是个明智的选择。”

column1: He understands now. It is not easy, but he is helping his brother to understand as well.
column2: “他现在明白了。这不容易，可他也在帮他的兄弟去明白。”

column1: Hm.
How long do humans keep their children around, anyway?
column2: “人类到底要把孩子留在身边多久？”

column1: I am surprised to learn that you are a mother, Moria. You must have been a very strict parent.
column2: “没想到你是一位母亲，Moria。你当父母一定非常严厉。”

column1: I can barely keep myself alive. What the hell would I do with kids?
column2: “我自己都快活不下去。我他妈要孩子干什么？”

column1: I couldn't say. I hadn't seen them for years prior.
column2: “我说不上来。在那之前我已经很多年没见过他们了。”

column1: I do imagine that, yes.
column2: “是的，我确实这么想。”

column1: I find that hard to believe. I can't imagine a warrior like you laying down with babes!
column2: “我很难相信。我没法想象你这样的战士会跟小娃娃躺在一起！”

column1: I had an orc uncle. One of my father's friends. They used to go fishing together, and then come home and tell me absurd stories of the gigantic fish they'd seen.
column2: “我有个兽人叔叔。是我父亲的一个朋友。他们以前常一起去钓鱼，回来就跟我讲他们见过的巨鱼，荒唐得很。”

column1: I imagine your children run barefoot and hunt beasts twice their size.
column2: “我猜你的孩子光着脚乱跑，猎比自己大一倍的野兽。”

column1: I see. You know, I've never really heard you talk about yourself.
column2: “这样啊。说起来，我几乎没听你谈过你自己。”

column1: I take it this doesn't bother you, then?
column2: “这么说，这事并不困扰你？”

column1: I understand it is rare for orc boys to know their fathers.
column2: “我知道，兽人男孩很少认得自己的父亲。”

column1: I wonder how long ago this was. I don't smell any traces of anybody but us, so it must've been a very long time ago.
column2: “不知道这是多久以前的事了。除了我们，我闻不到任何人的痕迹，所以一定是很久很久以前。”

column1: I wonder what my dad was like.
column2: “不知道我爸是什么样的人。”

column1: I would have, yes, but that was a long time ago. You might imagine that I have a somewhat different view of the law now.
column2: “是的，我会，但那是很久以前了。你大概能想到，我现在对法律的看法已经不太一样了。”

column1: I'm pretty sure I can't have kids. Either that, or I'm lucky, and I know damn well that I'm not lucky.
column2: “我很确定我没法有孩子。不然就是我走运了，而我他妈很清楚自己不走运。”

column1: I.. um... I suppose that's true.
column2: “我……呃……我想这倒是真的。”

column1: I... see. Thank you.
column2: “我……明白了。谢谢你。”

column1: In any case, being reminded of my sons does not require your belief.
column2: “反正，我想起我的儿子，并不需要你相信。”

column1: Is it? You don't really know me at all.
column2: “是吗？你根本不怎么了解我。”

column1: It's good that you remember him. It's part of what keeps you human.
column2: “你还记得他，这很好。这也是让你还没丢掉人性的一部分。”

column1: It's just about unheard of, actually. No sense worrying about it, I guess.
column2: “其实几乎闻所未闻。我想，操心这个也没什么用。”

column1: It's unbecoming of warriors to stand around and wax nostalgic over children, isn't it?
column2: “战士站在这儿怀念孩子，可不像样，不是吗？”

column1: May I speak, Moria?
column2: “我可以说句话吗，Moria？”

column1: Mom must've been a talented woman if Dad's face really looked like that! Look at the size of that grin!
column2: “要是爸的脸真长那样，妈一定是个有本事的女人！你看那笑容多大！”

column1: Most of the time orc men don't get to be dads. Those were some lucky kids. Look how happy they are.
column2: “兽人男人大多当不成爹。那些孩子真走运。你看他们多高兴。”

column1: Must everything always be about sex for you?
column2: “你就非得把什么都扯到性上吗？”

column1: My papa was like that too. Big nasty swamp hog with a broken smile and mead in his veins.
column2: “我老爸也那样。一头又大又恶心的沼泽野猪，笑容是破的，血管里流的是蜜酒。”

column1: My sons left my care when my eldest was twelve. His brother was ten.
column2: “我的儿子们离开我的时候，长子十二岁。他弟弟十岁。”

column1: Nah. Kids are great. Doesn't hurt to remember that.
column2: “才没有。孩子挺好的。记住这个又没坏处。”

column1: No, though I did entertain the thought. I would have been pleased to raise such a strong-blooded child.
column2: “没有，不过我确实想过。养一个血脉这么强的孩子，我会很高兴。”

column1: No. I raised them to be strong and to survive. My part is done.
column2: “不。我把他们养得强壮，能活下去。我的份尽了。”

column1: Oh wow, you had kids? That's nuts!
column2: “哇，你有过孩子？太离谱了！”

column1: Perhaps they do.
column2: “也许他们会。”

column1: That must be hard being away from your family.
column2: “离开家人一定很难受。”

column1: That's a... well I suppose it's a very practical perspective.
column2: “这……嗯，我想这倒是个很实际的看法。”

column1: That's so cute! You can tell by the way this was drawn that this kid thought his dad was a hero.
column2: “太可爱了！从这画法就能看出来，这孩子觉得他爸是个英雄。”

column1: The world is cruel, and will punish those who fail with starvation and death. I was considerably less strict than that.
column2: “世界是残酷的，会用饥饿和死亡惩罚失败者。我可比那宽松多了。”

column1: Then you haven't a very good imagination. Who do you think raises those babes to be warriors?
column2: “那是你想象力不行。你以为是谁把那些娃娃养成战士的？”

column1: They look happy, don't they? My children never did such things.
column2: “他们看着很开心，不是吗？我的孩子从没做过这种事。”

column1: Twelve years?! Crap, is that how long it takes you guys to get that tall? I don't know how old I am exactly but I can't be more than... maybe eight? And I'm old for a goblin.
column2: “十二年？！靠，你们要长那么高得花这么久？我不知道自己确切几岁，但最多……大概八岁？而且我在哥布林里已经算老的了。”

column1: Two sons, yes. They would be nearly grown by now.
column2: “两个儿子，对。他们现在该差不多成年了。”

column1: Useless rules writ by useless fools. 'Tis no country of mine.
column2: “无用的蠢货写下的无用规矩。这不是我的国家。”

column1: Well, you're very mature for an eight year old, Borfalgor.
column2: “嗯，以八岁来说，你相当成熟，Borfalgor。”

column1: What was that, Moria? I couldn't hear you over the sound of thinking about sex.
column2: “你说什么，Moria？我想着做爱的动静太大，没听见。”

column1: Why wouldn't all human women choose orc husbands? They are undeniably superior mates.
column2: “人类女人为什么不都选兽人当丈夫？他们毫无疑问是更优越的配偶。”

column1: Yeah.
column2: “是啊。”

column1: You are too easily impressed, Rosaline. Even animals can raise children.
column2: “你太容易被打动了，Rosaline。连动物都会养孩子。”

column1: You don't need my permission to speak, Vankan. Do whatever you wish.
column2: “你说话不用我准，Vankan。随你便。”

column1: You have children? Goodness, that's a surprise.
column2: “你有孩子？天哪，真想不到。”

column1: You've got children?
column2: “你有孩子？”

column1: Your countries have punishments for bearing half-orc children, don't they? I remember it happening a lot in my time.
column2: “你们的国家会惩罚生下半兽人孩子的人，对吧？我记得我那个年代这种事很多。”

column1: Anybody else smell that? It reminds me of an old lady trying to cover an infection with perfume. Keep an eye out.
column2: “还有人闻到了吗？像个老太婆想用香水盖住感染的伤口。留点神。”

column1: Byrne, are you alright? You seem bothered.
column2: “Byrne，你还好吗？你看起来有心事。”

column1: Guess there's not a lot to do when you're surrounded with nothing but workmen and trees, huh?
column2: “四周除了工人和树什么都没有的时候，大概也没什么别的可干，对吧？”

column1: He took us all by surprise, Byrne. Don't beat yourself up over it.
column2: “他打了我们所有人一个措手不及，Byrne。别为这事太自责。”

column1: Just a heads up, I smell flowers, and I smell it way too strong for it to just be regular flowers. Keep your eyes peeled.
column2: “先提醒一句，我闻到花香，而且香得过分，绝不是普通的花。把眼睛睁大。”

column1: Looks like a woodcutter's competition. Used to see a lot of these back in the days when the forest was more widely worked, or so I'm told.
column2: “像是一场伐木比赛。听说从前这片林子采伐得更广的时候，这种比赛很常见。反正别人是这么跟我说的。”

column1: Oh, I'm thinking of beating up a very specific someone over it, and it ain't me.
column2: “哦，我正想为这事揍一个很具体的人，而且那个人不是我。”

column1: Someone really jammed that in there. I wonder if it's still any good?
column2: “有人可真把它死死塞进去了。不知道还能不能用？”

column1: Sorry. I'm still thinking about Vankan. I can't believe that bastard would betray us.
column2: “抱歉。我还在想 Vankan。真不敢相信那混蛋会背叛我们。”

column1: Figured this place would be my grave. I guess I'm lucky you found me before some hungry animal did.
column2: “我本来以为这地方就是我的坟。算我走运，找到我的是你，不是哪只饿慌的动物。”

column1: I came looking for something... I don't remember. Just being too curious for my own good, maybe. Big guy grabs me from the darkness. I manage to get out of his grip and run back out, but I'm all the way outside before I realize he snatched the amulet.
column2: “我来找个东西……不记得了。也许就是好奇心太重，害了自己。黑暗里一个大块头抓住我。我挣开他跑了出去，可跑到外面才发现，他把护符抢走了。”

column1: I have nothing to offer you except for my thanks. I hope that you found something valuable inside, at least.
column2: “除了感谢，我没什么能给你的。至少希望你在里面找到了值钱的东西。”

column1: My name is Borfalgor. Surprised to see a goblin using proper speech? Can't say I blame you. That's part of what the amulet is for, I think. I don't really understand it, but without the amulet, I get stupid, and I get weak, and I probably die.
column2: “我叫 Borfalgor。看见哥布林说这么像样的话，吃惊了？我也怪不得你。我想护符的用处有一部分就在这儿。我并不真懂，可没有护符，我会变蠢，会变弱，大概还会死。”

column1: You're very kind. Thank you. I'll be fine in a moment.
column2: “你人真好。谢谢。我一会儿就没事。”

column1: I will watch as you suffer and die.
column2: “我会看着你痛苦地死去。”

column1: The color of blood is pleasing to my eyes.
column2: “鲜血的颜色令我悦目。”

column1: Come, then.
column2: “那就来吧。”

column1: I have slumbered here in peace for decades undisturbed by man or beast, the darkness holding back any who might dare enter.
column2: “我在此安睡数十年，人兽不来打扰，黑暗挡下一切胆敢进来的。”

column1: Now you presume your own invitation, intruding thus upon my home. I am awakened early, and my wrath stirs!
column2: “如今你竟不请自来，如此闯入我的居所。我被提前唤醒，怒意也随之翻涌！”

column1: Still, my heart desires a brief distraction, and perhaps more sleep thereafter.
column2: “不过，我仍想要一点短暂的消遣，之后或许再睡。”

column1: Then I shall sate my hunger with blood!
column2: “那我就以鲜血饱餐！”

column1: You, who leads the others! Offer yourself upon the bed. The others will wait outside. Ply my mood with thy flesh, and I shall let you leave in peace.
column2: “你，领着其他人的那个！把自己献到床上。其余的人在外面等。用你的肉体来取悦我，我便放你平安离开。”

column1: Build the kingdom for me and bask in its infant glory. Surely this is acceptable.
column2: “为我建起王国，沐浴在它初生的荣光里。这总该可以接受吧。”

column1: Go, meet with The Sunken One, and when he tries to destroy you, destroy instead the chains that bind him. Release his anchors, and I will treat with him myself.
column2: “去，去见沉没者。当他要毁灭你的时候，你转而去毁掉束缚他的锁链。解开他的锚，我自会与他交涉。”

column1: He will not let you leave. He will never let you leave, and you will never be able to make him understand.
column2: “他不会放你走。他永远不会放你走，你也永远没法让他明白。”

column1: I am not interested in talking, Mortal. If you're here for the party, then enter the palace and present yourself to Lord Barrod.
column2: “我对谈话没兴趣，凡人。你若是来赴宴的，就进宫殿，去面见 Barrod 领主。”

column1: I shall watch your battles from afar. If you decide to accept my offer, simply strike the chains. When they shatter, that will mark the signing of our contract. Simple, no?
column2: “我会从远处看着你的战斗。你若决定接受我的提议，只需击打那些锁链。它们碎裂之时，便是我们签约之时。很简单，不是吗？”

column1: I, however, can. My bargain for you is this.
column2: “我却可以。我与你的交易是这样。”

column1: Keep your distance, Mortal. I have no interest in harming you.
column2: “保持距离，凡人。我无意伤害你。”

column1: Now leave.
column2: “现在离开。”

column1: Soon, you will come up against something tremendous. Perhaps you know this already.
column2: “很快，你会撞上某个了不得的东西。也许你已经知道了。”

column1: The Commanding Oak
column2: “号令橡木”

column1: The Sunken One will protect this island in your name for five-hundred years, and you will owe him nothing. No sacrifices, and no rituals. In return, I shall appear at the end of those five-hundred years to claim the island's crown for myself.
column2: “沉没者将以你的名义守护这座岛五百年，而你什么都不欠他。没有献祭，也没有仪式。作为回报，那五百年结束时我会现身，亲自来取这座岛的王冠。”

column1: The Sunken One, he is like I am, a being that exists outside of the mortal space, but he is bound to it by great divine chains. These chains are his anchor, and his torment, and it is this torment that spurs his rage, causing him to lash out at you.
column2: “沉没者跟我一样，存在于凡俗空间之外，却被巨大的神圣锁链束缚其中。这些锁链是他的锚，也是他的折磨，正是这折磨激起他的狂怒，使他向你出手。”

column1: There are some others up on the eyrie, but I'll brook no nonsense in the archive. Through one door or another, leave.
column2: “上面的鹰巢还有几个，但档案室里我不许胡闹。从哪扇门走都行，离开。”

column1: Time to discuss your business, yes? Very well.
column2: “是时候谈你的事了，对吧？很好。”

column1: Welcome, Mortal, to my domain. I am Lord Barrod. Time is irrelevant here, so please make yourself at home and enjoy the party. Come and find me when you have had your fill of pleasure, and we shall discuss business.
column2: “欢迎来到我的领地，凡人。我是 Barrod 领主。这里时间毫无意义，请随意，享受宴会。等你把欢愉享受够了，再来找我，我们谈正事。”

column1: You don't want to be here, Love. This party ain't even been started yet, haw.
column2: “你不该待在这儿，亲爱的。这宴会还压根没开始呢，哈。”

column1: You need not decide now. You cannot, after all, break the divine chains without my blessing.
column2: “你不必现在决定。毕竟没有我的赐福，你也打破不了那些神圣锁链。”

column1: You will gain absolute control over the island, and you shall become its ruler. This I promise.
column2: “你将完全掌控这座岛，并成为它的统治者。我以此为诺。”

column1: Filthy swine!! What do you think you're doing here!?
column2: “肮脏的猪！！你以为你在这儿干什么！？”

column1: A dirty story, hmm?
column2: “一个下流故事，嗯？”

column1: All that work, and then all the pressure to plant a girl in her, I don't need it! Why anyone would long for port when his sailors are beside him at sea is beyond me.
column2: “费那么大劲，还得扛着往她肚子里种个女儿的压力，我才不需要！水手就在海上陪着他，谁还巴望着靠港，我是想不通。”

column1: Alright, I'm in. What do I have to do?
column2: “行，我加入。我得干什么？”

column1: Alright, Peregrine, that was my drink. My last drink. How many do you've left?
column2: “行啊，Peregrine，那是我的酒。我最后一杯。你还剩几杯？”

column1: And what happens if I run out of whiskey?
column2: “那要是我把威士忌喝光了呢？”

column1: And when I have the coin, I flip it, and you do the same?
column2: “等硬币到我手里，换我来抛，你也照样？”

column1: Aye, one moment.
column2: “好，等一下。”

column1: Before we came into port, we cracked open that barrel and we all took turns pumping our sweet nectar into it before sealing it back up, pretty as you please.
column2: “进港之前，我们把那桶撬开，大家轮流把甜汁射进去，再封得漂漂亮亮。”

column1: Captain! The game isn't - wow, Logus, your body is really - looking like a good body right now.
column2: “船长！这游戏可不是——哇，Logus，你这身子真是——现在看着可真是副好身子。”

column1: Captain, I could kiss you. Malkie is the one who got me shipped out here. Now, thinking about him with a belly full of sour sailors' pickles makes it all worth it.
column2: “船长，我真想亲你。是 Malkie 把我弄上船、送到这儿的。现在一想到他肚子里灌满水手的酸黄瓜，一切都值了。”

column1: Dammit! After a story like that, I'm gonna have to really step it up.
column2: “该死！听了这么个故事，我可得好好加把劲了。”

column1: Did you hear something?
column2: “你听见什么了吗？”

column1: Didn't you wonder why none of my stories had comely maidens or busty wenches? Logus has never been pretty enough to even think about earning a wife, an' honestly, I couldn't be bothered.
column2: “你就没想过，为什么我的故事里没有俊俏姑娘，也没有大奶子的娘们？Logus 从来就没漂亮到配去想着娶老婆，而且老实说，我也懒得费那个心。”

column1: Don't worry about it. We all act like cunts from time to time. Isn't that right, Logus?
column2: “别放在心上。我们谁都有犯贱的时候。对吧，Logus？”

column1: Fine, I'll trust you.
column2: “行，我信你。”

column1: Forget the coin. Finish your drink and drive me aground.
column2: “别管硬币了。喝完你的酒，把我撞上岸。”

column1: Glad to hear it. And by the way, I'm sorry I was such an asshole yesterday. I shouldn't offload my foul mood onto my friends. Forgive me.
column2: “听到这话真好。还有，抱歉，我昨天那么傻逼。不该把烂心情甩到朋友身上。原谅我。”

column1: Great. Time to bar the doors and hit the sack. I can't stay awake another minute.
column2: “很好。该把门关死睡觉了。我一分钟也撑不住了。”

column1: Hah! Wrong!

column1: Perfect. I'll break in through the upper level and then open the door from the inside. Won't be a hot minute.
column2: “好极了。我从上层破进去，再从里面把门打开。很快就好。”

column1: Still, it's been a very long time since I've had a decent conversation. I suppose you'll have to do.
column2: “不过，我已经很久没有过一场像样的谈话了。只好将就你了。”

column1: Such things I will do with you! I will brew within you a hatred so distilled, so pure, my loins ache at the very thought!
column2: “我要对你做的那些事！我要在你体内酿出一种浓到极致、纯到极致的恨，光是想想，我的胯就发疼！”

column1: This place is practically begging to be broken into. I could get us up to the balcony from here, no problem.
column2: “这地方简直在求人闯进去。我可以从这儿把我们弄上阳台，没问题。”

column1: Tsk. This place is practically begging to be robbed.
column2: “啧。这地方简直在求人来偷。”

column1: Uh oh.
column2: “糟了。”

column1: Well, how about it? Ready to break in?
column2: “怎么样？准备好闯进去了吗？”

column1: What's this? Someone come to my home without so much as introducing himself?
column2: “这是怎么回事？有人进了我的家，连个名都不报？”

column1: What? You can't!
column2: “什么？你不能！”

column1: You there, dullard. I trust your small ambitions will be satisfied with coin? Take 5000$ and leave. I will be keeping Peregrine, of course.
column2: “你，蠢货。我想你那点小小的野心，用钱就能满足吧？拿上5000$，离开。Peregrine 我当然要留下。”

column1: Alright. Everybody keep your eyes peeled.
column2: “好。大家都把眼睛放亮。”

column1: Astounding! Can you feel that?
column2: “惊人！你感觉到了吗？”

column1: He was a clever man, and a good friend. Perhaps something useful can be found here.
column2: “他是个聪明人，也是个好朋友。也许这里能找到些有用的东西。”

column1: He was the last person I saw before meeting you, in fact. He came to the oubliette and... whatever he did, I suppose, is what spared me from the island's fate.
column2: “事实上，遇见你之前，他是我见到的最后一个人。他来到地牢，然后……不管他做了什么，我想，正是那件事让我逃过了这岛的命运。”

column1: I don't know what waits within, but whatever it is, we should take it very seriously.
column2: “我不知道里面等着什么，可不管是什么，我们都该非常认真对待。”

column1: I haven't been able to secure nearly enough blackglass, however, and I don't think that I could find a suitably-skilled craftsman in this social climate. Blast my luck.
column2: “可我弄到的黑玻璃远远不够，而且照这世道，我也找不着技艺够格的工匠。真是倒霉。”

column1: I must advise caution. We have no idea what this device is or what its purpose is. Damaging it or even activating it could prove disastrous!
column2: “我必须劝你谨慎。我们完全不知道这装置是什么，也不知道它是干什么的。损坏它，甚至启动它，都可能酿成大祸！”

column1: I understand that we have few options, but I have a very bad feeling about this.
column2: “我知道我们没什么选择，可我对这件事感觉非常不好。”

column1: If it fails, I suspect that an eternity adrift the sea of stars awaits me. We shall see if I tire of the view. I pray that Maxim renders my efforts unnecessary.
column2: “若是失败，等待我的大概是在星海中漂流的永恒。且看我会不会厌倦那番景色。我祈祷 Maxim 能让我的努力变得没有必要。”

column1: My recommendation is that we begin careful study and experimentation immediately. This is surely important.
column2: “我的建议是立刻开始谨慎的研究与试验。这东西肯定重要。”

column1: The lattice is laid out. All that remains is to assemble the fetish and to weave the proper energy around it.
column2: “晶格已经布好。剩下的，只是把巫偶组装起来，再在它周围编织恰当的能量。”

column1: The veins here are wide open, positively rushing through this room!
column2: “这里的魔脉大开着，简直在这房间里奔涌！”

column1: There is no more time. I shall have to attempt the ritual shorthanded. If this succeeds, then I hope to strike a bargain with a being great enough to save us.
column2: “没有时间了。我只好在人手不足的情况下尝试这个仪式。若能成功，我希望与一个强大到足以拯救我们的存在做一笔交易。”

column1: This is Fastad's private study. I was here only once before.
column2: “这是 Fastad 的私人书房。我以前只来过一次。”

column1: This is important! Whoever this Fastad was, he began something here, something that has waited out the centuries for you to find it.
column2: “这很重要！不管这个 Fastad 是谁，他在这里起了个头，一件熬过许多世纪、等着你来发现的事。”

column1: This place has a familiar odour. I suspect that whatever its purpose, it draws at least some of its energy from the powers of hell.
column2: “这地方有股熟悉的气味。我怀疑不管它目的何在，它至少有一部分能量取自地狱的力量。”

column1: This place!
column2: “这地方！”

column1: Whatever this is, it's meant to channel an incredible magnitude of power, and the veins have been cultivated to provide it.
column2: “不管这是什么，它都是用来引导极其庞大的能量的，而魔脉被培育起来，就是为了供给它。”

column1: You are surely powerful enough to manage this, whatever its purpose. Seize this too, and turn it to your glory!
column2: “不管它目的何在，你肯定强大到足以驾驭。把这个也夺过来，化为你的荣光！”

column1: Ferris Market Tavern. Open mornings and afternoons - all welcome!
column2: “费里斯市场酒馆。上午与下午营业——欢迎所有人！”

column1: My contract here has long expired, and I am no longer compelled by mortal writ to consume the dead.
column2: “我在此地的契约早已期满，凡间的文书也不再强迫我吞食死者。”

column1: No, this time, I shall sample the succulent pain of the still-living! Come, morsels, dress yourselves in agony! My feast awaits!
column2: “不，这一次，我要品尝仍活着的人那鲜美的痛苦！来吧，小肉块们，把痛苦披在身上！我的盛宴正等着！”

column1: Please do not climb the fence.
column2: “请勿攀爬围栏。”

column1: Repeat offenders will undergo corporal punishment.\\r Resisting arrest, or demonstrating any degree of violence, is punishable by death.
column2: “累犯将受体罚。\\r 拒捕，或表现出任何程度的暴力，处以死刑。”

column1: Restricted access.
column2: “限制进入。”

column2: “凡在城墙之内行窃、施展魔法，或出售危险物质与爆炸物者，一经抓获，立即当众处决。”

column1: Those caught trading on Market Street after dusk, or without a valid permit, shall have their assets confiscated and will be imprisoned for an undisclosed amount of time.
column2: “凡于黄昏之后，或未持有效许可，在 Market Street 交易而被抓获者，财产没收，并监禁一段不予公开的时间。”

column1: Visiting hours are currently suspended.
column2: “探视时间现已暂停。”

column1: Welcome to Ferris Market Town Hall. Please inquire inside for trading permits.
column2: “欢迎来到费里斯市场市政厅。交易许可请入内询问。”

column1: You come and offer me violence, but you know nothing of violence.
column2: “你来向我施暴，可你对暴力一无所知。”

column1: Come with me.
column2: “跟我来。”

column1: So this is it. Time to get off this rock and never come back.
column2: “就是这一刻了。该离开这块破石头，再也不回来了。”

column1: Something happen on the way, did it? We can't leave without twenty strong, so find replacements for your casualties, and don't keep me waiting.
column2: “路上出了事，是吧？不满二十个人，我们不能走。把折损的人补上，别让我干等。”

column1: ...they mentioned something about selling me as a concubine.
column2: “……他们提过要把我当妾卖掉。”

column1: ...they want to sell me to a gorgon.
column2: “……他们想把我卖给一个蛇发女妖。”

column1: Agreed.
column2: “同意。”

column1: And I swear, if Kirilo gets to see Shapiro's goods before I do, I'm gonna kick his green ass too.
column2: “而且我发誓，Kirilo 要是比我先看到 Shapiro 的私货，我连他那绿屁股也要踹。”

column1: And I wager you've a warmer embrace than the gorgon I'm to be sold to.
column2: “而且我打赌，你的怀抱比那个要买我的蛇发女妖暖和。”

column1: Are you guys alright?
column2: “你们没事吧？”

column1: Bloody poison!
column2: “该死的毒药！”

column1: Crap.
Do you think we're gonna die here, Ro?

column1: Gah! God damned insects.

column1: Hmm. Not bad. If the inside is holding up as well as the outside, it should be a decent shelter.
column2: “嗯。不错。里面要是跟外面一样撑得住，倒是个像样的落脚处。”

column1: Hopefully the boss got your message.
column2: “希望头目收到了你的消息。”

column1: I am so lonely. Afore this marriage, I could at least convince a wench to warm my bed with a few coins, but now even that is gone and my bed is cold indeed.
column2: “我寂寞得很。这门亲事之前，我至少还能用几枚钱币说动一个娼妇来暖床，如今连这也没了，床冷得很。”

column1: I can barely even hear you over the throbbing of this headache.
column2: “头疼跳成这样，我几乎听不见你说话。”

column1: I could use a little heat right now. This place is freezing.
column2: “我现在倒想要点热的。这地方冷死了。”

column1: I don't hear anything. An animal perhaps?
column2: “我什么都没听见。也许是只动物？”

column1: I don't know. Perhaps I did.
column2: “我不知道。也许我听到了。”

column1: I don't suppose you guys want to give my friends back?
column2: “我想你们大概不打算把我的朋友还给我吧？”

column1: I don't... have much time. I can barely... project this image... and I ... cannot hear you, so please... listen closely.
column2: “我没有……多少时间。我几乎……投射不出这个影像……而且我……听不见你，所以请……听仔细。”

column1: I have definitely been better.
column2: “我绝对有过更好的时候。”

column1: I heard it.
column2: “我听到了。”

column1: I was the one who kept downplaying the possibility. I was tired and didn't want to think about it.
column2: “一直把这种可能往轻里说的人是我。我累了，不想去想。”

column1: I wasn't naked on a dungeon floor an hour or two ago.

column1: I'd rather be a concubine than a labourer.

column1: I'll take that as a no then.

column1: I'm sure you're just being paranoid. It was a hart or some harmless beast, and soon we'll-

column1: I'm well-ready for a rest. It's far too hot today.
column2: “我可真想歇一歇。今天热得过头了。”

column1: I've got a bad feeling about this, Ro.
column2: “我有不好的预感，Ro。”

column1: If he was at the house, he did, but for all we know he got captured too and is in another cell.
column2: “他要是在那房子里，就收到了。可谁知道呢，也许他自己也被抓了，关在另一间牢房。”

column1: If we aren't rescued soon, I may have little choice.
column2: “要是再不来人救，我也许就没得选了。”

column1: Kirilo, lad. Help me walk, will you?

column1: Kirilo... I can't... move...

column1: Let's get you guys out of here. You can recuperate somewhere warmer and drier.
column2: “我们把你们弄出去。找个更暖和、更干的地方养一养。”

column1: Maybe she, at least, will find some joy when I am gone, in the arms of a man with a smoother face.
column2: “也许至少她，在我离去之后，能在一个脸更光滑的男人怀里寻到些快活。”

column1: Maybe. We'd better do a quick sweep to make sure.
column2: “也许吧。我们最好快速搜一圈，确认一下。”

column2: “我倒是想愤愤不平，可 Kirilo 说得对，而且越来越糟。我几乎看不清东西，更别说施法了。”

column1: No rest just yet, it seems.
column2: “看来这会儿还歇不成。”

column1: No. I could understand most of what they were saying. They were sizing us up for our value as slaves.

column1: Noctum!
column2: “Noctum！”

column1: Now you sound like Peregrine.

column1: Of course.

column1: So far, so good.
column2: “到目前为止，还好。”

column1: So it was you making all that noise! I knew you'd come for us!
column2: “那些动静原来是你！我就知道你会来找我们！”

column1: So repulsed by me is my wife that she sleeps in a separate room, the room I built for the children I now know we will never have.
column2: “我的妻子厌恶我到了极点，睡在另一间屋里，那是我给孩子盖的房间，而我如今知道，我们永远不会有孩子。”

column1: Spoke too soon.
column2: “话说早了。”

column1: Surely even Peregrine has a good idea once in a while.

column1: That, I promise.

column1: Then we'll kick their asses like we always do.

column2: “他们用某种麻痹毒药把我们药倒了。知觉开始回到我的四肢，可这边可怜的 Ro 一直很遭罪。”

column1: They've been gone far too long. I don't like this.

column1: Try to stay positive. He'll come for us.

column1: Try to stay positive. She'll come for us.

column1: Wait, did you guys hear that?

column1: We shall see.

column1: Well, my boy, shall we?

column1: Why did you say it was your fault that we got captured?

column1: Yeah, yeah.

column1: Yeah. Probably nothing.

column1: Hold on for a minute.
column2: “等一会儿。”

column1: Hold on. I think I smell something. Might be another way in. If it is, we can get inside without using the main gate, maybe get the drop on old Fucko.
column2: “等一下。我好像闻到了什么。也许还有别的路进去。要是有，我们就能不走正门，也许还能给那个老傻逼来个突然袭击。”

column1: How dare you!
column2: “岂有此理！”

column1: I can't smell anything but rot. We'll have to look around, I guess. Best get to it.
column2: “我除了腐臭什么都闻不到。看来得四处找找。最好快点动手。”

column1: I do not make exceptions for misers! You approached me under the pretense of trade, so I will draw my due from you, one way or another!
column2: “我从不为守财奴破例！你打着贸易的幌子来见我，所以我会从你身上取走我应得的，用这种办法，或者那种！”

column1: I do not make exceptions for paupers! If you cannot pay in gold, I will draw my due from you in blood!
column2: “我从不为穷鬼破例！你要是付不出金子，我就用血来取我应得的！”

column1: I hate YOU Frico!
column2: “我恨的就是你，Frico！”

column1: I hate vampires! I hate your stupid fucking court and your stupid fucking blood parties!
column2: “我恨吸血鬼！我恨你那愚蠢透顶的宫廷，还有你那些愚蠢透顶的血宴！”

column1: I hate your hands and your fucking teeth on my skin, I hate all the stupid shit you make me do!
column2: “我恨你的手，恨你那该死的牙咬在我皮肤上，我恨你逼我做的所有蠢透了的破事！”

column1: I have gifted you with life eternal, and this is how you repay me? With treachery?!
column2: “我赐给你永生，你就这样报答我？用背叛？！”

column1: I owe you an awful lot, and I've never liked this castle anyway, so if you'll have me, I'm staying on. Whatever you're up to, I'm in it with you.
column2: “我欠你的太多了，而且我本来就不喜欢这座城堡，所以你要是肯收留我，我就留下。不管你要干什么，我都跟你一起。”

column1: I shall inform him of your arrival at once. Please, do come in.
column2: “我这就向他通报您的到来。请进。”

column1: I trust this will be a profitable arrangement for the both of us. It has been a pleasure doing business with you.
column2: “我相信这对我们双方都会是有利的安排。与你做生意，很愉快。”

column1: I will sweeten the draught of your blood by drawing it from you slowly, and with much pain! Your penance for this insult is nigh!
column2: “我要慢慢地、带着巨大的痛苦抽你的血，好让这一口更加香甜！你为这侮辱该受的罚，就在眼前！”

column1: I've seen the dead eyes peering at us from the shadows, the grinning fangs when one of us falls to your traps.
column2: “我见过死人的眼睛从暗处盯着我们，见过我们有人掉进你的陷阱时，那些咧开的尖牙。”

column1: I've seen the missives that forbid merchants from trading with us, penned in your cold hand.
column2: “我见过禁止商人与我们交易的文书，出自你那只冰冷的手。”

column1: If I am a pawn, then move me aside, leech! Show me your fangs so I can pull them out!
column2: “我要是棋子，就把我挪开啊，水蛭！亮出你的尖牙，我好把它们拔下来！”

column1: Instead you're a sad waste of loose skin and blunt fangs. It offends me to even sully my gaze upon you.
column2: “结果你却是一堆松垮的皮和钝牙，可悲的废物。看你一眼都脏了我的眼。”

column1: Look at you.
column2: “看看你。”

column1: Look, I'm saying if you're serious about getting through that gate, you're going to have to be ready to fight him. Don't let him convince you of anything else.
column2: “听着，我是说，你要是真想过那道门，就得准备好跟他打。别让他说服你相信别的。”

column1: Looks like we're in the kitchen. With any luck, we've managed to get in unnoticed. So far so good.
column2: “看来我们在厨房。运气好的话，我们进来没被人发现。目前还行。”

column1: My people suffer because of you Frico, and today, I'm going to be the one to put you down!
column2: “我的族人因你受苦，Frico，今天，要撂倒你的人是我！”

column1: Not too bad for a useless waste of skin, huh?
column2: “对一块没用的废皮来说，还不错吧？”

column1: Now that our business is concluded, please make yourselves at home in my court. When you are ready to leave, speak with me and I will have someone escort you outside.
column2: “既然生意已经谈完，请在我的宫廷里随意。你们准备离开时，跟我说一声，我会派人送你们出去。”

column1: Now we just have to track down Frico and put a sword in him. Let's go.
column2: “现在只要找到 Frico，给他一剑。走吧。”

column1: Now, leave. I tire of the sight of you.
column2: “现在，离开。我看你看得厌烦了。”

column1: Restrain them and bring them before me.
column2: “制住他们，带到我面前来。”

column1: Shit. I was hoping he'd still have a head, so I could take it home. Even his fangs are gone.
column2: “操。我还指望他脑袋还在，好带回家。连尖牙都没了。”

column1: Shut the fuck up, you rotten corpse! I didn't ask for this!
column2: “你他妈给我闭嘴，你这烂尸体！我可没求过这个！”

column1: Still, it seems you've brought me something interesting. Let's have a look, shall we?
column2: “不过，你似乎给我带来了点有意思的东西。我们看看，如何？”

column1: Still, the boldness does impart a certain richness to one's blood. I will enjoy draining you of it!
column2: “不过，这股莽劲倒真让血多了几分厚味。我会享受把你抽干！”

column1: Stupid mongrel, your people are nothing but pawns to move as I direct!
column2: “蠢杂种，你的族人不过是棋子，我说怎么动就怎么动！”

column1: Surely you seek passage to the east, yes? That is, after all, why anyone comes to this court.
column2: “你想必是要往东去的路，对吧？说到底，谁来这座宫廷，不都是为了这个。”

column1: Surprise guests? And one of them has a fierce heart indeed!
column2: “不速之客？而且其中一颗心可真够凶猛！”

column1: Take care you do not lose it, for I am not fond of giving second chances to incompetents.
column2: “小心别弄丢了。我对无能之辈，可不喜欢给第二次机会。”

column1: Thanks. Even if you don't really mean it, it's not something I ever get to hear. It's nice.
column2: “谢谢。就算你不是真心的，这话我也从没听人说过。挺好的。”

column1: That's the closest thing to joy I felt since being turned. Thank you.
column2: “这是我被转化以来，最接近喜悦的感觉。谢谢你。”

column1: The cost of safety is 10,000$, squarely. Pay this, and Westgate shall be open to you, along with the eastern half of Lukatt.
column2: “安全的代价是整整10,000$。付了这笔，西门便对你敞开，卢卡特的东半边也一样。”

column1: The mongrel's bark betrays its nature. What a woeful waste of the primal blood coursing through you.
column2: “杂种的吠声暴露了它的本性。在你体内奔流的原始之血，浪费得何其可悲。”

column1: The price you may find steep, but in the interest of... fairness... it must be the same for all travellers. You understand, of course.
column2: “这价钱你也许觉得高，可出于……公平……对所有旅人必须一样。你当然明白。”

column1: This has been a long time coming, Frico!
column2: “这一天等得够久了，Frico！”

column1: This way.
column2: “这边。”

column1: Ugh, finally. I can climb this no problem. Let me go first and I'll help you up.
column2: “呃，终于。这个我爬上去没问题。让我先上，再拉你。”

column1: Ugh, fuck, it's some kind of... charnel pit or something. I can barely breathe.
column2: “呃，操，这是什么……尸坑之类的。我几乎喘不上气。”

column1: Wait. There's a lot of... red tape, if we go in through the main door. Let's go in through my entrance instead. Skip the wait and take you straight to the boss.
column2: “等等。走正门的话，手续……麻烦得很。咱们改走我的入口。省得干等，直接带你去见老大。”

column1: Watch your step. And try to keep your voices down.
column2: “脚下留神。声音也尽量放低。”

column1: Welcome, honoured guests, to my humble abode. It is rare we have visitors at all, and rarer still to have ones as obviously well-travelled as you.
column2: “欢迎，尊贵的客人，光临我的寒舍。我们这儿少有访客，而像你们这样一看便知见多识广的，更是稀少。”

column1: Welcome. You have come to seek audience with Lord Frico, have you not?
column2: “欢迎。你是来求见领主 Frico 的，对吧？”

column1: Well, at least the soft-skinned pup wants not for bravado! Brains, on the other hand, he sorely lacks.
column2: “哼，至少这只皮嫩的小狗崽不缺虚张声势！脑子嘛，他可缺得厉害。”

column1: What a weird feeling. I want to cry, but vampires don't cry. I want to piss on his corpse, but vampires don't piss either.
column2: “感觉真怪。我想哭，可吸血鬼不哭。我想在他尸体上撒尿，可吸血鬼也不会撒尿。”

column1: Yeah, funny, huh? It's kind of great still having a heartbeat. Not that you ever had one to start with.
column2: “是啊，好笑吧？还能有心跳，还挺好的。也不是说你一开始就有过。”

column1: Yeah. Ha ha, right?
column2: “是啊。哈哈，对吧？”

column1: You do not deserve the blood you boast! Give it hence!
column2: “你不配拥有你所夸耀的血！交出来！”

column1: You freed me, and you should be able to get through the gate now.
column2: “你让我自由了，现在你应该也能过那道门了。”

column1: You should be a paragon of brutal, primal physicality, a sculpture of muscle and flesh, chiseled to perfection by moonlight!
column2: “你本该是残暴、原始肉体的典范，一尊肌肉与血肉的塑像，被月光雕琢到完美！”

column1: You've left your key on the floor, fool.
column2: “你把钥匙掉在地上了，蠢货。”

column1: You, dog, do not make demands of me!
column2: “你这狗东西，别对我发号施令！”

column1: Daze
column2: “眩晕”

column1: Entangle
column2: “缠绕”

column1: Focus
column2: “专注”

column1: Grace
column2: “优雅”

column1: Nexus
column2: “连结”

column1: Pain
column2: “剧痛”

column1: Poison
column2: “中毒”

column1: Rage
column2: “狂怒”

column1: Shadowcloak
column2: “暗影斗篷”

column1: Vigor
column2: “活力”

column1: Madam Johan, if you are reading this, you may consider your outstanding debt paid in full. -B
column2: “Johan 夫人，若你读到这个，可视为你未清的债务已经全部偿清。——B”

column1: You bastard, Regar, this was only half the payment promised. If you value your pretty little face, you'll have the rest of the payment next time we meet.
column2: “你这个混蛋，Regar，这只是答应过的一半报酬。要是你还珍惜你那张漂亮小脸，下次见面把剩下的钱带来。”

column1: All of these graves lie empty. This one, at least, I know why, but I will never know what became of all my cousins.
column2: “这些坟墓全是空的。这一座，至少我知道为什么，可我那些表亲都落得什么下场，我永远不会知道了。”

column1: Beauregard, are you alright?
column2: “Beauregard，你还好吗？”

column1: Before I go, there is something I must ask of you. Another shared my burden, and unlike me, he was guiltless.
column2: “在我离开之前，有件事必须拜托你。还有一个人与我分担这负担，而他与我不同，是无辜的。”

column1: Enough dwelling. I am ready to quit this place.
column2: “不必再流连了。我准备离开这地方。”

column1: Glamig. My cousin. My Queen.
column2: “Glamig。我的表亲。我的女王。”

column1: I am not. Let us finish what we need to do here and begone.
column2: “我不好。把这里该做的做完，然后离开吧。”

column1: Lingun Cosova, Duchess of Babe
column2: “Lingun Cosova，Babe 女公爵”

column1: Phara Cosova, Queen Mother
column2: “Phara Cosova，王太后”

column1: Please, stranger, if you would do me this one last honour, take the crown from my body and visit Blackspire Oubliette, learn what became of my cousin, and if his spirit suffers still, cut him free, as you have cut me free. His duty is long finished.
column2: “陌生人，求你，若肯给我这最后的体面，从我身上取走王冠，前往黑尖塔地牢，查明我表亲的下场。若他的灵魂仍在受苦，就斩断他，还他自由，正如你斩断了我。他的职责早已完成。”

column1: Ryke Tsarath, Duke of Knavewood
column2: “Ryke 察拉思，无赖林公爵”

column1: Shur bree ah! Id shur bree ah! Dum ay, dum ay Id shur bree ah!
column2: “舒尔布里啊！伊德舒尔布里啊！达姆哎，达姆哎伊德舒尔布里啊！”

column1: Shur bree ah. Dum ay or pen d'Id shur bree ah.
column2: “舒尔布里啊。达姆哎奥彭迪德舒尔布里啊。”

column1: There is more I would say, but I have no time left. My journal may yet remain in the nearby abbey if you would learn more. Now go, and know that you go with my thanks.
column2: “我还有更多话想说，可我没有时间了。你若想知道更多，我的日记也许还在附近的修道院里。现在走吧，你走的时候，带着我的感谢。”

column1: These graves were preordained for my servants and ministers, but so despised was I that none were actually buried with me, and all lay empty. The angry spirits in this place were drawn here from afar by my grief, and you have my blessing to take from here whatever suits you.
column2: “这些坟墓本是为我的仆从和大臣预备的，可我被人厌弃到这种地步，竟没有一个人真正与我同葬，墓穴全是空的。我的哀恸把愤怒的灵体从远方引到了这里，此处凡合你用的，我都准你取走。”

column1: Thinking they had escaped my notice, my Lord Husband and my prime minister conspired to ease his suffering. This was treason, but I feigned ignorance and allowed them to work in secrecy, so I know not what they planned.
column2: “我的夫君与我的宰相以为瞒过了我的耳目，密谋减轻他的痛苦。这是叛国，可我佯装不知，任他们秘密行事，因此我并不知道他们筹划了什么。”

column1: To stand above his own grave is, I think, something a man was never meant to do.
column2: “站在自己的坟墓之上，我想，本不是一个人该做的事。”

column1: When my reign over this island came to an end, I was much despised by my subjects, and I was buried here without ceremony. Your gesture, however small, is the first shred of dignity I have been offered since long before my death, and it is enough to grant me proper rest. Thank you.
column2: “我对这座岛的统治走到尽头时，臣民深深厌弃我，我被葬在这里，没有葬仪。你的举动虽小，却是自我死前很久以来，头一次有人给予我的一丝尊严，已足够让我得以安歇。谢谢你。”

column1: When my subjects began to demand I be punished, my cousin volunteered to suffer as my proxy, as is the law of Orcs. He went dutifully to Blackspire Oubliette in the Blackglass Sprawl, where he should have perished, forgotten.
column2: “当我的臣民开始要求惩罚我时，我的表亲按兽人的律法自愿代我受刑。他尽职前往黑璃城区的黑尖塔地牢，本该在那里死去，被人遗忘。”

column1: When we came here, we were all so happy. How did everything turn out so wrong?
column2: “我们来到这里的时候，大家都那么快乐。怎么一切会变成这样？”

column1: Alright boys, enough chatter! Fuck 'em up!
column2: “好了伙计们，少废话！干死他们！”

column1: Pretty place, ain't it? You should be pleased that we picked out such a nice burial plot for you.
column2: “这地方挺漂亮，是不是？我们给你们挑了这么好一块坟地，你们该高兴才是。”

column1: Well, lookie here. A batch of right pretty ones, you are.
column2: “哟，瞧瞧。你们这一批可真够标致的。”

column1: ... what do you want?
column2: “……你想干什么？”

column1: ... whatever you wish, Alpha.
column2: “……全凭您吩咐，Alpha。”

column1: ...as you wish.
column2: “……如您所愿。”

column1: A bit of an overreaction, wouldn't you say? He barely said anything.
column2: “你不觉得这反应有点过头了吗？他几乎什么都没说。”

column1: And who could blame him, really? Lass, you're showing more thigh than the butcher on market day.
column2: “说真的，这能怪他吗？丫头，你露出来的大腿，比赶集日屠夫摊子上的肉还多。”

column1: Anyway, I've been thinking about it a lot lately because...
column2: “反正，我最近一直在想这件事，因为……”

column1: As you say.
column2: “如你所说。”

column1: At least he can still have feelings like that. I don't even remember what it's like.
column2: “至少他还能有那样的感觉。我连那是什么滋味都不记得了。”

column1: Bite you? Son, it doesn't work like that. It... would take too long to explain, but you can't become a werewolf by being bit by one. That's just stupid superstition.
column2: “咬你？小子，不是那么回事。这……解释起来太久了，可被狼人咬了是不会变成狼人的。那纯粹是蠢迷信。”

column1: Compared to what I wanted to do, that was gentle. Back way off, beardy.
column2: “跟我想做的比起来，那已经算轻的了。给我退远点，大胡子。”

column1: Cry me a river. Oh what's that? Can't cry either? Try shutting up then. You can still do that, right?
column2: “你倒是哭条河出来。哦，怎么？哭也不行？那就试试把嘴闭上。这你总还办得到吧？”

column1: Do not be afraid. You are not an enemy. Not yet.
column2: “别怕。你不是敌人。暂时还不是。”

column1: Don't toy with me, fool. I can smell the stink of Frico's blood on you already.
column2: “别跟我耍花招，蠢货。我已经闻见你身上沾着 Frico 的血臭了。”

column1: Don't you tell me how to dress, you old shit pirate! He has no right to look, no matter what I wear!
column2: “轮不到你教我怎么穿衣服，你这老屎海盗！不管我穿什么，他都没资格看！”

column1: Excuse me, but I'm not really in the mood to chat with strangers. Please leave me be.
column2: “抱歉，我这会儿实在没心情跟陌生人聊天。请让我一个人待着。”

column1: Girl, you're crazy. That guy was cute!
column2: “姑娘，你疯了吧。那家伙挺可爱的！”

column1: Go to hell.
column2: “下地狱去。”

column1: Good. Leave.
column2: “很好。离开。”

column1: Grant!
column2: “Grant！”

column1: Grant, my boy. You've done a great service for all of us. I am very proud of you.
column2: “Grant，我的孩子。你为我们所有人立了大功。我非常为你骄傲。”

column1: Hah! You plan to march into the vampire lord's castle and murder him upon his throne? Oh, that would be a sight to see! I salivate at the thought of it.
column2: “哈！你打算一路杀进吸血鬼领主的城堡，在他的王座上谋杀他？哦，那场面可值得一看！我光想想就流口水。”

column1: Halfway there, Kirilo. Drop it.
column2: “你已经惹到一半了，Kirilo。打住。”

column1: Haven't seen you around here before, strangers. This is Hayill. If you've come lookin' for trouble, you'll find more of it than you care for. If not, we welcome you and your coin. Just watch yourselves.
column2: “以前没在这儿见过你们，陌生人。这里是海伊尔。要是来找麻烦，麻烦会多得你们受不了。要是不找，我们欢迎你们，也欢迎你们的钱。自己小心点。”

column1: He has grown powerful through the advantage that pass affords him, taxing those he deems useful and bleeding those he does not. How do you intend to deal with him?
column2: “他靠那条山口带来的便利壮大了自己，对他认为有用的人抽税，对没用的人放血。你打算怎么对付他？”

column1: He is... brief, but even fat as he is, he is powerful. You will not be disappointed.
column2: “他这人……不多话，可就算胖成这样，也一样强。你不会失望的。”

column1: He's been dropping hints that he wants to lay with me though. I pretend to be too dumb to notice. I ain't a poofter.
column2: “不过他一直在暗示想跟我上床。我装傻，当没看出来。我可不是搞基的。”

column1: Head over to the store if you need any supplies. I'm sure he'll be glad to see your coin.
column2: “要补给就去商店。他看见你们的钱肯定高兴。”

column1: Hey. You're from out of town, right? You seen many women on the island?
column2: “嘿。你们是外地来的吧？在岛上见过很多女人吗？”

column1: I appreciate your help, but if you don't mind, we could use some privacy. We've got a lot to talk about.
column2: “感谢你的帮助，不过如果不介意，我们想单独待会儿。有很多话要说。”

column1: I didn't think so. There's even less women here than there were back home in Tsarath, and that's saying something.
column2: “我就知道。这儿的女人比老家察拉思还要少，这可真说明问题。”

column1: I expect you to return with blood under your claws and stories under your tongue.
column2: “我指望你回来的时候，爪子底下有血，舌头底下有故事。”

column1: I feel kinda bad for the guy, honestly.
column2: “说实话，我有点替那家伙难受。”

column1: I feel much better now. Thanks again.
column2: “我现在好多了。再次谢谢。”

column1: I feel rather bad for him. He must've thought he spied a fallen angel just now.
column2: “我相当替他难过。他刚才一定以为自己看见了堕落天使。”

column1: I guess compared to the brand and the exile, it's a stupid detail to get hung up on. \nI'm gonna go talk to him. Thanks for listening.
column2: “跟烙印和流放比起来，纠结这种小事挺蠢的。 \n我去跟他谈谈。谢谢你听我说。”

column1: I have decided that you shall serve as our emissary instead. Lead them to the mountain, slaughter that leech upon it, and piss on everything he owns.
column2: “我决定改让你当我们的使者。带他们上山，宰了山上那条蚂蟥，再往他的一切东西上撒尿。”

column1: I have given you all the help I dare. Go, and remember my generosity.
column2: “我敢给的帮助都给了。走吧，记住我的慷慨。”

column1: I have no idea what just happened.
column2: “我完全不知道刚才发生了什么。”

column1: I heard you talking earlier, you know. I should probably be mad, but it's hard for me to feel upset right now. Thank you.
column2: “我早先听见你们说话了，你知道的。我大概该生气，可我现在实在气不起来。谢谢你。”

column1: I just guard the door, stranger. If you need something else, you'll have to find someone more important to ask.
column2: “我只负责守门，陌生人。你要是有别的事，得找个更重要的人去问。”

column1: I kill my enemies, Rangda. I don't go out of my way to make more of them. There is a difference.
column2: “我杀的是敌人，Rangda。我不会特意再去树敌。这是两回事。”

column1: I see. Well, you'll find Hayill a pleasant enough place if you mind yourselves. Visit our shop and tavern, if you need supplies. Good day.
column2: “明白了。只要你们安分一点，会发现海伊尔是个够舒服的地方。需要补给的话，去我们的商店和酒馆。日安。”

column1: I suppose your leech can stay, for the time being, as a show of goodwill.
column2: “你的那条蚂蟥可以暂时留下，就当我表示一点善意。”

column1: I understand you have killed Frico! This is excellent news!
column2: “我知道你杀了 Frico！这真是好消息！”

column1: I was talking about you nursing your frivolous pride, woman. Next time, ignore it and keep your braying to yourself.
column2: “我说的是你在娇惯自己那点无谓的自尊心，女人。下次别管它，把你的驴叫收回去。”

column1: I will.
column2: “我会的。”

column1: I wonder if the barkeep will bother putting his shirt on today.
column2: “不知道酒保今天会不会费神把衬衫穿上。”

column1: I'd like to actually hear you shut your mouth right about now.
column2: “我现在倒真想听你把嘴闭上。”

column1: I'm just the Alpha's bodyguard. You don't need to talk to me.
column2: “我只是 Alpha 的保镖。你不用跟我说话。”

column1: I'm sure they weren't orc women, not that I'd get picky over a human right about now.
column2: “我肯定她们不是兽人女人。不过我现在对人类也挑剔不起来。”

column1: I'm the scum of the earth, and even I think you're a bitch.
column2: “我是天底下的人渣，连我都觉得你是个贱人。”

column1: I'm... ashamed that I ever bought this. I don't think I'd have had the heart to use it anyway. It was expensive though, so... take it. Maybe you can sell it.
column2: “我……很羞愧自己居然买了这东西。反正我觉得自己也下不了手用。不过它挺贵的，所以……拿去吧。也许你能卖掉。”

column1: I've been thinking about it though, and... even if I did find a woman on this island, why would she care about me? Not like any other woman ever did.
column2: “不过我也想过……就算我真在这岛上找到一个女人，她凭什么在乎我？别的女人可从来没在乎过。”

column1: If we're really never going to get out of here, then... I'm pretty damn lucky to have a friend in this at all.
column2: “要是我们真的永远出不去了，那……这件事里还能有个朋友，我已经够他妈走运的了。”

column1: If you hurt our town, you will suffer.
column2: “你们要是伤害我们的镇子，就得吃苦头。”

column1: In truth, that foppish corpse has been a nuisance to us for quite some time, but my people are not fighters, and I would not throw them at him in suicidal defiance.
column2: “说实话，那具打扮得花哨的尸体已经烦了我们很久，可我的族人不是战士，我不会把他们送去跟他拼命。”

column1: It's a lot easier to keep control of ourselves when we aren't forced to hide what we are. Getting sent here was the best thing that ever happened to me.
column2: “不用被迫藏起自己是什么的时候，我们控制自己要容易多了。被送到这儿，是我这辈子最好的事。”

column1: It's been awful lonely, and he has been real good to me. I don't know. What do you think?
column2: “实在太寂寞了，而且他对我一直很好。我不知道。你觉得呢？”

column1: It's clear I don't need a bodyguard. You've grown fat from a lack of any real work to do.
column2: “显然我已经不需要保镖了。没有真正的活干，你都养肥了。”

column1: Just leave me alone.
column2: “别来烦我。”

column1: Just try it, hamshanks!
column2: “你倒是试试啊，火腿腿！”

column1: Let me be entirely unsubtle. Get out of my town.
column2: “我就直白地说。滚出我的镇子。”

column1: Let us not waste time with such idle distractions.
column2: “我们不必在这种无谓的消遣上浪费时间。”

column1: Like I care what you think, fatass.
column2: “我才不在乎你怎么想，肥屁股。”

column1: Like hell! I know where that compliment was going.
column2: “鬼才信！我知道那句夸奖想往哪儿引。”

column1: Maybe I will!
column2: “也许我会！”

column1: Mind your business while you're here, and you'll have no trouble from us.
column2: “在这儿少管闲事，我们就不找你麻烦。”

column1: Mouth off like that to one of my brothers again and you'll see where my boot is going.
column2: “再敢对我哪个兄弟这么放肆，你就等着看我的靴子往哪儿踢。”

column1: My favorite part was how you could actually see the wound forming on his soul. Real nice, Rangda. Classy broad, you.
column2: “我最喜欢的是，能看见伤口正在他灵魂上成形。真不错，Rangda。你这娘们可真有格调。”

column1: My patience is wearing thin, leech-lover. Begone!
column2: “我的耐心要耗尽了，爱蚂蟥的。滚开！”

column1: No shirt, no shorts, no problem. Come on in.
column2: “没衬衫，没短裤，没问题。进来吧。”

column1: Nobody asked you. Mind your damn business.
column2: “没人问你。管好你自己的屁事。”

column1: Now go.
column2: “现在去吧。”

column1: Oh goodness. That poor fellow. I think I actually heard his heart breaking.
column2: “天哪。那可怜的人。我好像真听见他的心碎了。”

column1: Shit, Rangda, that was cold. You could've at least let him down gently.
column2: “靠，Rangda，这也太冷了。你至少可以拒绝得委婉一点。”

column1: Shit, is that all it takes? Remind me not to get on your bad side.
column2: “靠，就这点事就够了？提醒我别惹到你头上。”

column1: Shut up, Shapiro.
column2: “闭嘴，Shapiro。”

column1: Shut your mouth, you old fossil. He has no right to gawk at me.
column2: “闭上嘴，你这老化石。他没资格盯着我看。”

column1: T'was just a look then, wasn't it? But fine, suit yourself.
column2: “那不过就是看了一眼，不是吗？行吧，随你便。”

column1: Take care of Grant for us. The Alpha would never admit it, but he cares deeply for that boy, and he would be devastated if anything were to happen to him.
column2: “替我们照顾好 Grant。Alpha 绝不会承认，可他非常在乎那个孩子，要是那孩子出了什么事，他会崩溃的。”

column1: Take your sermon and stuff it, priest.
column2: “把你的说教给我塞回去，牧师。”

column1: Tell Grant that I am proud of him.
column2: “告诉 Grant，我为他骄傲。”

column1: Thank you, Alpha.
column2: “谢谢你，Alpha。”

column1: That guy over there, he's a good friend of mine. We've watched each others' backs since shipping up here, and there's nobody I trust more.
column2: “那边那个人是我的好朋友。从被船运到这儿开始，我们就一直互相照应，没有我更信任的人了。”

column1: That was a shit thing to do, Rangda. He's a good guy, and he was just trying to pay you a compliment.
column2: “你这么做真够操蛋的，Rangda。他是个好人，只不过想夸你一句。”

column1: That's rich coming from a murderer.
column2: “这话从谋杀犯嘴里说出来，可真讽刺。”

column1: The people here don't really seem all that happy.
column2: “这儿的人看上去实在不怎么快乐。”

column1: Then why do you feel compelled to offer your inane commentary? Nobody cares what you think, Goblin.
column2: “那你干嘛非要发表那些废话？没人关心你怎么想，哥布林。”

column1: Then, you'll be needing a good deal of money, and no small share of luck. I'm afraid, however, that I can help you with neither. Good day.
column2: “那你就需要一大笔钱，还得有不少运气。可惜这两样我都帮不上忙。日安。”

column1: There is only one path to go further east, and it is controlled by the vampire lord, Frico.
column2: “再往东去只有一条路，控制在吸血鬼领主 Frico 手里。”

column1: There's no sense wasting time on the problems of every random passer-by, after all.
column2: “毕竟，没道理把时间浪费在每个过路人的麻烦上。”

column1: This island is a prison, you idiot. Nobody's supposed to be happy.
column2: “这岛就是座监狱，白痴。谁都不该高兴。”

column1: Ugh, sorry. I shouldn't use strangers for sounding boards. Forget it.
column2: “呃，对不起。我不该拿陌生人当树洞。当我没说。”

column1: Ugh. Drop dead, asshole. I don't care how long it's been since you've seen a healthy orc woman, I don't want anything to do with you.
column2: “呃。去死吧，混蛋。我不管你多久没见过健壮的兽人女人，我都不想跟你有任何关系。”

column1: Very well. You have earned the right to choose this. Go with my blessing.
column2: “很好。你已经赢得自己做这个选择的权利。带着我的祝福去吧。”

column1: We couldn't have made a better go at starting our own community if we had tried. Here there's no law, and there were already ruined towns just waiting for us.
column2: “就算我们刻意去试，也建不出更好的自己的聚落。这儿没有法律，废掉的镇子又早就等着我们。”

column1: Welcome to Hayill, stranger. Is there something I can do for you?
column2: “欢迎来到海伊尔，陌生人。有什么我能帮你的？”

column1: Welcome to Hayill. Yes, we're all werewolves. Play nice and you're good, fuck with us and we kill you. Simple, right?
column2: “欢迎来到海伊尔。对，我们全是狼人。规矩点就没事，惹我们就把你们杀了。很简单，对吧？”

column1: Who asked you, anyway? Mind your own business.
column2: “再说，谁问你了？管好你自己的事。”

column1: Why the hell should I care?
column2: “我他妈干嘛要在乎？”

column1: Yeah, I'm sure that he wouldn't want me to agree just to humour him. Thanks for listening.
column2: “是啊，我肯定他也不希望我只是为了迁就他才答应。谢谢你听我说。”

column1: Yeah. Alright. Sorry, miss.
column2: “嗯。好吧。对不起，小姐。”

column1: Yeah? Well why don't you fuck him then.
column2: “是吗？那你怎么不去操他。”

column1: Yeah? Why don't you go let him flirt with you then?
column2: “是吗？那你怎么不自己去让他跟你调情？”

column1: Yes, Alpha.
column2: “是，Alpha。”

column1: Yes, exactly.
column2: “对，正是如此。”

column1: Yes, for a time at least. I will return when I am ready.
column2: “是的，至少眼下是这样。我准备好了就回来。”

column1: You enjoyed hurting him. I've seen you treat our enemies with more dignity.
column2: “你享受伤害他。我见过你对待敌人都更有体面。”

column1: You have some brass if nothing else. I would very much like to see Frico brought down by your hands. Perhaps I can support you in this.
column2: “别的不说，你倒是有胆子。我非常想看到 Frico 栽在你手里。这件事上我也许能帮你。”

column1: You have the scent of the road heavy on you now, and I do not see you returning with your belongings. You intend to remain with your new companions then?
column2: “你身上现在满是路上的气味，我也没看见你把行李带回来。那么，你是打算留下，跟你的新同伴一起了？”

column1: You know Rangda, patience is a virtue. You have no idea what he's been through, and he was terribly polite.
column2: “你知道的，Rangda，耐心是美德。你根本不知道他经历过什么，而且他礼貌得不得了。”

column1: You must have come a long way. There are smells on you I don't recognize.
column2: “你们一定走了很远的路。你们身上有我认不出的气味。”

column1: You should speak with the Alpha if you haven't already. He is well-connected, and may be able to help you.
column2: “你要是还没跟 Alpha 谈过，该去谈谈。他门路广，也许能帮上你。”

column1: You suppose there are any other orc women on the island at all, or are you really the only one?
column2: “你觉得这岛上到底还有没有别的兽人女人，还是真就只有你一个？”

column1: You! You're a woman! I ain't seen a woman in forever! I... um... you haven't by any chance seen other women around the island, have you?
column2: “你！你是女人！我好久好久没见过女人了！我……呃……你该不会碰巧在岛上见过别的女人吧？”

column1: You... um... you are awful strong-looking, miss. That armour... I mean it looks amazing on you.
column2: “你……呃……你看起来壮得吓人，小姐。那身护甲……我是说穿在你身上真好看。”

column1: Evening, gents. Why not take a seat and rest a spell.
column2: “晚上好，先生们。何不坐下来歇一会儿。”

column1: Hedgefort Gardens Cafe - Open!
column2: “篱堡花园咖啡馆——营业中！”

column1: Hedgefort Maze - Open to all visitors.
column2: “篱堡迷宫——对所有访客开放。”

column1: I can't sell 'em any lower than that.
column2: “再低我就卖不了了。”

column1: I feel bad, though... most of the grass\nhas worn out along the route I usually take.
column2: “不过我有点过意不去……我常走的那条路上\n草大部分都磨秃了。”

column1: I'll need to close up soon before it gets too dark, but I've still got one last platter of sandwiches here.
column2: “天太黑之前我得打烊了，不过这儿还剩最后一盘三明治。”

column1: I'm not going to ask any questions, though. They just seem to want to relax and, so long as there's no nonsense, I've got nothing against them being here.
column2: “不过我什么都不会问。他们好像只想放松放松，只要不胡闹，我不反对他们待在这儿。”

column1: I've been back and forth through the maze so many times, but it never seems to get old.
column2: “这座迷宫我来回走了那么多遍，可好像永远也不会腻。”

column1: I've been getting some... interesting customers, to say the least. Nearly had a heart attack when that skeleton walked up to the counter.
column2: “我最近的客人……怎么说呢，挺有意思。那具骷髅走到柜台前的时候，我差点心脏病发作。”

column1: Thanks!
column2: “谢谢！”

column1: That's three of my best toasted sandwiches for 125$.\nHow does that sound?
column2: “三份我最好的烤三明治，125$。\n你觉得怎么样？”

column1: These egg and cress sandwiches are simply divine. I must ask that fellow over there for the recipe.
column2: “这些鸡蛋水芹三明治简直妙不可言。我得去向那边那位要食谱。”

column1: When I get home, I shall write a book about this place...\nif I ever do get home.
column2: “等我回家，我要写一本关于这地方的书……\n要是我真能回去的话。”

column1: You were right, there was a problem with the steam pressure. Looks like I owe you a drink. We've had the leak plugged up, so you shouldn't have any trouble getting the doors open.
column2: “你说得对，蒸汽压力确实有问题。看来我欠你一杯。漏洞已经补上了，开门应该不会再有麻烦。”

column1: A beast. No doubt a large one. Keep your eyes peeled.
column2: “一头野兽。绝对是大家伙。把眼睛放亮。”

column1: A common thug, running from his own inadequacy. Best ignore him.
column2: “一个寻常的暴徒，在逃避自己的无能。最好别理他。”

column1: Aaah! Run away!!
column2: “啊啊！快跑！！”

column1: Ah, you don't... you don't suppose maybe we could find another way through? Do we really have to go in the direction of the howling and screaming?
column2: “啊，你不会……你不会觉得咱们也许能另找一条路吧？咱们真的得朝那嚎叫和尖叫的方向走吗？”

column1: As entertaining as that was, this pass is probably dangerous. Keep your eyes open.
column2: “刚才虽然挺有意思，这条山口大概很危险。眼睛睁大点。”

column1: Beware of Falling Rocks
column2: “小心落石”

column1: Bye! We'll just help ourselves to whatever you might've dropped back there, kay?
column2: “再见！你刚才落在后面的东西，我们就拿走了，好吧？”

column1: Goodness! Perhaps, maybe we should find another way 'round?
column2: “天哪！也许，说不定咱们该绕条别的路？”

column1: Hah! Was that our ambush? What a joke.
column2: “哈！那就是冲我们来的埋伏？真是笑话。”

column1: He's probably running for a very good reason. Stay on-guard.
column2: “他这么跑，八成有很充分的理由。保持戒备。”

column1: Hey! You forgot your ambush! Now how are you going to get all our money?
column2: “嘿！你把埋伏给忘了！这下还怎么把我们的钱全抢走？”

column1: I guess he didn't want our coin badly enough to work for it. What do you suppose set him off?
column2: “我猜他没那么眼馋我们的钱，不值得为此卖力。你觉得是什么把他吓跑的？”

column1: I smelled sasquatch when I came through here before. Guess that guy found it.
column2: “我以前打这儿过的时候闻见过大脚怪。看来那家伙碰上了。”

column1: I'd bet my cutlass that noise was a sasquatch. Usually not too aggressive, but that one sounds mightily set-off.
column2: “我敢拿我的弯刀打赌，那声音是大脚怪。它们通常不怎么凶，可这一只听起来火气大得很。”

column1: I'd know that sound anywhere. Sasquatch, for sure. Nothing we can't handle.
column2: “这声音我到哪儿都认得。绝对是大脚怪。没什么我们搞不定的。”

column1: I'm not sure if I'm relieved, or more worried than before. Let's just be careful.
column2: “我不知道自己是松了口气，还是比刚才更担心。咱们还是小心点吧。”

column1: Oh, great. I wasn't looking forward to tomorrow anyway. Let's go directly toward the horrible thing, shall we?
column2: “哦，太好了。我本来也不指望活到明天。咱们直接朝那可怕的东西走，如何？”

column1: Something up ahead seriously stinks. I'd wager it's also angry. Be careful.
column2: “前面有东西臭得厉害。我打赌它还在发火。小心。”

column1: That sound was a sasquatch. An irritated one. No wonder he was in such a hurry.
column2: “那声音是大脚怪。还是只被惹毛了的。难怪他那么急。”

column1: There's blood up ahead. Probably his friends got wasted and he's the only one who ran in time. Watch yourself.
column2: “前面有血。大概他的朋友被干掉了，只有他跑得及时。小心。”

column1: Well, shall we see what got his panties into such a twist?
column2: “好吧，咱们去看看是什么把他吓得内裤都拧成结了？”

column1: Well, so much for getting rich quick, huh? Why would someone even care about getting rich here anyway?
column2: “得，快速发财到此为止了，嗯？再说，在这儿谁还会在乎发财？”

column1: Whatever it is, I can handle it. Don't worry about it.
column2: “不管是什么，我都能应付。别担心。”

column1: Exec. Suites
column2: “行政套房”

column1: Yes, your discipline is bound within the myriad folds of this steel pearl. Go then, Crusader, with this symbol of the righteous, and scour this land!
column2: “是的，你的戒律缚于这颗钢珍珠的万千褶皱之中。去吧，十字军，带着这正义的徽记，去荡涤这片土地！”

column1: You come seeking power, as did the demons, but the power guarded herein belongs only to those with the discipline to use it wisely.
column2: “你来寻求力量，正如那些恶魔也曾如此，可此处所守护的力量，只属于有戒律、能明智使用它的人。”

column1: This place gives me an uneasy feeling. If we must explore it, I would caution you to stay alert. Something unholy this way waits.
column2: “这地方让我心里不安。倘若非探索不可，我劝你保持警觉。有不洁之物在此等候。”

column1: ...unless you'd like to help with a little project of mine.
column2: “……除非你愿意帮我一个小项目的忙。”

column1: All five veins are present, to be sure, and they have not collapsed into the null-vein, but they are somehow... cancelling one another out?
column2: “五条魔脉确实都在，而且没有坍缩成空脉，可它们不知怎么……在互相抵消？”

column1: Good morning! I just finished!
column2: “早上好！我刚刚做完！”

column1: Great! Let's see!
column2: “太好了！让我看看！”

column1: I grew it myself. Look.
column2: “我自己长出来的。你看。”

column1: I have a feeling you have nothing to worry about!
column2: “我觉得你完全不用担心！”

column1: I haven't touched the forge lately. I'm very busy working out the theory for my next attempt. It'll probably be a few months before I even know where to start with more materials. Thanks for checking in though.
column2: “我最近没动过锻炉。我忙着推敲下一次尝试的理论。大概还得几个月，我才知道接下来的材料该从哪下手。不过还是谢谢你来看我。”

column1: I hope.
column2: “希望如此。”

column1: I love secrets! What's the project? A crown of unlimited power? A breastplate of invulnerability? I have some ideas for one of those.
column2: “我就爱秘密！什么项目？一顶无限力量的王冠？一件无敌的胸甲？其中一样我倒有些想法。”

column1: I will take the time to double-check my alignments.
column2: “我会花时间，把各条魔脉的对齐再核对一遍。”

column1: I'm honoured! Beyond honoured! This is really special. I won't even charge you for it.
column2: “太荣幸了！荣幸至极！这真的很特别。我甚至不会收你钱。”

column1: I'm so glad to hear it! Are you by yourself? What brings you out to my forge today?
column2: “听你这么说真高兴！就你一个人？今天怎么到我的锻炉来了？”

column1: I'm sure you'll think of something!
column2: “你肯定能想出办法的！”

column1: I... I've finished. I can't believe that I've just done that. My experiment was a success, but...
column2: “我……我做完了。真不敢相信我刚刚做成了。实验成功了，可是……”

column1: It was my pleasure! Good luck!
column2: “我的荣幸！祝你好运！”

column1: It's an engagement gift.
column2: “是件订婚礼物。”

column1: It's fine, thanks. Very useful!
column2: “挺好的，谢谢。非常有用！”

column1: It's good to see you again! How's the ring working out?
column2: “又见到你真好！戒指用着怎么样？”

column1: It's yours, as promised, but I'm afraid I can't tell you how to make effective use of it. You may have to do some experimentation of your own. As for me...
column2: “按约定，它是你的了，不过恐怕我没法告诉你怎样有效使用它。你也许得自己做些实验。至于我……”

column1: Looks like someone's here to pick you up. Guess we didn't finish a moment too soon, hmm? Don't worry, my lips are sealed!
column2: “看来有人来接你了。我们完成得可一点也不早，是吧？别担心，我守口如瓶！”

column1: My interest in this is purely academic, so I propose this - if you bring me the necessary components to complete my experiment, I will give you the resulting item. If it works, you'll have all five veins of mana at once, and even if it doesn't work, you'll have a powerful and valuable piece.
column2: “我对这个纯粹是学术兴趣，所以我这么提议——你把完成实验所需要的材料给我带来，我就把做出来的东西给你。要是成功，你就能同时拥有全部五条法力魔脉；就算不成功，你也会得到一件既强大又贵重的物品。”

column1: Not as exciting for me, perhaps, but I'm sure it's exciting for you, and I do owe you one, so count me in! What did you have in mind?
column2: “对我也许没那么刺激，可我肯定你觉得刺激，而且我欠你一个人情，算我一个！你打算做什么？”

column1: Now I just need to figure out where and when to give it to him.
column2: “现在我只要想好在什么地方、什么时候给他。”

column1: Of course not. Thank you again.
column2: “当然不介意。再次谢谢你。”

column1: Oh, wow! Is that what I think it is? Where'd you find one of these?
column2: “哦，哇！这就是我想的那个东西吗？你从哪儿弄到这种东西的？”

column1: Sounds good, right? Of course it does. In order to complete the project, I'll need a diamond, a ruby, a sapphire, an emerald, an onyx, and... oh, let's say a ring. Come find me when you have all of those things, and I will make for you a miracle.
column2: “听起来不错，对吧？当然不错。要完成这个项目，我需要一颗钻石、一颗红宝石、一颗蓝宝石、一颗祖母绿、一颗缟玛瑙，还有……哦，就说一枚戒指吧。这些都齐了就来找我，我会为你造出一件奇迹。”

column1: That's very generous. I know you'll do it justice.
column2: “你太慷慨了。我知道你不会亏待它。”

column1: This is perfect. He's going to love it.
column2: “这太完美了。他一定会喜欢。”

column1: Travelers? Well, I don't have anything for you. Rest up in the yard if you need to, but best be moving on. Unless...
column2: “旅人？嗯，我没什么能给你们的。要歇脚就在院子里歇，不过最好还是赶路。除非……”

column1: Very well. Make yourself comfortable, but leave me in peace. This will take several hours, and I must not be disturbed.
column2: “很好。你自己随意，不过让我清静。这要花好几个小时，绝不能打扰我。”

column1: We've just made history! Nobody's ever accomplished such a thing before! I'll have to revise my method and figure out how to strengthen the braid. I've got a lot of work ahead of me, but I would not have come this far without your help. Take the ring with my thanks!
column2: “我们刚刚创造了历史！以前从没有人做成过这种事！我得修正我的方法，想办法强化这道编织。我前面还有好多工作，可没有你的帮助我到不了这一步。带着我的谢意，把戒指拿走吧！”

column1: Well, I need a little favor. I need a smith, but this is kind of a secret, so I can't have the work done at my own camp. I was hoping you could help me out.
