column2: “嗯，我想请你帮个小忙。我需要一个铁匠，可这事得保密，不能在我自己的营地做。希望你能帮我。”

column1: Well, I've figured out how to do it!  ... I think. Enchantments are a more permanent and controlled form of magic. It should be possible for me to braid all five veins of mana together into a single object. The problem is that the materials necessary for such an experiment are beyond my means.
column2: “嗯，我已经想出办法了！  ……我觉得。附魔是更持久、也更可控的一种魔法。我应当能把全部五条法力魔脉编织进同一件物品里。问题是，这种实验所需的材料超出了我的能力。”

column1: Wow, working with that bezoar was really inspiring! I'm just bursting with ideas right now! I have to jot these down while they're still fresh. You don't mind if I excuse myself?
column2: “哇，摆弄那块牛黄真是太有灵感了！我现在想法快溢出来了！得趁新鲜把它们记下来。你不介意我先失陪吧？”

column1: Yes, well I am an enchanter-smith, you see. You probably already know that there are five veins of mana, and it is practically impossible to use more than one at a time without their unique qualities simply collapsing into the null-vein, Arcus.
column2: “是啊，我是个附魔铁匠。你大概已经知道，世上有五条法力魔脉，一次用超过一条几乎不可能，否则它们各自的特性就会直接坍缩成空脉 Arcus。”

column1: You actually went through that hellish ritual? And... then you thought to bring it to me?
column2: “你真的熬过了那场地狱般的仪式？而且……然后还想到把它带给我？”

column1: You again. Remember, in order to make that ring, you'll need to bring me a diamond, a ruby, a sapphire, an emerald, an onyx, and the base ring.
column2: “又是你。记住，要做那枚戒指，你得带给我一颗钻石、一颗红宝石、一颗蓝宝石、一颗祖母绿、一颗缟玛瑙，还有那枚当基底的戒指。”

column1: You... you actually have them all! I am ready. Shall I begin?
column2: “你……你真的全都有了！我准备好了。要我开始吗？”

column1: This is the best I can do. I shall have to hope that this seal holds until someone comes along with enough strength to destroy those spirits once and for all.
column2: “我能做的只有这些了。只能希望这道封印撑得住，直到出现一个有足够力量的人，把那些灵体彻底消灭。”

column1: Alright, I'm gone! Have fun with the purging and stuff!
column2: “好了，我走了！净化什么的，你们玩得开心！”

column1: Are you new? You can use the other bed if you want. We're all brothers and sisters here.
column2: “你是新来的吗？想用另一张床的话就用。在这儿我们都是兄弟姐妹。”

column1: Assassins! Protect the master!
column2: “刺客！保护主人！”

column1: He's around here somewhere. He has black hair and the body of a self-absorbed patriarch. If you want the key to pass through to Lord Frico's castle, you'll go and kill Grae for me.
column2: “他就在这附近。黑头发，一副自我陶醉的族长身子。你要是想要通往 Frico 领主城堡的钥匙，就去替我把 Grae 杀了。”

column1: He's dead? Excellent! Here is your key as promised.
column2: “他死了？好极了！这是答应你的钥匙。”

column1: I'm not one of them, I swear! I just came here for the free sex!
column2: “我发誓，我不是他们的人！我就是来免费做爱的！”

column1: I'm sorry, I'm quite tired. Don't mind me though, use the bed if you need it.
column2: “抱歉，我实在累了。不过别管我，需要的话就用这张床。”

column1: Maybe we can cut a deal, yeah? You let me go and I'll give you some keys! You can loot the place, and I'll quietly fuck off! Come on, that's a good deal, right?
column2: “也许咱们能做笔交易，啊？你放我走，我就给你几把钥匙！你们可以把这儿搜刮一遍，我就悄悄滚蛋！拜托，这买卖不错吧？”

column1: No, you aren't here to join us, are you? Travelers looking to pass east, I'd wager. Excellent. It seems I'd worried for nothing.
column2: “不，你们不是来加入我们的，对吧？我敢说，是想往东去的旅人。很好。看来我白担心了。”

column1: Of course. Go on through.
column2: “当然。过去吧。”

column1: Stop right there!
column2: “站住！”

column1: Thanks! I'm sure they have something good stashed somewhere around here. Maybe. Oh, and there's a key for moving into the pass, too, you'll want that one.
column2: “谢了！我肯定他们在这附近藏了点好东西。也许吧。哦，还有一把进隘口用的钥匙，你们会想要那把。”

column1: That little wretch, Grae, came to the commune a few weeks ago, and he's already attracted more attention than any of the others. He could never outshine me, of course, but I worry he might start thinking that he actually has some influence.
column2: “那个小混蛋 Grae 几周前来到这处公社，吸引的注意已经超过了其他所有人。他当然永远盖不过我，可我担心他会开始以为自己真有点影响力。”

column1: Ugh, more? Listen you little worm, I am the one destined to be Frico's queen, so you can just turn around and...
column2: “呃，又来？听好了，你这小虫子，注定成为 Frico 的王后的人是我，所以你最好转身就……”

column1: Well? Go and do it. I'm not giving you the key until Grae is dead.
column2: “怎么？去办啊。Grae 不死，我不会把钥匙给你。”

column1: What's your business taking this route?
column2: “走这条路，你们有何贵干？”

column1: What? How dare you!
column2: “什么？你怎么敢！”

column1: Whoah! Easy, easy! You're here to like... purge the place of vampire-worshippers, right?
column2: “哇！别激动，别激动！你们是来……把这儿的吸血鬼崇拜者清掉的，对吧？”

column1: Claire Sand, Lady of the Guilds
column2: “Claire Sand，行会贵妇”

column1: First Lady of Whetners, Lina Maize
column2: “惠特纳的第一夫人，Lina Maize”

column1: Here lies his honour Prime Minister Elgar
column2: “尊敬的首相 Elgar 长眠于此”

column1: King Spar, \nwho wished to be buried neath the blue sky
column2: “国王 Spar，\n愿葬于蓝天之下”

column1: Lord Wyatt, whose magicks saved many lives
column2: “Wyatt 领主，其魔法拯救了许多生命”

column1: Mother Veda, who suffered so others need not
column2: “母亲 Veda，受苦以使他人不必受苦”

column1: Olivia Wise, who fought for common folk
column2: “Olivia Wise，为平民而战”

column1: Prince Kalf, who never saw the sun
column2: “王子 Kalf，从未见过太阳”

column1: Samuel Bright, beloved poet
column2: “Samuel Bright，受人爱戴的诗人”

column1: Tam Brennan, Queen's Maid
column2: “Tam Brennan，女王的侍女”

column1: This man died to protect Princess Chelsea. \nWe know not his name.
column2: “此人为保护公主 Chelsea 而死。\n我们不知其名。”

column1: Windyssa, mother to the motherless
column2: “Windyssa，无母者之母”

column1: only worms remember me
column2: “只有虫子还记得我”

column1: Anyway, I think I'll help these guys clean up a bit before moving on. There are a few monsters around that I dodged earlier, so watch yourself.
column2: “总之，我想先帮他们收拾一下再走。附近还有几只我先前躲开的怪物，你自己小心。”

column1: I don't know what we would have done if you hadn't showed up. Thank you.
column2: “要是你没出现，我不知道我们该怎么办。谢谢你。”

column1: I knew this detour was a trap, I just knew it.
column2: “我就知道这条绕路是个陷阱，我就知道。”

column1: I thought that I could get them to fight back by setting an example, but there were too many. It would've been a slaughter.
column2: “我以为做个榜样就能让他们还手，可人太多了。那会变成一场屠杀。”

column1: I'm not even with these guys actually, I was just walking them through the pass. They seemed like they could use the help. Ugh, I'm going to get myself killed at this rate.
column2: “其实我根本不是他们一伙的，我只是护送他们穿过隘口。他们看上去用得上帮忙。唉，照这样下去我非把自己弄死不可。”

column1: Out of the way, folks! Heads down and you'll be okay!
column2: “让开，大伙儿！低下头就没事！”

column1: We got them! That was amazing!
column2: “我们搞定他们了！太厉害了！”

column1: We wouldn't have come out of that alive if you hadn't come along.
column2: “要不是你来了，我们不可能活着出来。”

column1: Well, that was more exciting than I was hoping this trip was going to be.
column2: “好吧，这可比我希望的这趟行程刺激多了。”

column1: What the... we got some idiots playing hero over here. Take 'em out!
column2: “搞什么……这边有几个白痴在扮英雄。干掉他们！”

column1: Whew, good job there. Sorry I didn't jump in, I was trying to make sure none of those bastards broke off to take a hostage.
column2: “呼，干得不错。抱歉我没冲进去，我在盯着，免得那些混蛋分出去抓人质。”

column1: Wow, that was some fight! I don't know what we'd have done if you hadn't come along!
column2: “哇，这一架打得真够劲！要是你没来，真不知道我们会怎么样！”

column1: The darkness keeps her hidden, the darkness keeps her safe.
column2: “黑暗让她隐匿，黑暗让她平安。”

column1: Bastards, all of them! I've hardly got enough room in here to think, let alone move, but I need to come up with a plan to get away from these insane cultists. Who knows what they plan to do to me?
column2: “全是混蛋！我在这儿连想事情的地方都不够，更别说动一动，可我得想办法摆脱这些疯狂的邪教徒。谁知道他们想把我怎样？”

column1: Test subjects one and three were given the blue formula. Zombification occurred within 5 hours. Two and four were given the red formula, and are ready for mana immersion.
column2: “1号与3号受试者被给予蓝色配方。5小时内发生僵尸化。2号与4号被给予红色配方，已准备好进行法力浸泡。”

column1: I was prepared for something a good deal more macabre when I first entered the estate, so imagine my surprise to find myself greeted by such civilized statuary.
column2: “我初进这处宅邸时，原以为会撞见阴森可怖得多的东西，因此当如此文明的雕像来迎接我，那份惊讶可想而知。”

column1: My host must have caught me staring, for he launched into a most thorough account of the history of the pieces. Had I been less tired, I'd have listened more earnestly, but I excused myself early. The agreed-upon price for these accomodations will require all my strength.
column2: “主人想必察觉我盯着看，于是把这些作品的来历详详细细讲了一遍。我若没这么疲倦，本会听得更认真些，可我早早告了退。这住处说定的代价，要耗尽我全部的力气。”

column1: I'm just putting a fresh log on the fire. Come on in and make yourself at home.
column2: “我刚往火里添了根新柴。进来吧，把这儿当自己家。”

column1: Why hello, deary,
column2: “哟，你好呀，亲爱的，”

column1: Even if you managed to talk me into it, I have a lot of trees to fell. I've already been paid for it and I can't leave until the job is done. You understand.
column2: “就算你真把我说服了，我也还有一大堆树要砍。钱我已经收了，活干完之前不能走。你明白。”

column1: I see. Well, if you don't mind, I've got a lot of work to do. If there's nothing else, I should get to it.
column2: “明白了。嗯，你要是不介意，我还有不少活。要是没别的事，我该去干了。”

column1: Oh ho, is that so? That's quite a thing to ask for, you know.
column2: “哦呵，是这么回事？你这要求可真不小，知道吧。”

column1: Oh, I almost forgot. Can't leave my favorite axe behind.
column2: “哦，差点忘了。可不能把我最喜欢的斧头落下。”

column1: Oh, hello. Not a lot of visitors way out here. Did you need something?
column2: “哦，你好。这地方偏得很，没什么客人。你需要什么吗？”

column1: Sorry, what was it you wanted again?
column2: “抱歉，你刚才想要什么来着？”

column1: Was that you making all that noise out back? You cut down all those trees?
column2: “后面那么大动静是你弄出来的？那些树都是你砍的？”

column1: Well, I ain't got shit to do now. Guess I'll just relax for now. Thanks!
column2: “行了，我现在屁事没有。看来先歇着吧。谢了！”

column1: Well, fuck.
Well, you scratched my back, so it's only fair I scratch yours, right? Just give me a minute to gather up some things.
column2: “行啊，你帮了我，我也该回你一把，对吧？给我一分钟，我去收拾点东西。”

column1:
Lucky I, to find such loot
ungrabbed by giants' greedy hands,
but now I think it's time to boot
in search of other wealthy lands.
column2:
“我真走运，寻得这般财物
未被巨人贪婪的手抢走，
可如今我想该开路了
再去另寻富饶之地。”

column1: Bring me one of them gold potions, alright? That should get me on my feet and in fighting shape again.
column2: “给我弄一瓶那种黄金药水来，行不？那就能让我重新站起来，恢复能打的身子。”

column1: Damn, that's the good stuff, isn't it?
column2: “该死，这东西真带劲，是不是？”

column1: I figured I was dead, but I found dry land again and made my way up here to this lighthouse. Whoever lit this thing saved me life, or what's left of it anyway.
column2: “我以为自己死定了，可又摸到了陆地，一路爬上这座灯塔。不管是谁点亮了这东西，都算救了我的命，或者说，救下了我还剩的那条命。”

column1: I was thrown clear of the ship, and I saw him. The thing what sunk us. It was all darkness and churning, but I saw him. Then I spied this light, so I swim toward it for all I'm worth.
column2: “我被甩出了船，然后我看见他了。那个把我们弄沉的东西。四周全是黑暗和翻搅的水，可我看见他了。接着我瞅见这盏灯，就拼了命朝它游。”

column1: I'd like to come with you. You're my crew, after all, but me belly was torn open on the rocks. It ain't bleeding too bad right now, but every time I stand up and move around it gets worse.
column2: “我想跟你们走。你们毕竟是我的船员。可我的肚子在礁石上被撕开了。这会儿血流得还不算太凶，可我每次站起来走动，就会更糟。”

column1: I'm a man of my word, as you know. You just say the word, and I'm with you.
column2: “你知道，我说话算话。你一开口，我就跟你走。”

column1: You got the potion? I know those ones are rare, but I don't think anything less is going to do the trick.
column2: “那种药水拿到了吗？我知道那东西稀有，可我觉得差一点的都解决不了。”

column1: You! I thought for certain you'd all drowned out there!
column2: “是你！我还以为你们全淹死在外面了！”

column1: ... it is a profound shame to have such a gift refused.
column2: “……这样的礼物遭人拒绝，是极大的耻辱。”

column1: A Bogani stone is really just a bezoar. The hopeful orc imbibes a seed concoction to begin the process, and then the stone grows in his gut.
column2: “Bogani 石其实就是一块牛黄。心怀期冀的兽人服下一种种子配成的药，过程由此开始，然后石头便在他肚子里生长。”

column1: A Bogani stone?
column2: “Bogani 石？”

column1: A short length of your gut was utterly destroyed, but I removed it and reconnected what was left. You probably won't even notice.
column2: “你有一小段肠子彻底毁了，但我把它切除，又把剩下的接了起来。你大概甚至不会察觉。”

column1: Ah, finally awake! You've nothing to worry about, everything went well.
column2: “啊，终于醒了！你没什么可担心的，一切都很顺利。”

column1: Ah, then I will not insist, but it is your loss, I assure you!
column2: “啊，那我便不强求，不过我向你保证，这是你的损失！”

column1: All finished. I trust you feel well?
column2: “都结束了。我想你感觉还好吧？”

column1: Alright. See you soon, then.
column2: “好。那回头见。”

column1: An orc man! Most orc men would kneel at a simple asking. He must be magnificent indeed for you to want to court him so.
column2: “一个兽人男人！你只要开口一求，大多数兽人男人就会跪下。你愿意这样追求他，他一定确实了不起。”

column1: An orc man, actually.
column2: “其实是个兽人男人。”

column1: And here you go, one cold tea coming right up! Enjoy!
column2: “给，一杯冰茶这就来！好好喝！”

column1: And the stone? How did it turn out?
column2: “那石头呢？结果如何？”

column1: Any other healer might destroy the stone in the process, and after all your suffering, you'll be wanting to keep it.
column2: “换作别的治疗师，过程中也许会把石头毁掉，而你受了这么多苦，一定会想留下它。”

column1: Applesauce.
column2: “苹果酱。”

column1: Are you hungry then? Well, that's what it's there for! It's all-you-can eat for one price. 400$ and you can help yourselves.
column2: “那是饿了？嘿，摆出来就是让人吃的！一份价钱吃到饱。400$，自己动手。”

column1: As it happens, I have a great deal of personal interest in orcish courtship right now.
column2: “碰巧，我眼下对兽人的求爱格外有兴趣。”

column1: Best stay out of the church. We don't use it, and if it collapses, I'm not sending someone in to pull you out.
column2: “最好别进那座教堂。我们不用它，塌了的话，我不会派人进去把你拖出来。”

column1: But... I don't really think you can afford this right now. Come back when you've got more money!
column2: “可是……我真不觉得你现在买得起。等钱多点再来！”

column1: Come again when you feel weary!
column2: “觉得疲乏时，再来便是！”

column1: Come back when you are ready, and I will remove it for you.
column2: “等你准备好了再回来，我会帮你把它取出来。”

column1: Come on now, don't be shy! I just put out a fresh spread!
column2: “来嘛，别害羞！我刚摆好一桌新的！”

column1: Curse away. I'll be waiting, and I'll keep my scalpel sharp and oiled.
column2: “尽管咒。我会等着，手术刀也会磨快、上好油。”

column1: Did you need something, dear? The community house should have everything you need. Best stock up before you head out again.
column2: “需要点什么吗，亲爱的？公共会馆里该有你要的一切。再次上路前最好备足。”

column1: Disrobe while I prepare my things.
column2: “我准备用具的时候，把衣服脱掉。”

column1: Draped in gold? I think you must have me confused for someone else.
column2: “披金？我想你一定认错人了。”

column1: Eventually, however, one of his rivals brought an assassin of his own down upon him, and I was captured. They sent me here, as much to cover up the fact that my order existed as to silence me.
column2: “然而到最后，他的一个对手也派了自己的刺客来对付他，我被抓住了。他们把我送到这儿，既是为了封口，也是为了掩盖我那个修会曾经存在的事实。”

column1: Everyone here has a story, and now you know mine. My days of killing are long behind me, but I am pleased to have been of some service to you.
column2: “这儿每个人都有自己的故事，现在你知道我的了。我杀人的日子早已远去，但能帮上你一些，我很高兴。”

column1: Go to the healer, and ask him of the Bogani stone. This sets the flood into motion.
column2: “去找治疗师，向他打听 Bogani 石。这会让洪水开始涌动。”

column1: Good day, traveler! Come and let me show you the art of somatic healing. I guarantee you will not be disappointed.
column2: “日安，旅人！来，让我向你展示躯体疗愈这门技艺。我保证你不会失望。”

column1: Halt, stranger. You approach the town of Marsaven. You are welcome to enter, but you'll be expected to behave yourselves. Enter the building straight ahead if you're looking to spend some money.
column2: “站住，陌生人。你们走近的是马尔萨文镇。欢迎进来，但得守规矩。想花钱的话，进正前方那栋房子。”

column1: Have you been on the island long? Feels like I've already been here a lifetime.
column2: “你在这岛上待很久了吗？我觉得自己已经在这儿过了一辈子。”

column1: Have you had enough? Is it time to cut the stone free?
column2: “你受够了吗？是时候把石头切出来了吗？”

column1: He is magnificent. Please, tell me about the ritual.
column2: “他很了不起。请告诉我那个仪式。”

column1: He probably doesn't even know what they are, and I can't afford to be debilitated for who knows how long. I'm really sorry for bothering you.
column2: “他大概根本不认得那东西，而我也不能就这么虚弱下去，天知道要多久。真的很抱歉打扰你。”

column1: Hey you. Wanna buy something rare and wonderful?
column2: “嘿，你。想买点稀罕又奇妙的东西吗？”

column1: Hey, you stay away from that! It's not even ready, besides. You want something to eat, you come see me.
column2: “嘿，离那个远点！再说它还没好。想吃东西就来找我。”

column1: Hmm? I'm sorry, I don't have any potions for sale. I think there's a baba in the marketplace if you need some.
column2: “嗯？抱歉，我没有药水可卖。你要是需要，集市上好像有个巫婆。”

column1: How do you feel?
column2: “你感觉如何？”

column1: I Do
column2: “我有兴趣”

column1: I Want One
column2: “我要一颗”

column1: I admit I did not have high expectations of you, but I am impressed. This stone is fine indeed. Larger and smoother than mine, to be sure.
column2: “我承认对你原本期望不高，但我很佩服。这块石头确实很好。比我那块更大，也更光滑，这是肯定的。”

column1: I am flexible with your contribution, but I must insist on 50$ at minimum. It may be simple, but it still requires effort from me. You understand.
column2: “出资多少我可以通融，但最少必须是 50$。这也许简单，仍要我费力气。你明白的。”

column1: I assume you're ready to see your prize! It's hardened up nicely overnight.
column2: “我想你已经准备好看你的成果了！它过了一夜，硬得正好。”

column1: I can count, you know. Come back when you've got enough coin to afford it!
column2: “我会算账，知道不？等你钱够了再来！”

column1: I cannot tell for certain how firm or large it is however, and only you can decide on the limits of your body.
column2: “不过我无法确定它有多硬、有多大，只有你能决定自己身体的限度。”

column1: I do lots of things that are usually the province of men. I can handle it. Please tell me about the stones.
column2: “很多通常属于男人的事，我都做。我扛得住。请跟我讲讲这些石头。”

column1: I don't much care for this place, to be truthful, but I care even less for raw wilderness survival. What a place we've ended up in.
column2: “说实话，我不太喜欢这地方，可我更受不了在荒野里硬熬着活命。我们竟落到了这么个地方。”

column1: I don't normally talk about that, but you've been most generous, so I suppose you deserve to know.
column2: “我通常不谈那个，但你如此慷慨，我想你有资格知道。”

column1: I don't think you-
column2: “我不觉得你——”

column1: I escaped from the prison with relative ease, and thought to make a living here for myself once again as an assassin, but as it turns out, death and pain are in abundant supply here, and there is little demand for more of it.
column2: “我相当轻松地逃出了监狱，本想在这儿重新靠当刺客过活，可结果是，这儿的死亡和痛苦已经过剩，再多也没什么人要。”

column1: I hope so. Thank you for everything.
column2: “希望如此。感谢你做的一切。”

column1: I see a choice that welds a golden chain around you forever. The first link of that chain is forged here.
column2: “我看见一个选择，它把一条金链永远焊在你身上。那条链的第一环，便在这里铸成。”

column1: I see a sword that cuts down your foes, and I see red eyes in the dark that cut through your flesh with greater ease still.
column2: “我看见一把斩杀敌人的剑，也看见黑暗中的红眼，它们剖开你的皮肉，比那剑更加轻易。”

column1: I sense that you work well with others, and you should avoid going out-of-doors tomorrow.
column2: “我感觉你跟别人处得来，明天最好别出门。”

column1: I trained in a monastic order, where I learned the limits of the body, and how to manipulate it. They trained me to be an assassin. I was meant to use these techniques to paralyze and subdue, so that the victim would not struggle. For a time, I worked in the employ of a noble lord doing exactly that.
column2: “我在一个隐修会受训，在那里学到了身体的极限，以及如何操控它。他们把我训练成刺客。我本该用这些手法麻痹并制服目标，让受害者无法挣扎。有一段时间，我受雇于一位贵族领主，做的正是这件事。”

column1: I understand. It is not something to be undertaken lightly.
column2: “我理解。这不是可以轻率着手的事。”

column1: I was glad to do it. It does my heart good to see such a dedicated love alive and well in a place like this.
column2: “我很乐意。在这种地方，还能看见如此执着的爱安然无恙，我心里高兴。”

column1: I will still be here when you change your mind!
column2: “等你改变主意，我依然会在这里！”

column1: I would be happy to do this for you, or for any of your companions, for only 50$, though I am quite sure you will find that to be a bargain. If you feel that it is worth more, you can decide the amount for yourself. What say you?
column2: “我很乐意为你，或你的任何同伴做这件事，只要 50$。我很确定你会觉得这是笔划算的买卖。若你觉得它值更多，金额可以自己定。你意下如何？”

column1: I'd put my life on the line for his. I can tolerate it.
column2: “我可以为他的命押上我的命。我忍得住。”

column1: I'll just go on takin' care of the little things, so folk like you are free to take care of the big things.
column2: “我就继续照看着这些小事，好让你们这样的人去管大事。”

column1: I'm going into surgery. Please see that I am not interrupted.
column2: “我要开始手术了。请务必别让人打扰我。”

column1: I'm not here for that. I wanted to know about the Bogani stone.
column2: “我不是为那个来的。我想知道 Bogani 石的事。”

column1: I'm sorry, I don't have any potions for sale right now. You should go to the market if you need something. There's a lovely woman who-
column2: “抱歉，我现在没有药水可卖。你要是需要什么，该去集市。那儿有一位可爱的女人，她——”

column1: I'm sorry, but even at 40$, that's me doin' you a favor. I can't let it go for less.
column2: “抱歉，可就算 40$，也是我在让你。再便宜我不卖。”

column1: I'm sorry, but you can't afford that. Look, I ain't heartless, I won't let you starve. It isn't the good stuff, but maybe this will take the edge off.
column2: “抱歉，可你买不起。听着，我又不是无情的人，不会让你饿着。不是什么好东西，但也许能先垫垫。”

column1: I've got the blood of the underground beast, bottled and preserved. An alchemist can use it to make a youth potion, or you could brew it into a beer that will let you screw for days without stopping!
column2: “我有地底巨兽的血，装瓶保存好了。炼金术士能用它做成青春药水，你也可以把它酿成啤酒，让你连着操上好几天都停不下来！”

column1: If there's nothing else, I have a lot of work yet to do today.
column2: “要是没有别的事，我今天还有不少活要干。”

column1: If you just can't get enough, come back anytime. I've got all you could ever want!
column2: “要是你怎么都觉得不够，随时再来。你想要的，我这儿全都有！”

column1: In the dark, perfection waxes, waiting to be never seen, leash in hand of demon blackest, rapt 'round throat of sunken king. That is what the wind whispers of you.
column2: “黑暗之中，完美渐盈，候着永不见光，缰绳在最黑的恶魔手中，缠紧沉没之王的咽喉。这便是风对你的低语。”

column1: It feels like I'm giving birth to a gnashing demon!
column2: “感觉就像我正在生一只咬牙切齿的恶魔！”

column1: It is a long, agonizing process, but it is meant to be. He holds the stone within his gut for as long as he can possibly tolerate it, and then, it is cut out of his body and polished as a gem. He presents this product of his own flesh and his own suffering to his beloved, usually in a bid for marriage.
column2: “这是一段漫长而痛苦的过程，但本来就该如此。他把石头留在肚子里，能忍多久忍多久，然后从体内切出来，打磨成宝石。他把这件由自己的血肉与痛苦做成的东西献给心上人，通常是为了求婚。”

column1: It is considered a profound honour to receive such a gift, and...
column2: “能收到这样的礼物，被视为极大的荣耀，而且……”

column1: It is quite simple for one who knows how. I search your flesh and bones for your aches, your tension, and your weariness, and I pluck them out and discard them. I will leave you lighter, stronger, and sounder of mind, and I would ask only a pittance of coin for my time.
column2: “对懂得的人来说，这很简单。我在你的皮肉和骨头里找出酸痛、紧绷和疲惫，把它们摘出来扔掉。我会让你更轻快、更强壮、神志更清明，而我的时间只要一点点钱。”

column1: It's a fairly impressive stone, all told.
column2: “总的来说，这块石头相当可观。”

column1: It's fine. Not so much as scratched. I have it in the kiln now to dry out.
column2: “挺好。连一道划痕都没有。我正把它放在窑里烘干。”

column1: It's important.
column2: “这很重要。”

column1: Just 15000$, and it's all yours!
Just leave your clothes and equipment on the floor.
column2: “衣服和装备放在地上就行。”

column1: Keep your nose clean while you're here. I know we all come from questionable backgrounds, but we work hard to keep this place safe. Please respect it.
column2: “在这儿规矩点。我知道我们来路都不干净，但我们费了大力气才让这儿安全。请尊重这一点。”

column1: Looks good, dunnit? Raspberry cold tea, that is, made right here. You've never tasted sweeter, I can promise. Just 50$ if you'd like one.
column2: “看着挺好，是不是？覆盆子冰茶，就在这儿做的。我打包票，你没尝过比这更甜的。想要一杯，只要 50$。”

column1: Me?
Nevermind
column2: “算了”

column1: No! I will see this through! I just... wanted to be certain that nothing was abnormal.
column2: “不！我会做到底的！我只是……想确认没有什么不正常。”

column1: No. I see the firelight, the furs, and golden skin glistening with sweat from your body.
column2: “不。我看见火光、毛皮，还有从你身上透出的、汗水发亮的金色肌肤。”

column1: Not Yet
column2: “还不到时候”

column1: Of course. Goodbye.
column2: “当然。再见。”

column1: Of course. Lay down over here and I'll examine you.
column2: “当然。躺到这边来，我检查一下。”

column1: Oh, hello again. I trust you are feeling well.
column2: “哦，又见面了。相信你感觉不错。”

column1: One day, this whole island may swing from that golden chain. Best weld the seams tightly.
column2: “有朝一日，整座岛也许都会吊在那条金链上晃。接缝最好焊牢。”

column1: Please, I can't stand it any longer! Get this thing out of my body!
column2: “求你了，我再也受不了了！把这东西从我身体里弄出去！”

column1: Right. I will.
column2: “好。我会的。”

column1: Sit there on the bed. This won't take long.
column2: “坐到那张床上。这花不了多久。”

column1: So that is what she meant.
column2: “原来她说的是这个。”

column1: So? Still interested in getting one of these stones?
column2: “所以呢？还想得到一颗这样的石头吗？”

column1: Some of your companions came looking for you, but I told them to come back in the morning. Lay back down, give my salves a chance to heal your wounds, and get some sleep.
column2: “你有几位同伴来找过你，我让他们早上再来。躺回去，让药膏有时间治好你的伤，睡一觉吧。”

column1: Sorry to bother you.
column2: “抱歉打扰。”

column1: Sorry to bother you. I don't need your stone.
column2: “抱歉打扰。我不需要你的石头。”

column1: Take It Out!
column2: “取出来！”

column1: Take it to a competent jeweler, and forge it into something fitting for your lover. I'm sure he will be moved by the gesture.
column2: “把它交给一个够格的珠宝匠，打成配得上你爱人的东西。我相信这个举动会打动他。”

column1: The Bogani were an ancient orc people, and their stones were part of a brutal courtship ritual. You've no interest in that, surely.
column2: “Bogani 是一支古老的兽人部族，他们的石头属于一套残酷的求爱仪式。你对那个肯定没兴趣。”

column1: The healer is in the house near the west exit. Go to him.
column2: “治疗师在西边出口附近的房子里。去找他。”

column1: The stone is forming up nicely.
column2: “石头形成得很好。”

column1: The stones are usually the province of men, though I suppose there's no reason a woman couldn't obtain one.
column2: “这些石头通常是男人的领域，不过我想，女人也不是不能得到一颗。”

column1: Then you'll have to excuse me. I have a lot of herbs to process.
column2: “那恕我失陪。我还有许多草药要处理。”

column1: Then you've just made my day a lot more interesting.
column2: “那你刚让我这一天有意思多了。”

column1: There used to be a grand field here long ago. Oat, I think. I can't remember the last time I had oat. It doesn't matter anyway, the forest swallowed it up long before we arrived.
column2: “很久以前这儿有一大片田。我记得是燕麦。上次吃到燕麦是什么时候，我都想不起来了。反正也不要紧，森林在我们到这儿之前早就把它吞了。”

column1: They are rare and precious, and at once everywhere and worthless. I doubt you have use for such a thing.
column2: “它们既稀有又珍贵，同时又遍地都是、一文不值。我怀疑你用不上这种东西。”

column1: This place is decent enough. Repairing a ruined town is a lot easier than building a new one. I mean, it has to be, right?
column2: “这地方还算凑合。修一座废镇比新建一座容易多了。我是说，肯定是这样，对吧？”

column1: This will knock you out. Drink it and lie down.
column2: “这会让你失去知觉。喝下去，躺下。”

column1: Very well. I already have my tools set aside. Come this way.
column2: “很好。工具我已经备好了。请这边来。”

column1: We get more visitors than I ever expected we would. There are a few small communities, and I think everybody knows that we need each other to survive. Trade is... surprisingly brisk.
column2: “来的人比我原先想的多。附近有几个小聚落，我想大家都明白，要活下去就得互相依靠。买卖……出奇地热闹。”

column1: We'll just close the screen then. You won't be needing any clothes, either.
column2: “那就把屏风拉上。衣服你也不用穿了。”

column1: Well don't wait too long, you hear? It won't stay cold forever, and I'll sell out before long, just you wait and see!
column2: “可别等太久啊，听见没？它不会一直这么凉，我过不了多久就卖光，你等着瞧！”

column1: Well then you got a deal. I hope it serves you well in all your... erm... logging.
column2: “那就算成交。希望它在你那些……呃……伐木的事上好使。”

column1: Well then, you are now officially my guests. You just go on and help yourselves to as much as you like!
column2: “那好，你们现在正式算我的客人了。尽管自己动手，爱吃多少吃多少！”

column1: Well, before the misery sets in, let me say thanks. I might be cursing your name later.
column2: “趁痛苦还没上来，先谢你。过后我也许会咒你的名字。”

column1: Well, it sounds like everything is progressing properly, then.
column2: “嗯，听上去一切都进展正常。”

column1: Well, let's get you alone then!
column2: “那好，就咱俩单独待着吧！”

column1: Well, that's fine. You probably want somethin' fancier anyway.
column2: “行，无所谓。你大概本来就想要更花哨的。”

column1: Well. Bottoms up.
column2: “好。一口干了。”

column1: What is in short supply, however, is comfort, and my techniques are versatile, as you can no doubt attest to. Ever since I began using my talents to remove pain instead of causing it, I have been very busy indeed, and there is something redeeming in that.
column2: “然而紧缺的是舒适，而我的手法用途很广，这一点你无疑深有体会。自从我开始用这本事消除痛苦，而不是制造痛苦，我确实一直非常忙碌，其中也颇有救赎之意。”

column1: Why are you telling me all of this?
column2: “你为什么把这些告诉我？”

column1: Yes, of course, Orum.
column2: “是，当然，Orum。”

column1: Yes, you. The one draped in gold. Come here.
column2: “对，就是你。那个披金的。到这儿来。”

column1: You definitely won't regret it!
column2: “你绝对不会后悔！”

column1: You don't look like the sort who deals in lumber and grain, am I right? I ain't got much in the way of steel, but I can sell you an axe if you want. It's more for fellin' than killin', but it'll do the job sure enough. How's 40$?
column2: “你看着不像做木材和粮食生意的，对吧？我这儿钢家伙不多，不过你想要，我可以卖你一把斧子。它砍树多过杀人，但干这活绝对够。40$ 怎么样？”

column1: You just have a look at what we've got, and give a holler if you want to buy something.
column2: “你们先看看有什么，想买就喊一声。”

column1: You must be impressed with me indeed. For that, I'll use every technique I know. Perhaps you should tell your friends to browse. We may be a while.
column2: “你对我确实印象很深。既然如此，我会把我会的每一种手法都用上。也许你该让朋友们去逛逛。我们可能要好一会儿。”

column1: You should go. Enjoy walking around while you can still do it without pain.
column2: “你该走了。趁现在走路还不疼，好好走走吧。”

column1: You should go. Your companions will come looking for you soon.
column2: “你该走了。你的同伴很快就会来找你。”

column1: You there!
column2: “喂，那边的！”

column1: You will make a grave mistake, but make it you must, for all our sakes. The one to pay the price for that mistake is yet to come. It will not be your burden, nor mine, nor anyone you yet could find.
column2: “你会犯一个重大的错误，但为了我们所有人，你必须犯下它。为这个错误付出代价的人还没到来。那不会是你的担子，也不会是我的，更不会是你现在找得到的任何人的。”

column1: You will not be disappointed. Now, let's have a little privacy.
column2: “你不会失望的。现在，我们私下待一会儿。”

column1: You'll be feeling very bad very soon. Tolerate it as long as you possibly can, and then return to me. I know just the place in the gut where the stone will grow, and I'll be able to get it out with minimal damage to you and to the stone.
column2: “你很快就会非常难受。能忍多久就忍多久，然后再回来找我。我知道石头会在肚子里哪个位置长大，到时能把它取出来，尽量少伤到你，也少伤到石头。”

column1: You'll change your mind sooner or later. Your curiosity will get the better of you! I'll be waiting.
column2: “你迟早会改主意。好奇心会赢过你！我等着。”

column1: You'll come back! The smell will haunt you till you do!
column2: “你会回来的！那股味儿会缠着你，直到你回来！”

column1: You're back, and you are not looking well.
column2: “你回来了，气色可不怎么样。”

column1: You've an orc woman you love dearly, then?
column2: “这么说，你深爱着一位兽人女子？”

column1: You've returned! I am not surprised. If you would like another session, my fee is the same, 50$.
column2: “你回来了！我不意外。若你想再来一次，费用照旧，50$。”

column1: Also, I've never had to give a goblin a pep-talk before so I think you must be something different.
column2: “还有，我以前从没给哥布林打过气，所以我觉得你肯定有点不一样。”

column1: Aren't I? Either I'm a dumb goblin, or I'm a piece of jewelry! I don't know which thought is more disgusting!
column2: “难道不是吗？要么我是个蠢哥布林，要么我是一件首饰！我不知道哪个念头更恶心！”

column1: Because you're one of my men, Borf, and I don't leave my people behind. It doesn't need to be any more complicated than that.
column2: “因为你是我的人，Borf，而我不会丢下自己人。不必比这更复杂。”

column1: Borf!
column2: “Borf！”

column1: Borf! You're gonna be alright!
column2: “Borf！你会没事的！”

column1: Borf, it's not your fault. You tried.
column2: “Borf，这不是你的错。你尽力了。”

column1: Borf, most of us are criminals, and all of us are exiles. I'm sure most people back in Crest would see the whole lot of us as nothing but dumb animals.
column2: “Borf，我们大多是罪犯，而且所有人都是流放者。我敢说，克雷斯特那边大多数人会把我们整个团伙看成纯粹的蠢畜生。”

column1: Can we get moving? Bato had some venison he was going to cook tonight, and I'd rather not miss it.
column2: “能出发了吗？Bato 今晚本来要做鹿肉，我可不想错过。”

column1: Can we get moving? I don't want to be here anymore, and I'm starting to really miss my tent right about now.
column2: “能出发了吗？我不想再待在这儿了，这会儿我开始真的想念我的帐篷。”

column1: Dammit, Borf, we don't have a lot of choice here! We're going to have to fight them!
column2: “该死，Borf，我们没什么选择了！只能跟他们打！”

column1: Fuck it all! You brought this on yourselves!
column2: “去他妈的！这是你们自找的！”

column1: Hey, I know what'll cheer you up. I've got a flank of venison back at the stronghold I was saving for a special occasion. I think maybe tonight's the night.
column2: “嘿，我知道什么能让你打起精神。我在据点留着一块鹿腰肉，本来打算留给特别的日子。我想也许就是今晚了。”

column1: I don't want you to have to die! This is your last chance! Just run!
column2: “我不想让你们非死不可！这是你们最后的机会！快跑！”

column1: I know that! Dammit, why won't they listen?
column2: “我知道！该死，他们为什么不听？”

column1: I'm really looking forward to getting out of this rain. We should finish up and go.
column2: “我真盼着走出这雨。我们该收尾，然后走。”

column1: If they had just walked away, they'd all still be alive. Surely even a dumb animal could figure that out.
column2: “他们当时要是走开，现在全都还活着。就算是头蠢畜生也该想得明白。”

column1: Isn't this... the way it was... supposed to be? Now... the goblins... are dead.
column2: “难道这……不就是……本来该有的样子吗？现在……哥布林……都死了。”

column1: Just dumb animals. That's really all they are, isn't it? Is that all I am too?
column2: “不过是些蠢畜生。他们真就只是这样，对不对？那我也只是这样吗？”

column1: Let's get moving. Bato had some venison he was going to cook tonight, and I've been fantasizing about it all day.
column2: “我们走吧。Bato 今晚本来要做鹿肉，我一整天都在幻想它。”

column1: Maybe you're right. Sorry.
column2: “也许你说得对。对不起。”

column1: One of Us
column2: “自己人”

column1: Sure, Borf.
column2: “行，Borf。”

column1: Sure, Borf. Let's go.
column2: “行，Borf。我们走吧。”

column1: That sounds good, Bato. I'm looking forward to it.
column2: “听起来不错，Bato。我很期待。”

column1: That sounds good, Bato. Thanks.
column2: “听起来不错，Bato。谢谢。”

column1: Those goblins came up against the wrong targets today, but they didn't wallow in their doubts searching for some perfect identity. They lived their lives the way they wanted, and they ended their lives the same way.
column2: “那些哥布林今天找错了对手，可他们没有沉溺在怀疑里，去寻找什么完美的身份。他们按自己想要的方式活，也按同样的方式死。”

column1: Whether you think that puts you in good company or not is up to you, but the way I see it, you're one of us, and just like us, it's up to you to either own it, or to rise above it.
column2: “你觉得这样算不算让你有了好同伴，由你自己判断。可在我看来，你就是我们中的一个，和我们一样，要么认下这一点，要么超越它，都由你决定。”

column1: Who Cares?
column2: “谁在乎？”

column1: Who cares? Do you think anybody else has that figured out either?
column2: “谁在乎？你觉得别人就把这事想明白了吗？”

column1: Why... bother? I... am no different... from them.
column2: “何必……呢？我……和他们……没有分别。”

column1: Why? Why couldn't I make them listen?
column2: “为什么？为什么我没法让他们听进去？”

column1: You aren't like that Borf.
column2: “你不是那样的，Borf。”

column1: You guys really don't know who you're messing with here! Turn around and leave! Nobody has to get hurt!
column2: “你们根本不知道自己在惹谁！转身离开！谁都不必受伤！”

column1: You know, I've got a flank of venison back at the stronghold I was saving for a special occasion. I think maybe tonight's the night.
column2: “说起来，我在据点留着一块鹿腰肉，本来打算留给特别的日子。我想也许就是今晚了。”

column1: You should give them a little more credit. Maybe, you spending all your time worrying about who you are and what you should be means the stupid one here is you.
column2: “你该多给他们一点肯定。也许，你把所有时间都花在担心自己是谁、该成为什么人，说明这儿真正蠢的是你。”

column1: You're right. Thanks for helping me sort it out.
column2: “你说得对。谢谢你帮我理清楚。”

column1: Ah! It's too hot!
column2: “啊！太烫了！”

column1: All my wounds, my losses, my scars. They're worth it, for leading me to you.
column2: “我受过的伤、失去的一切、留下的伤疤，都值得，因为它们把我领到了你面前。”

column1: Always. Lead the way!
column2: “随时。你带路！”

column1: And what on earth is that noise?
column2: “还有，那到底是什么动静？”

column1: Anyway, I'm beat. See you in the morning.
column2: “总之，我累坏了。早上见。”

column1: Bring me low, you damn fool!
column2: “把我压倒，你这该死的傻瓜！”

column1: Chief? What are you doing out of bed?
column2: “首领？你怎么起来了？”

column1: Getting here was a harder hike than I'm used to. It looked promising from that watchtower, but I don't think this place is stronghold material.
column2: “走到这儿，比我习惯的路难走多了。从那座瞭望塔看过来还挺有盼头，可我不觉得这地方适合做据点。”

column1: I got worried when you didn't come back, and then I heard that noise. Are you alright?
column2: “你一直没回来，我担心了，然后又听见那动静。你还好吗？”

column1: I haven't ever met a man like you before. The things I feel when I watch you fight, or when I feel your eyes on my skin, they are savage and desperate in ways I can't describe.
column2: “我从来没遇见过像你这样的男人。看着你战斗的时候，或者感觉到你的目光落在我皮肤上的时候，那些感觉野蛮而拼命，我根本形容不出来。”

column1: I just wanted to make sure you were alright. It sounds like you know what you're doing, so I'm going back to bed.
column2: “我只是想确认你没事。听起来你知道自己在干什么，那我回去睡了。”

column1: I know you aren't Tsarathi, so I wouldn't expect you to know about those, but you probably get the idea by now that orc cities have way too many men and not enough women.
column2: “我知道你不是察拉思人，所以不指望你知道这些，可你现在大概也明白了，兽人的城市男人太多，女人不够。”

column1: I need to drag my tusks through the hair of your chest and forge us into a single flesh!
column2: “我要把獠牙拖过你的胸毛，把我们锻成同一具肉体！”

column1: I never imagined I'd meet such an amazing woman on this island, of all places. You are beautiful and powerful, and I crave you like the night sky craves the sun.
column2: “我从没想过，偏偏在这座岛上，会遇见如此了不起的女人。你美丽，又强大，我渴求你，就像夜空渴求太阳。”

column1: I slept really well, thanks. Ready for another day on the road?
column2: “我睡得很好，谢谢。准备好再赶一天路了吗？”

column1: I thought there might be enough life left in it to get it running one more time, so I opened the valves and lit the furnace.
column2: “我以为它还剩一口气，能再转一次，所以打开了阀门，把炉子点着了。”

column1: I was one of those boys. No idea who my parents are, because I was raised by captains and swordsmen.
column2: “我就是那些男孩里的一个。我不知道父母是谁，把我养大的是队长和剑士。”

column1: I'm ready. Let's go.
column2: “我准备好了。我们走。”

column1: I'm sorry.
column2: “对不起。”

column1: Iday, Bru. Slept well?
column2: “Iday，Bru。睡得好吗？”

column1: Iday, Brudum. Slept well?
column2: “Iday，Brudum。睡得好吗？”

column1: It's a military school, or at least it used to be. I grew up in one just like it back in Tsarath.
column2: “这是一所军校，至少曾经是。我就是在察拉思一所一模一样的军校里长大的。”

column1: It's hard to tell for sure without daylight, but I think you're right.
column2: “没有天光很难确定，不过我想你是对的。”

column1: Let's find out if I'm lucky or not.
column2: “看看我运气好不好。”

column1: Nazar!
column2: “Nazar！”

column1: No, no, don't get me wrong! It's a very typical upbringing for an orc boy, and I look back on it fondly. I have some very special memories of that school, and this place reminds me of that.
column2: “不，不，别误会！对兽人男孩来说这非常典型，我回想起来还挺怀念。那所学校有些很特别的回忆，这地方让我想起那些。”

column1: Of course I do.
column2: “我当然信任你。”

column1: Of course. Goodnight Nazar.
column2: “当然。晚安，Nazar。”

column1: See you in the morning, I guess.
column2: “那就早上见了。”

column1: Shall we go, Id Brudum?
column2: “我们走吧，Id Brudum？”

column1: Shut up and kiss me, Nazar.
column2: “闭嘴，亲我，Nazar。”

column1: So why are you naked?
column2: “所以你为什么光着身子？”

column1: Sure thing. I won't be too much longer anyhow.
column2: “行。反正我也快好了。”

column1: Surrender them?
column2: “交出去？”

column1: Tell me you feel this too! Tell me you need to command my flesh as badly as I need to command yours!
column2: “告诉我你也有这种感觉！告诉我，你也一样迫切地需要主宰我的肉体，就像我需要主宰你的！”

column1: That's right. Just hand 'em over and never look back. One less mouth to feed, one less kid to pay attention to.
column2: “对。交出去，然后别再回头看。少一张要喂的嘴，少一个要管的孩子。”

column1: The water will last longer if we share.
column2: “一起用的话，水能撑更久。”

column1: This place felt familiar to me ever since we got here. It was bugging me, and I couldn't shake it, so I decided to come take a look.
column2: “从我们到这儿起，这地方就让我觉得熟悉。它一直烦我，甩不掉，所以我决定来看看。”

column1: This place has a rainwell and a boiler. It's old, but the school where I grew up had a setup just like it.
column2: “这儿有一口集雨井，还有一台锅炉。旧是旧，可我长大的那所学校，装置一模一样。”

column1: Too hot is perfect!
column2: “太烫才完美！”

column1: We're lucky we found this place all the way out here. I wouldn't call it luxury, but it beats sleeping on the ground.
column2: “我们运气好，在这么偏的地方找到了这儿。说不上奢侈，可比睡地上强。”

column1: Well enough. Let's pack up and get moving.
column2: “还行。收拾一下出发吧。”

column1: Well, in order to make things easier on parents trying to conceive girls, they have these military schools where you can go and just surrender boys of any age.
column2: “嗯，为了让想生女孩的父母轻松一点，他们办了这些军校，任何年纪的男孩都可以送去，直接交出来。”

column1: What are you doing here?
column2: “你在这儿做什么？”

column1: What do you think? Worth it, right?
column2: “你觉得呢？值吧？”

column1: Why don't you leave your clothes by the door and come find out?
column2: “你何不把衣服留在门口，进来自己看？”

column1: Worth it. You haven't disappointed me yet!
column2: “值。你到现在还没让我失望过！”

column1: Yeah, of course, I'm fine. Didn't mean to make you worry.
column2: “嗯，当然，我没事。不是故意让你担心。”

column1: Yeah. I figure that it will.
column2: “嗯。我想是这样。”

column1: You embrace the world like a brazen, naked beast, and I cannot help but stare. Your immodesty excites me.
column2: “你像一头厚颜的赤裸野兽那样拥抱这个世界，我忍不住盯着看。你的不知羞让我兴奋。”

column1: You parade your naked body before me again and again, and my hunger for you grows more ferocious by the day!
column2: “你一次次把赤裸的身体在我面前招摇，我对你的饥渴一天比一天凶猛！”

column1: You really do trust me, don't you?
column2: “你是真的信任我，对不对？”

column1: Your breasts are magnificent. I can scarcely push their image out of my mind.
column2: “你的乳房美极了。那画面我几乎没法从脑子里赶出去。”

column1: Please be courteous and leave the shelter as clean as you found it.\n\n-Royal Highway Commission
column2: “请保持礼貌，离开时让庇护所和你来时一样整洁。\n\n——皇家公路委员会”

column1: Ah, this place brings back memories. If I had a coin for every night I've spent in a bandit fort, I'd be a rich man!
column2: “啊，这地方让人想起从前。要是我在强盗寨里过夜的每一晚都能换成一枚硬币，我早就发财了！”

column1: Anyway, what's the plan? We camping here?
column2: “总之，计划是什么？我们在这儿扎营吗？”

column1: Well, maybe not too rich. I could afford a new shirt, at least.
column2: “嗯，也许也没那么富。至少一件新衬衫还买得起。”

column1: . It's a song about remembering home, even when you're far away, and about being able to find your way back.
column2: “。这是一首歌，唱的是身在远方也要记住家，还要能找到回去的路。”

column1: And does Lukatt feel like home to you?
column2: “那卢卡特让你觉得像家吗？”

column1: Anyway, we'll camp here for tonight, but let's not build the fire inside. It'll smoke us out before morning for sure.
column2: “总之，今晚我们在这儿扎营，但别在屋里生火。不到早上，烟肯定把我们熏出去。”

column1: But that's fine. I get moments like these, and I am happy.
column2: “可这也没什么。我能有这样的片刻，我就高兴。”

column1: Do you hear it? The timbre of this old building is great.
column2: “你听见了吗？这栋老房子的音色好极了。”

column1: Do you know what it's called?
column2: “你知道它叫什么吗？”

column1: Do you want to go home, Rosaline?
column2: “你想回家吗，Rosaline？”

column1: Everybody needs a home, don't they? The poor family that sold me to a dance troupe sure isn't it. The people who raised me to be a killer aren't it either. Now, here, surrounded by outcasts and monsters...
column2: “谁都需要一个家，不是吗？把我卖给舞团的那户穷人家当然不算。把我养大、训练成杀手的那些人也不算。现在，在这儿，身边尽是被放逐的人和怪物……”

column1: For what it's worth, I know how you feel. I'm gevaudan. Do you know what that means?
column2: “不管怎样，我懂你的感受。我是 gevaudan。你知道这是什么意思吗？”

column1: Hey, I haven't seen Wisaka in a little while. Did you see where he went?
column2: “嘿，我有一会儿没看见 Wisaka 了。你看见他去哪儿了吗？”

column1: Hmm? Oh sorry, I was distracted. This place has a really interesting sound to it, don't you think?
column2: “嗯？哦，抱歉，我走神了。这地方的声音很有意思，你不觉得吗？”

column1: Huh. That's such a simple question. I wish the answer could be that simple.
column2: “呵。这问题真简单。真希望答案也能这么简单。”

column1: I don't really hear anything, but you hear a lot better than I do, so you're probably right.
column2: “我其实什么都没听见，可你比我听得清楚多了，所以你大概是对的。”

column1: I get to wear nicer clothes, though. Grant can look human enough, but he dresses in rags that he can just tie back on after he explodes out of them.
column2: “不过我能穿更体面的衣服。Grant 看着可以挺像人，可他穿的是破布，身子炸出来之后再绑回去就行。”

column1: I heard it once, a long time ago. A woman was singing it over the body of a dead man, her husband, I think. I hadn't properly learned the language at the time so I couldn't understand the words, but her voice cut through me, and I never forgot it.
column2: “我很久以前听过一次。一个女人在一具男尸前唱着它，我想那是她的丈夫。那时候我还没真正学会那种语言，听不懂歌词，可她的声音穿透了我，我再也没忘记。”

column1: I just have more questions, and no satisfying answers at all. Sorry, Wisaka.
column2: “我只是问题更多了，一个让人满意的答案都没有。抱歉，Wisaka。”

column1: I'm okay with it if you guys are. Wisaka?
column2: “你们觉得行我就行。Wisaka？”

column1: I'm pretty sure he didn't leave. I'll see if he's inside.
column2: “我挺确定他没离开。我去看看他在不在里面。”

column1: I, however, cannot shapeshift at all. What you see is what you get, so unlike other werewolves, I can't blend in with humans no matter how hard I try.
column2: “可我完全不会变身。你们看到的就是我，所以不像别的狼人，我再怎么努力也混不进人类里。”

column1: Is this home? Could it be? Can someone like me ever find a place that feels like home?
column2: “这是家吗？会是吗？像我这样的人，还能找到一个让人觉得像家的地方吗？”

column1: It means I'm a werewolf more than once, basically. Neither of my parents were werewolves, but they were both carriers, so I got a double dose.
column2: “意思是，我基本上算是不止一次的狼人。我父母都不是狼人，可他们都是携带者，所以我得了双份。”

column1: It's not all bad, though. I don't wreck my clothes every five minutes like some other werewolves do.
column2: “不过也不全是坏事。我不会像有些狼人那样，每隔五分钟就把衣服撑烂。”

column1: It's... hard to say. No satisfying answer, I suppose.
column2: “这……很难说。我想，没有让人满意的答案。”

column1: No, I've never heard the word before. What does it mean?
column2: “不，我从没听过这个词。什么意思？”

column1: Of course! Anything for an audience!
column2: “当然！为了观众，什么都行！”

column1: Seems somehow fitting that I'd hear it again in a place like this.
column2: “在这样的地方再听见它，倒也合适。”

column1: That song! I haven't heard that song since I was a little girl. Since before I started training to be a dancer.
column2: “那首歌！从我还是小女孩起就没再听过。那还是我开始接受舞者训练之前的事。”

column1: The building is in good shape. It's a shame it's so small.
column2: “这房子还挺完好。可惜太小了。”

column1: Would you play the song again?
column2: “你愿意把那首歌再奏一遍吗？”

column1: You think it'll be alright for us for tonight?
column2: “你觉得我们今晚住这儿行吗？”

column1: You've probably seen Grant shapeshifting, right? He's quite good at it.
column2: “你大概见过 Grant 变身，对吧？他相当在行。”

column1: Alright, fine. You're obviously not with them, so if you're just travelling the road, travel it away from me.
column2: “行了，好吧。你显然不是跟他们一伙的。你要只是赶路，就离我远点赶你的路。”

column1: Hey now, this weren't my plan! You can keep your gold!
column2: “嘿，这可不是我的主意！金子你们留着！”

column1: I said empty your purse, you deaf cow! Of course, if you'd prefer, we can always just pick the coins out of the mess of your corpse.
column2: “我说了，把钱袋倒空，你这聋母牛！当然，你要是更乐意，我们也可以从你那摊烂尸里把硬币抠出来。”

column1: More? How many of you must I kill before you leave me in peace?
column2: “还有？我还得杀多少个，你们才肯让我清静？”

column1: That is what I thought you said.
column2: “我果然没听错。”

column1: What... what in the... you killed Samwell!
column2: “什……这他妈的……你杀了 Samwell！”

column1: You want to say that again? I didn't quite hear you.
column2: “你想再说一遍吗？我没太听清。”

column1: A frog told me that something dangerous is coming, and I don't care to find out what. You want the hut, you can have it.
column2: “一只青蛙告诉我，有危险的东西要来了，我可不想弄清是什么。你要这小屋，就拿去。”

column1: Come to loot and destroy, have you? Well, be my guest. I was just leaving anyhow.
column2: “来抢来砸的，是吧？请便。反正我正要走。”

column1: What? Is someone there?
column2: “什么？有人在吗？”

column1: A sad day then. At least I'll get to die surrounded by my treasures.
column2: “那今天真是可悲。至少我能死在自己的珍宝中间。”

column1: Ack! How did you get in here!?
column2: “啊！你们怎么进来的！？”

column1: I've tried to be civil, and those hits really did hurt, but finishing me off isn't that easy. Now I'll just be taking my stuff back and be on my way.
column2: “我已经尽量客气了，那些打也确实疼，可要取我性命可没那么容易。现在我要把我的东西拿回去，然后走人。”

column1: Oh deary me, trying to steal from my collection are we. Just because you thought you killed me, you think that this place now belongs to you? While I may not be a fighter, I have survived here for quite a while.
column2: “哎呀呀，想偷我的收藏是吧。就因为你们以为把我杀了，就觉得这地方现在归你们了？我也许不会打架，可我在这儿活了相当久了。”

column1: There you go. Everything else in here is too sentimental for me to part with, and wouldn't be useful to you anyhow. So please just leave and never come back.
column2: “拿去吧。这里其余的东西我都太有感情，舍不得撒手，对你们反正也没用。所以请离开，永远别再回来。”

column1: Very good, very good. Now wait here a tick, will you? You're going to like this.
column2: “很好，很好。在这儿稍等片刻，好吗？你们会喜欢这个的。”

column1: Well, I know better than to fight when I'm outmatched. If you let me go, I'll give you some good things from my plunders. What do you say?
column2: “唉，打不过的时候我可不会硬打。你们放我走，我就从掠来的东西里拿几件好的给你们。怎么样？”

column1: ... I don't intend to let your shoulders go cold ever again.
column2: “……我再也不打算让你的肩膀受凉了。”

column1: Am I going mad with worry? Perhaps. Are they dreams, or are they visions? Perhaps this is Leviathan sending me madness to punish my lapse.
column2: “我是忧心得快疯了吗？也许吧。那是梦，还是异象？也许是 Leviathan 降下疯狂，惩罚我的失职。”

column1: And... it's not without its appeals.
column2: “而且……这种生活也不是全无吸引力。”

column1: Another life I'm glad to be rid of. This life is harder, but it's real.
column2: “另一段人生，我很高兴已经摆脱了。这种生活更难，但它是真的。”

column1: Generations ago, long before the days of my grandmother's mother, Lukatt was a hive of beasts and worse. Orcs and men came to conquer it, but no matter how ferociously they struggled, the island always brought them low.
column2: “数代以前，远在我祖母的母亲所处的年月之前，卢卡特是野兽与更糟之物的巢窟。兽人与人类前来征服，可无论他们如何凶猛地挣扎，这座岛总能把他们击垮。”

column1: Gloried... he... hear... voices... echo... love
column2: “荣耀……他……听……声音……回响……爱”

column1: He mouths the same word over and over again. Bertan. Pertan. Mortan. Purtan. I can't make it out clearly. Why does it seem so important?
column2: “他一遍遍用口型念着同一个词。Bertan。Pertan。Mortan。Purtan。我辨不清楚。它为什么显得如此重要？”

column1: I have revealed the secret to two others before now: my Lord-husband, and my prime minister. They strive now to find some way to appease Leviathan and spare us all. Hopefully the focus on me and my deeds will afford them some fortune.
column2: “在此之前，我已把这秘密透露给另外两人：我的夫君主上，以及我的首相。他们此刻正竭力寻找办法安抚 Leviathan，好放过我们所有人。希望众人的目光集中在我和我的所作所为上，能给他们带来一些运气。”

column1: I hold a secret forbidden to ever pass my lips, but this telling of it shall be my third. I only hope that by the time someone finds this regretful tome, its knowledge will be unnecessary.
column2: “我守着一个永不许说出口的秘密，而这一次讲述将是第三回。我只希望，等有人找到这本满载悔恨的典籍时，其中的知识已经不必再用。”

column1: I remember how much pain you were in. A stone that large might've killed you!
column2: “我记得你那时有多疼。那么大一块石头，说不定会要了你的命！”

column1: I see a man's body, perfect in every way, but broken into many pieces, black and glittering. His head, broken away from his body tries to speak, but no air passes his lips.
column2: “我看见一个男人的身体，处处完美，却碎成许多片，漆黑而闪光。他的头颅脱离了躯体，试图开口，可没有气息通过他的嘴唇。”

column1: I was sewing a cloak for you. To keep your shoulders warm when I could not. It is unfinished, but...
column2: “我在给你缝一件斗篷。在我没法陪在你身边的时候，让你的肩膀暖和。还没缝完，不过……”

column1: I was. Please, take it!
column2: “是的。请收下！”

column1: Id krav oraidumten, Nazar.
column2: “Id krav oraidumten，Nazar。”

column1: If they fail, then I will have truly been the queen to destroy Lukatt, in a far fuller sense than anyone can imagine. Lord Leviathan, have mercy upon us.
column2: “倘若他们失败，我便真正成了毁灭卢卡特的女王，其意义远比任何人想象的更为彻底。主 Leviathan，怜悯我们。”

column1: In return, Leviathan would allow his chosen few, the Lukattites, to flourish, to build upon the island, and he would protect and nurture them as a part of the island itself.
column2: “作为回报，Leviathan 会允许他拣选的少数人，即卢卡特人，繁荣昌盛，在岛上兴建，并保护他们、滋养他们，把他们当作岛屿本身的一部分。”

column1: It couldn't... you mean all that time you were sick, you... you were holding a Bogani stone? For me...?
column2: “不可能……你是说你生病的那些日子里，你……你一直留着一块 Bogani 石？为了我……？”

column1: It is a stone of my own flesh, and it is my promise of faith \nto you. Accept it, and I will belong to you evermore, in flesh and blood, in love and war. I desire no other.
column2: “这是我自身血肉凝成的石头，也是我向你立下的忠贞之誓。\n接受它，我便永远属于你，在血肉之中，在爱与战争之中。我不要别人。”

column1: It's so peaceful here. Like nothing bad ever happened here at all.
column2: “这里好平静。仿佛从来没有坏事发生过。”

column1: It's so warm. I don't know what to say! I never imagined somebody would think me worthy of something like this. How can I possibly repay this?
column2: “好温暖。我不知道该说什么！我从没想过有人会觉得我配得上这样的东西。我该怎么偿还？”

column1: It's yes, you fool! That was our last kiss as idle lovers.
column2: “我答应，你这傻瓜！那是我们还只做恋人时的最后一吻。”

column1: Leviathan will be angered, and this island will be doomed.
column2: “Leviathan 会发怒，这座岛将注定毁灭。”

column1: Many Lukattites call for my blood, and my words are widely mocked as lies. If I am killed, the bargain will go unhonoured. If I reveal this secret to my people, they will think that I am spinning a fantastic yarn to save my own head.
column2: “许多卢卡特人喊着要我的血，我的话也被到处嘲笑成谎言。我若遇害，这约定便无人履行。我若向我的人民揭开这秘密，他们会以为我在编造奇谈，只为保住自己的脑袋。”

column1: Maxim is mounting an expedition at his hunting lodge in Pagewood, hoping to treat with Leviathan himself, and Fastad has retreated to his archive in Bracewind to search for other solutions. All of my hopes rest on them.
column2: “Maxim 正在他侍从林的狩猎行馆集结一支远征，希望亲自与 Leviathan 交涉；Fastad 则退入他在布雷斯温德的档案馆，寻找别的办法。我全部的希望都寄于他们。”

column1: Nazar, it's beautiful. Thank you.
column2: “Nazar，它真美。谢谢你。”

column1: Never. Not when the end of the day promised me back to you.
column2: “不会。一天的尽头总会把我送回你身边。”

column1: Since meeting you, I have thought of little else. Whatever happens here, whatever becomes of this island, I don't ever want to lose you.
column2: “自从遇见你，我几乎没想过别的。无论这里发生什么，无论这座岛变成什么样，我永远不想失去你。”

column1: The greatest of the terrors was Leviathan, his coils tangled around every reef and shoal. The island belonged to him, and he would not lightly release it.
column2: “诸恐怖之中最可怖的是 Leviathan，他的躯体盘绕缠住每一处礁石与浅滩。这座岛属于他，他不会轻易松手。”

column1: The hero, Chevre, went low into the bowels of the island, and there, he struck a bargain with the lord of the island's monsters. Rites, sacrifices, festivals in his honour, those were the promises made.
column2: “英雄 Chevre 向下走入岛屿的脏腑，在那里与岛上怪物之主订下约定。仪式、献祭、奉他之名的节庆，这些便是许下的诺言。”

column1: This bargain was kept secret, so as to prevent our enemies from interfering with it, and its terms were passed from Chevre, who became the island's first king, to each monarch in succession. Now, the burden of this bargain rests with me.
column2: “这约定被保密，以免敌人插手，其条款由后来成为岛上第一位国王的 Chevre 传给其后每一位君主。如今，这约定的重担落在我身上。”

column1: This kingdom is fallen, and my people torn. My life is in danger, so I have fled here, to the cloister I once lived as a young girl. Even here is not safe, however, and soon, nowhere will be safe.
column2: “这个王国已经倾覆，我的人民四分五裂。我的生命处于危险之中，于是我逃到这里，逃到我少女时代住过的隐修院。然而即便这里也不安全，很快，任何地方都不会安全。”

column1: This kiss shall be as your husband.
column2: “这一吻，便是以你丈夫的身份。”

column1: What is your answer then?
column2: “那么，你的答复是什么？”

column1: What's this?
column2: “这是什么？”

column1: Yeah. There are some things on this island that make all of the bad stuff seem really far away. Like another life.
column2: “是啊。这岛上有些东西，能让所有糟糕的事显得非常遥远。像是另一段人生。”

column1: You can repay it by laying with me every night and standing with me every day, until time or battle takes us.
column2: “你可以这样偿还：每夜与我同床，每日与我并肩，直到时间或战斗把我们带走。”

column1: You... you what?
column2: “你……你说什么？”

column1: And thanks.
column2: “还有，谢谢。”

column1: Bigs! Bigs coming! Protect King!
column2: “大个子！大个子来了！保护国王！”

column1: I've got to get out of this place. As for you, sack it, loot it, claim it, or burn it to the ground for all I care. If there's anything of use to you, it's all yours. I just want out.
column2: “我得离开这地方。至于你们，洗劫、搜刮、占下，或者烧成白地，我都不管。要是有什么对你们有用，都归你们。我只想出去。”

column1: It worked, I suppose, for they were certainly in awe of me, but then they dragged me back here and said I was their king. They didn't ever plan to let me leave, and there were far more than I could hope to overcome alone, so I had no choice but to play along.
column2: “我想这奏效了，他们确实对我十分敬畏，可接着就把我拖回这里，说我是他们的国王。他们根本没打算放我走，人数也远不是我一个人能对付的，我别无选择，只能顺着演下去。”

column1: My name is Shapiro, and I am... or was... a professor of sorcery. When I came under attack by these creatures, naturally I used my sorcery to defend myself.
column2: “我叫 Shapiro，我是……或者说曾经是……一名巫术教授。这些生物袭击我的时候，我自然用巫术自卫。”

column1: Oh thank the Gods. Did you get them all?
column2: “哦，感谢诸神。你们把他们都解决了？”

column1: Rest assured, I have no love for these diminuitive savages, and I was never their king.
column2: “请放心，我对这帮矮小的野蛮人毫无感情，我也从来不是他们的国王。”

column1: If there was anyone I'd want to see just one more time, Max, it would be you.
column2: “如果这世上还有谁是我想再看一眼的，Max，那就是你。”

column1: Max. I remember when these sculptures were made. You probably think I'm lying, but the sculptor really didn't exaggerate much.
column2: “Max。我记得这些雕塑是什么时候做的。你大概觉得我在撒谎，可雕刻的人真的没怎么夸张。”

column1: Anyway, can I have it? I'm the only one with any chance of withstanding the pure darkness of that cake, after all.
column2: “总之，能给我吗？毕竟，只有我还有机会承受那块蛋糕纯粹的黑暗。”

column1: But, of course!
column2: “那当然！”

column1: Dark arcane secrets, what else?
column2: “黑暗的奥术秘密，还能是什么？”

column1: I really thought the cake would be chocolate, though. Strange.
column2: “我本来真以为那蛋糕是巧克力的。奇怪。”

column1: I'm uniquely-suited and such.
column2: “我是独一无二的合适人选，之类的。”

column1: It isn't working! It's rebellious! Like the darkness has a will of its own!
column2: “不行！它在反抗！就像那黑暗有自己的意志！”

column1: Just get your rod, and let's go.
column2: “把法杖拿上，我们走。”

column1: Let's see what this rod can do!
column2: “看看这法杖能干什么！”

column1: Man was not meant to know chocolate as dark as this!
column2: “人类本不该知晓如此黑暗的巧克力！”

column1: My moment of weakness is past. Best that you carry the cake back to the stronghold though, lest I be tempted.
column2: “我软弱的那一刻已经过去了。不过蛋糕最好由你带回据点，免得我又受诱惑。”

column1: No matter. It is only a matter of time before its secrets bend to my will. Let's be off.
column2: “无妨。它的秘密向我的意志屈服，不过是时间问题。我们走。”

column1: Oh no! While we were screwing around with that cake, some trolls wandered up!
column2: “哦不！我们正拿那块蛋糕瞎折腾，几头巨魔晃过来了！”

column1: Oh, drat! I got so caught up in the excitement of battle, I completely forgot to pick up the rod!
column2: “哦，可恶！我让战斗的兴奋冲昏了头，彻底忘了把法杖捡起来！”

column1: Oh, no no no. You can't feel it? Look at this masterpiece!
column2: “哦，不，不，不。你感觉不到吗？看看这件杰作！”

column1: Oh, they'll be sorry they came this way today.
column2: “哦，他们今天挑这条路会后悔的。”

column1: Perhaps, in the end, that is the wiser choice. Who knows what could happen if I unraveled the moist, dark secrets of that eldritch wonder?
column2: “也许，到头来这才是更明智的选择。谁知道，倘若我揭开那件诡秘奇物那些湿润、黑暗的秘密，会发生什么？”

column1: Right. Well. Let's go then.
column2: “行。嗯。那我们走吧。”

column1: Rosewood Teahouse Menu
column2: “玫瑰木茶馆菜单”

column1: Seriously? Lots of people back at the stronghold would love to have some cake too. I get that you're desperate for it, but really, I thought you'd be more willing to share.
column2: “认真的？据点里好多人也会想吃点蛋糕。我知道你馋得要命，可我真以为你更愿意跟人分。”

column1: So you intend to deny me the power, then?
column2: “所以你是打算不把这力量给我了？”

column1: Such magnificent power!
column2: “如此宏伟的力量！”

column1: The loft! The crumb! The heady aroma! The fine, pure cocoa! It's positively bewitching!
column2: “那蓬松！那碎屑！那醉人的香气！那细腻纯粹的可可！简直令人着魔！”

column1: This is the weirdest thing I've seen since we got here. Even when compared to that thing with the face.
column2: “这是我们到这儿以来见过最怪的东西。就算跟那个长着脸的东西比，也是。”

column1: This rod contains all of the power of that cake. I'm sure we'll be able to find a way to turn its power toward the greater good.
column2: “这根法杖蕴含着那块蛋糕的全部力量。我相信我们能找到办法，把这力量用于更大的善。”

column1: This thing could make enough cake to feed everybody forever!
column2: “这东西做出来的蛋糕，够所有人一直吃到永远！”

column1: Unbelievable! To think that this was just sitting here all these years!
column2: “难以置信！想不到它就这么在这儿搁了这么多年！”

column1: Unbelieveable!
column2: “难以置信！”

column1: Wait, Greening, what are you doing?
column2: “等等，Greening，你要干什么？”

column1: Watch, I'll make a gigantic one right now!
column2: “看着，我现在就做一个巨大的！”

column1: What the hell was that?
column2: “刚才那他妈的是什么？”

column1: What's wrong?
column2: “怎么了？”

column1: What? It's just a cake.
column2: “什么？不就是块蛋糕。”

column1: Yikes, Green, if it's really that important to you, then take it.
column2: “我的天，Green，既然这对你真那么要紧，那就拿去吧。”

column1: You'd better not forget it after all the fuss you made to get it. Go pick it up!
column2: “你闹出那么大动静才弄到它，可别回头就忘了。去拿！”

column1: Breathtaking harmony heard the isle over! Come and treat your ears to the Royal Seamen's Chorus, playing all week!
column2: “全岛都听得见的惊人和声！来让你们的耳朵享享福吧，皇家水手合唱团，演满一整周！”

column1: I had to fire one of the guards today. He tried to get Odluk to escape, but the old orc told on him and refused to go. I did everything by the book on this one, but... I don't know. If I was Odluk, I'd have gone. He spends more time in the cell than he does at home with that awful wife he loves so much.
column2: “我今天不得不开除一名卫兵。他想帮 Odluk 逃走，可那老兽人告发了他，不肯走。这件事我完全照章办了，可是……我不知道。我要是 Odluk，我早走了。他待在牢房里的时间，比待在家里陪那个他那么爱的可恶老婆还长。”

column1: I have given my response already. Though I was born in Crest, Lukatt is now my home, and I will not abandon it, nor sell it to you to use as a wedge against the orc nation. If you do not remove your provocateurs, my next missive to you shall be writ in steel.
column2: “我已经给过答复。我虽生于克雷斯特，卢卡特如今已是我的家。我不会抛弃它，也不会把它卖给你，供你用作对付兽人国度的楔子。你若不撤走挑衅者，我下一封信将用钢铁写成。”

column1: I'd get audiences used to the idea of a clothed singing werewolf before you try to get them on board with a naked one.
column2: “我会先让观众习惯一只穿着衣服唱歌的狼人，再试着说服他们接受一只光着的。”

column1: I've arranged your passage already. Please, sail for Tsarath and do not return. I know you want to try to calm things down in court, but this country is heading for disaster and you can not stop it. I beg you, flee while you can.
column2: “我已经替你安排好了船。求你，驶向察拉思，不要回来。我知道你想在宫廷里把事情平息，可这个国家正在走向灾难，你阻止不了。我求你，能走就走。”
